questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of pulse oximetry?
questions.explanation: Hypertension does not interfere with the optical signal. Inaccuracy arises from poor pulsatile flow (vasoconstriction, shock, hypothermia), dyshemoglobinemias (carboxyhemoglobin reads falsely normal), anemia, and optical interference.

questions.text: All of the following statements regarding pulse oximetry are true, EXCEPT:
options: It provides a continuous noninvasive measurement of pulse rate
It provides a continuous noninvasive measurement of the partial pressure of oxygen
It depends on differential light absorption by oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin
Significant dyshemoglobinemia can affect its accuracy
Excessive ambient light can interfere with its accuracy
originalOptions: It provides a continuous noninvasive measurement of pulse rate
It provides a continuous noninvasive measurement of the partial pressure of oxygen
It depends on differential light absorption by oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin
Significant dyshemoglobinemia can affect its accuracy
Excessive ambient light can interfere with its accuracy
questions.correctAnswer: B) It provides a continuous noninvasive measurement of the partial pressure of oxygen
questions.correctAnswerText: It provides a continuous noninvasive measurement of the partial pressure of oxygen
questions.explanation: Pulse oximetry estimates hemoglobin saturation (SpO₂), not PaO₂. The partial pressure of oxygen requires arterial blood gas analysis.

questions.text: You are alone with a patient in suspected cardiac or respiratory arrest. After ensuring scene safety and before sending for help, what is the next step?
questions.explanation: Responsiveness must be established first. Only then is EMS activated, followed by assessment of breathing and pulse.

questions.text: A 21-year-old intoxicated college student turns blue and collapses while eating a hot dog. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Sudden cyanosis while eating indicates foreign-body airway obstruction, and intoxication increases the risk of aspiration. Cardiac arrest would be a consequence of prolonged obstruction, not the primary cause.

questions.text: A 39-year-old man has a GCS of 6, no facial trauma, a deviated nasal septum, and a full beard. What is the most appropriate airway management?
options: Orotracheal intubation by two operators with in-line cervical spine stabilization
Forced nasotracheal intubation past the deviated septum
Bag-valve-mask ventilation until the beard can be shaved
Bag-valve-mask ventilation until the cervical spine is excluded
originalOptions: Orotracheal intubation by two operators with in-line cervical spine stabilization
Forced nasotracheal intubation past the deviated septum
Bag-valve-mask ventilation until the beard can be shaved
Bag-valve-mask ventilation until the cervical spine is excluded
questions.correctAnswer: A) Orotracheal intubation by two operators with in-line cervical spine stabilization
questions.correctAnswerText: Orotracheal intubation by two operators with in-line cervical spine stabilization
questions.explanation: A GCS of 6 requires a definitive airway, and a deviated septum argues against the nasal route. A beard is not a contraindication to orotracheal intubation, and surgical cricothyrotomy is reserved for failed airway access.

questions.text: A 65-year-old man on a short ladder suddenly collapses and is unresponsive. What is the next step?
options: Call EMS and obtain an AED
Place him in the recovery position
originalOptions: Call EMS and obtain an AED
Place him in the recovery position
questions.correctAnswer: D) Call EMS and obtain an AED
questions.correctAnswerText: Call EMS and obtain an AED
questions.explanation: After unresponsiveness is established, EMS is activated and an AED obtained, then breathing and pulse are assessed. CPR cannot be started before arrest is confirmed.

questions.text: After finding an unresponsive child, shouting for help, and confirming that the child is not breathing but has a pulse, what is the next step?
options: Leave the child to search for an AED
Open the airway by head tilt–chin lift and give rescue breaths
Begin back blows and chest thrusts
originalOptions: Leave the child to search for an AED
Open the airway by head tilt–chin lift and give rescue breaths
Begin back blows and chest thrusts
questions.correctAnswer: B) Open the airway by head tilt–chin lift and give rescue breaths
questions.correctAnswerText: Open the airway by head tilt–chin lift and give rescue breaths
questions.explanation: A palpable pulse with absent breathing is respiratory arrest, which is managed with airway opening and rescue breathing. Compressions are indicated only when the pulse is absent.

questions.text: After finding an unresponsive child with no normal breathing and no definite pulse, and with help already activated, what should the rescuer do next?
options: Leave to search for an AED
Begin back blows and chest thrusts
originalOptions: Leave to search for an AED
Begin back blows and chest thrusts
questions.explanation: The absence of a pulse defines cardiac arrest, so CPR starts immediately. A lone rescuer uses 30:2, and the AED is applied as soon as it is available.

questions.text: After finding someone unresponsive with a pulse but not breathing, you are unable to deliver effective breaths. What is the next step?
options: Repeat head tilt–chin lift and reattempt the breath
Leave the patient to search for an AED
originalOptions: Repeat head tilt–chin lift and reattempt the breath
Leave the patient to search for an AED
questions.correctAnswer: C) Repeat head tilt–chin lift and reattempt the breath
questions.correctAnswerText: Repeat head tilt–chin lift and reattempt the breath
questions.explanation: Ineffective breaths usually result from inadequate airway positioning, so the airway is repositioned first. Compressions are not indicated while a pulse is present.

questions.text: A witnessed adult collapse is followed by loss of consciousness and absent normal breathing. What is the correct resuscitation sequence?
options: Recognize arrest, activate EMS and obtain an AED, begin high-quality CPR (30:2), and defibrillate promptly if the rhythm is shockable
Establish IV access, give epinephrine, begin CPR, then apply the AED
Intubate, begin CPR, call EMS, then apply the AED
Check the pulse for 30 seconds, give rescue breaths first, call EMS, then begin compressions
Perform CPR for 5 minutes, activate EMS, then apply the AED
originalOptions: Recognize arrest, activate EMS and obtain an AED, begin high-quality CPR (30:2), and defibrillate promptly if the rhythm is shockable
Establish IV access, give epinephrine, begin CPR, then apply the AED
Intubate, begin CPR, call EMS, then apply the AED
Check the pulse for 30 seconds, give rescue breaths first, call EMS, then begin compressions
Perform CPR for 5 minutes, activate EMS, then apply the AED
questions.correctAnswer: A) Recognize arrest, activate EMS and obtain an AED, begin high-quality CPR (30:2), and defibrillate promptly if the rhythm is shockable
questions.correctAnswerText: Recognize arrest, activate EMS and obtain an AED, begin high-quality CPR (30:2), and defibrillate promptly if the rhythm is shockable
questions.explanation: Early activation, immediate high-quality CPR, and early defibrillation form the core sequence. Advanced airway or drug therapy must never delay CPR or the first indicated shock.

questions.text: Which of the following findings in a child indicates a currently patent airway, so that immediate invasive airway intervention is not required?
options: Inability to speak or make sounds
originalOptions: Inability to speak or make sounds
questions.explanation: Vocalization requires airflow through the airway, whereas the other findings indicate obstruction or respiratory failure. Ongoing reassessment is still required, since stridor, fatigue, or deterioration can develop.

questions.text: All of the following are true regarding confirmation of endotracheal tube position, EXCEPT:
options: Auscultation of the chest and epigastrium
Visualizing the tube passing through the esophagus
Direct visualization of the tube passing between the vocal cords
originalOptions: Auscultation of the chest and epigastrium
Visualizing the tube passing through the esophagus
Direct visualization of the tube passing between the vocal cords
questions.correctAnswer: B) Visualizing the tube passing through the esophagus
questions.correctAnswerText: Visualizing the tube passing through the esophagus
questions.explanation: A tube passing into the esophagus is a misplacement, not a confirmation. Correct placement is through the vocal cords into the trachea, confirmed by waveform capnography and clinical checks.

questions.text: All of the following are true regarding retropharyngeal abscess, EXCEPT:
options: It presents with fever, neck pain, drooling, and torticollis
The prevertebral soft-tissue space is widened on a lateral neck X-ray
It may obstruct the airway or extend into the mediastinum
It is most common between ages 5 and 7 years
originalOptions: It presents with fever, neck pain, drooling, and torticollis
The prevertebral soft-tissue space is widened on a lateral neck X-ray
It may obstruct the airway or extend into the mediastinum
It is most common between ages 5 and 7 years
questions.correctAnswer: E) It is most common between ages 5 and 7 years
questions.correctAnswerText: It is most common between ages 5 and 7 years
questions.explanation: Retropharyngeal abscess is more common in young children, and the stated age range is not the typical peak. The other statements are true, and the condition is potentially life-threatening.

questions.text: Apnea is defined as a respiratory pause lasting at least:
questions.explanation: Apnea is a pause of at least 20 seconds, or a shorter pause accompanied by bradycardia, desaturation, cyanosis, or pallor. The same definition applies to apnea of prematurity in a preterm infant.

questions.text: An unresponsive adult has no pulse, and the rescuer is unable or unwilling to give breaths. What should the rescuer do?
options: Start hands-only chest compressions immediately and use an AED as soon as available
Wait for EMS to arrive before any intervention
Recheck the pulse repeatedly until help arrives
Place the patient in the recovery position
originalOptions: Start hands-only chest compressions immediately and use an AED as soon as available
Wait for EMS to arrive before any intervention
Recheck the pulse repeatedly until help arrives
Place the patient in the recovery position
questions.correctAnswer: A) Start hands-only chest compressions immediately and use an AED as soon as available
questions.correctAnswerText: Start hands-only chest compressions immediately and use an AED as soon as available
questions.explanation: Compressions and early defibrillation are the priority in pulseless arrest, and hands-only CPR is acceptable when breaths cannot be given. Trained rescuers should add ventilation when feasible.

questions.text: What is the best artery for assessing the pulse in an infant?
questions.explanation: The brachial artery is the preferred pulse-check site in infants (under 1 year), because the short, fat neck makes the carotid pulse difficult to palpate.

questions.text: What is the correct initial BLS sequence after finding a collapsed adult?
options: Start chest compressions, call EMS, check the pulse, assess responsiveness
Assess responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, check breathing and pulse (≤10 seconds), start chest compressions
Assess responsiveness, open the airway, give two breaths, call EMS, start compressions
Call EMS, check the pulse for 30 seconds, give rescue breaths, start compressions
Assess responsiveness, check breathing and pulse, start compressions, then call EMS
originalOptions: Start chest compressions, call EMS, check the pulse, assess responsiveness
Assess responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, check breathing and pulse (≤10 seconds), start chest compressions
Assess responsiveness, open the airway, give two breaths, call EMS, start compressions
Call EMS, check the pulse for 30 seconds, give rescue breaths, start compressions
Assess responsiveness, check breathing and pulse, start compressions, then call EMS
questions.correctAnswer: B) Assess responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, check breathing and pulse (≤10 seconds), start chest compressions
questions.correctAnswerText: Assess responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, check breathing and pulse (≤10 seconds), start chest compressions
questions.explanation: Responsiveness is assessed first, EMS and an AED are requested early, and breathing and pulse are checked together within 10 seconds before compressions begin.

questions.text: Which is the most common cause of bronchiolitis in children under 2 years of age, including many children older than 1 year?
questions.explanation: RSV is the most common cause of bronchiolitis in this age group, although it is not the only pathogen. Parainfluenza virus is the typical cause of croup.

questions.text: How often should compressors switch during two-rescuer CPR?
questions.explanation: Rescuers switch about every 2 minutes (approximately 5 cycles of 30:2) to prevent fatigue and preserve compression quality, with the pause kept minimal.

questions.text: Which is the earliest sign of respiratory distress or airway compromise?
questions.explanation: An increased respiratory rate is the earliest change. Flaring and retractions reflect increased work of breathing, whereas cyanosis and hypotension are late signs.

questions.text: A farmer presents with cyanosis, frothy oral secretions, difficulty breathing, and pinpoint pupils. What is the first step?
options: Remove contaminated clothing and wash the skin
originalOptions: Remove contaminated clothing and wash the skin
questions.explanation: This is an organophosphate toxidrome with copious bronchial secretions. Airway and breathing take priority over antidotes (atropine, pralidoxime) in the ABC approach.

questions.text: Which is the most commonly used first-choice intraosseous (IO) access site in pediatric patients?
questions.explanation: The proximal tibia is the classic first-choice site in children. The distal tibia and proximal humerus are alternatives depending on age, equipment, and training.

questions.text: Which maneuver should be used to open the airway when cervical spine injury is suspected?
options: Rolling the patient into the lateral position
Jaw thrust with manual in-line stabilization
originalOptions: Rolling the patient into the lateral position
Jaw thrust with manual in-line stabilization
questions.correctAnswer: E) Jaw thrust with manual in-line stabilization
questions.correctAnswerText: Jaw thrust with manual in-line stabilization
questions.explanation: Jaw thrust opens the airway without extending the neck. Head tilt–chin lift is used only if the airway cannot otherwise be opened.

questions.text: In an unresponsive patient, the pulse should be checked for no more than ____ seconds.
questions.explanation: The pulse check is limited to 10 seconds so that compressions are not delayed. If there is any doubt about the pulse, CPR is started.

questions.text: Which of the following is a late sign of airway compromise?
questions.explanation: Desaturation appears late, so the airway must be addressed before it develops. Agitation, tachypnea, voice change, and stridor or gurgling are early signs.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered a definitive airway?
questions.correctAnswer: D) Cuffed tube in the trachea
questions.explanation: A definitive airway is a cuffed tube in the trachea, which protects against aspiration and allows full ventilatory control. Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal airways and masks are adjuncts.

questions.text: Which of the following is the appropriate management of peritonsillar abscess?
options: Penicillin plus clindamycin plus vancomycin for every patient
Drainage plus antibiotics covering group A streptococci and oral anaerobes (e.g., ampicillin–sulbactam)
originalOptions: Penicillin plus clindamycin plus vancomycin for every patient
Drainage plus antibiotics covering group A streptococci and oral anaerobes (e.g., ampicillin–sulbactam)
questions.correctAnswer: B) Drainage plus antibiotics covering group A streptococci and oral anaerobes (e.g., ampicillin–sulbactam)
questions.correctAnswerText: Drainage plus antibiotics covering group A streptococci and oral anaerobes (e.g., ampicillin–sulbactam)
questions.explanation: Treatment combines drainage with antibiotics directed at group A streptococci and oral anaerobes. Penicillin plus clindamycin and/or vancomycin is not a blanket regimen for every patient.

questions.text: Which route is the preferred first-line route for administering drugs during cardiac arrest?
questions.explanation: The peripheral IV route is first-line, with IO as the alternative when IV access fails. The endotracheal route is a last resort because absorption is poor and unpredictable.

questions.text: What is the first maneuver to improve oxygenation after chest injury?
options: Ascertain the need for a chest tube
Obtain a lateral cervical spine X-ray
originalOptions: Ascertain the need for a chest tube
Obtain a lateral cervical spine X-ray
questions.explanation: The simplest effective intervention comes first, and supplemental oxygen is given to all critically ill patients. Definitive airway management follows only if indicated.

questions.text: Which is an appropriate first-aid measure for snake bite?
options: Keep the patient calm, remove rings and constricting items, immobilize the limb at about heart level, and arrange urgent transport for antivenom
A tight arterial tourniquet above the bite
originalOptions: Keep the patient calm, remove rings and constricting items, immobilize the limb at about heart level, and arrange urgent transport for antivenom
A tight arterial tourniquet above the bite
questions.correctAnswer: A) Keep the patient calm, remove rings and constricting items, immobilize the limb at about heart level, and arrange urgent transport for antivenom
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the patient calm, remove rings and constricting items, immobilize the limb at about heart level, and arrange urgent transport for antivenom
questions.explanation: Incision, suction, ice, and tight tourniquets worsen local tissue damage and delay proper care without reliably reducing venom spread.

questions.text: What approximate inspired oxygen concentration is delivered by a standard low-flow nasal cannula at 1–6 L/min?
questions.explanation: A nasal cannula at 1–6 L/min delivers approximately 24–44% oxygen, varying with flow rate and the patient's inspiratory pattern.

questions.text: A choking patient becomes unresponsive. What is the best method to clear the obstruction?
questions.correctAnswer: B) Start CPR with chest compressions
questions.explanation: In an unresponsive choking victim, compressions double as expulsion attempts. The mouth is inspected before each set of breaths, and an object is removed only if visible, never by blind finger sweep.

questions.text: What is the preferred initial peripheral vascular access for major trauma resuscitation?
questions.correctAnswer: E) Two large-bore peripheral IV lines
questions.explanation: Two 14–16G cannulae allow rapid fluid and blood-product administration. IO access is used if IV access fails or is delayed.

questions.text: What is the best method to confirm and continuously monitor endotracheal tube placement?
questions.explanation: Waveform capnography is the most reliable objective confirmation and allows continuous monitoring. Auscultation alone is insufficient.

questions.text: What is the earliest sign of ARDS?
questions.explanation: An increased respiratory rate precedes hypoxemia, crackles, and radiographic changes.

questions.text: A child is found pulseless and not breathing (unwitnessed), and the rescuer is alone. What is the initial management?
options: Start CPR immediately for 2 minutes, then call EMS
originalOptions: Start CPR immediately for 2 minutes, then call EMS
questions.correctAnswer: D) Start CPR immediately for 2 minutes, then call EMS
questions.correctAnswerText: Start CPR immediately for 2 minutes, then call EMS
questions.explanation: In a child, paediatric arrest is usually respiratory in origin, so CPR is started first and EMS is called after 2 minutes if the rescuer is alone. This differs from a witnessed adult collapse, where EMS is called first.

questions.text: What is the first-line treatment for symptomatic bradycardia with a pulse in an adult?
questions.explanation: Atropine is first-line, repeated every 3–5 minutes to a maximum of 3 mg. Pacing or dopamine/epinephrine infusion follows if atropine is ineffective.

questions.text: When can a laryngeal mask airway be used after an attempted endotracheal intubation?
options: To replace the tube after successful intubation
Only when the patient is fully conscious
As a definitive airway that fully protects against aspiration
As a rescue airway when intubation fails and ventilation is required
originalOptions: To replace the tube after successful intubation
Only when the patient is fully conscious
As a definitive airway that fully protects against aspiration
As a rescue airway when intubation fails and ventilation is required
questions.correctAnswer: E) As a rescue airway when intubation fails and ventilation is required
questions.correctAnswerText: As a rescue airway when intubation fails and ventilation is required
questions.explanation: A supraglottic airway is quicker to place and serves as a rescue device in failed or delayed intubation. It does not fully protect against aspiration and is not a definitive airway.

questions.text: When giving rescue breaths to an apneic patient who has a pulse, how often should the pulse be rechecked?
questions.explanation: The pulse is rechecked about every 2 minutes. CPR is started if the pulse is lost.

questions.text: Which of the following is the LEAST likely, by itself, to justify unusually prolonged resuscitation?
questions.explanation: Prolonged resuscitation is justified when a potentially reversible cause exists, such as hypothermia, toxins, electrical injury, or pregnancy near term. Arrest from catastrophic SAH carries a poor prognosis and does not justify extension.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an indication for admission in an asthma exacerbation?
options: Persistent symptoms despite initial bronchodilator therapy
Frequent MDI use over the previous months
originalOptions: Persistent symptoms despite initial bronchodilator therapy
Frequent MDI use over the previous months
questions.correctAnswer: D) Frequent MDI use over the previous months
questions.correctAnswerText: Frequent MDI use over the previous months
questions.explanation: Admission is determined by the severity and response of the current episode. Chronic frequent inhaler use does not by itself mandate admission.

questions.text: Which statement about high-quality adult CPR is WRONG?
options: Compress at least 5 cm (2 in) while avoiding excessive depth
Use 30:2 before an advanced airway is placed
originalOptions: Compress at least 5 cm (2 in) while avoiding excessive depth
Use 30:2 before an advanced airway is placed
questions.correctAnswer: B) Allow only partial chest recoil
questions.explanation: Full chest recoil must be allowed after every compression to permit cardiac refilling. Incomplete recoil reduces coronary and cerebral perfusion.

questions.text: While performing CPR on an infant, a second rescuer arrives and EMS has already been activated. What is the next step?
options: Ask the second rescuer to repeat the call to EMS
Have the second rescuer give ventilations only at a 30:2 ratio
Have the second rescuer join for two-rescuer CPR (15:2) and switch compressor roles about every 2 minutes
originalOptions: Ask the second rescuer to repeat the call to EMS
Have the second rescuer give ventilations only at a 30:2 ratio
Have the second rescuer join for two-rescuer CPR (15:2) and switch compressor roles about every 2 minutes
questions.correctAnswer: E) Have the second rescuer join for two-rescuer CPR (15:2) and switch compressor roles about every 2 minutes
questions.correctAnswerText: Have the second rescuer join for two-rescuer CPR (15:2) and switch compressor roles about every 2 minutes
questions.explanation: Two-rescuer pediatric CPR uses 15:2, and switching roles about every 2 minutes minimizes fatigue and preserves compression quality. EMS activation has already been completed.

questions.text: A rescuer is uncomfortable giving mouth-to-mouth breaths to an unresponsive person with no pulse. What should be done?
options: Attempt head tilt and jaw thrust, then give a breath
Wait for EMS before any intervention
Place the patient in the recovery position
originalOptions: Attempt head tilt and jaw thrust, then give a breath
Wait for EMS before any intervention
Place the patient in the recovery position
questions.explanation: Hands-only compressions are the priority in pulseless arrest and are acceptable when the rescuer is unable or unwilling to give breaths.

questions.text: Which of the following lists the correct steps of basic life support (BLS)?
options: Assess the victim, activate EMS and bring an AED, perform chest compressions, give rescue breaths
Assess the victim, perform chest compressions, give rescue breaths, defibrillate before calling EMS
Call EMS, intubate, perform chest compressions
Give rescue breaths, assess the victim, perform chest compressions
originalOptions: Assess the victim, activate EMS and bring an AED, perform chest compressions, give rescue breaths
Assess the victim, perform chest compressions, give rescue breaths, defibrillate before calling EMS
Call EMS, intubate, perform chest compressions
Give rescue breaths, assess the victim, perform chest compressions
questions.correctAnswer: A) Assess the victim, activate EMS and bring an AED, perform chest compressions, give rescue breaths
questions.correctAnswerText: Assess the victim, activate EMS and bring an AED, perform chest compressions, give rescue breaths
questions.explanation: BLS begins with assessment and activation of the emergency response with AED retrieval, followed by compressions and breaths. Early defibrillation follows when an AED is available.

questions.text: A choking patient is unresponsive but still has a pulse, and EMS has been activated. What is the next step?
options: Place the patient in the recovery position
originalOptions: Place the patient in the recovery position
questions.explanation: A pulse is present, so compressions and an AED are not indicated. The airway obstruction must be addressed first by opening the airway.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding basic life support?
options: Scene safety must be ensured first
For a child, the compression-to-breath ratio is 15:2 when only one rescuer is present
For a child, two-rescuer CPR uses 15:2
The brachial artery is used for the pulse check in infants
Compression depth is about one-third of the chest depth in children
originalOptions: Scene safety must be ensured first
For a child, the compression-to-breath ratio is 15:2 when only one rescuer is present
For a child, two-rescuer CPR uses 15:2
The brachial artery is used for the pulse check in infants
Compression depth is about one-third of the chest depth in children
questions.correctAnswer: B) For a child, the compression-to-breath ratio is 15:2 when only one rescuer is present
questions.correctAnswerText: For a child, the compression-to-breath ratio is 15:2 when only one rescuer is present
questions.explanation: Single-rescuer pediatric CPR uses 30:2, while 15:2 applies only when two rescuers are present.

questions.text: After a failed attempt at peripheral IV access, what is the next step?
options: Central venous catheter via the femoral vein
Central venous catheter via the internal jugular vein
Central venous catheter via the subclavian vein
originalOptions: Central venous catheter via the femoral vein
Central venous catheter via the internal jugular vein
Central venous catheter via the subclavian vein
questions.explanation: IO access is the rapid, reliable alternative when peripheral IV access fails or is delayed, and it works even in shock. Central lines are slower and carry more complications.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a contraindication to intraosseous line insertion (before placement)?
options: Previous IO attempt in the same bone
originalOptions: Previous IO attempt in the same bone
questions.correctAnswer: C) Fluid leakage from the line
questions.explanation: Leakage is a post-insertion sign of extravasation or malposition, after which the line should be abandoned. Fracture, local infection, and a prior attempt in the same bone are pre-insertion contraindications.

questions.text: What is the target oxygen saturation range in a COPD patient with hypercapnia?
questions.explanation: Controlled oxygen therapy targets 88–92% in patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure, to avoid worsening CO₂ retention. The 94–98% target applies to patients without this risk.

questions.text: A conscious child older than 1 year shows the universal sign of choking. Which maneuver is used for severe foreign-body airway obstruction?
options: Alternating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts
originalOptions: Alternating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts
questions.correctAnswer: D) Alternating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts
questions.correctAnswerText: Alternating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts
questions.explanation: Cycles of 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts are continued until the object clears or the child becomes unresponsive. At that point CPR is started.

questions.text: All of the following are indications for admission of a pediatric patient with croup, EXCEPT:
options: Persistent moderate–severe symptoms despite corticosteroid and nebulized epinephrine
originalOptions: Persistent moderate–severe symptoms despite corticosteroid and nebulized epinephrine
questions.explanation: Admission depends on severity, response to treatment, and risk of deterioration, not on an age of 24 months. Admission or PICU escalation is required for persistent symptoms despite treatment, repeated epinephrine need, failure to maintain oxygenation or hydration, or impending respiratory failure.

questions.text: Which is NOT a component of the Pediatric Assessment Triangle?
questions.explanation: The triangle comprises Appearance, Work of breathing, and Circulation to skin. Airway is assessed separately in the hands-on primary survey.

questions.text: All of the following cause acute stridor in children, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Bronchiolitis is a lower-airway disease presenting with wheeze and crackles, not stridor. The other conditions are upper-airway causes of acute stridor.

questions.text: Which statement regarding epiglottitis is correct?
options: Hib vaccination has markedly reduced Hib epiglottitis, but other organisms such as streptococci and staphylococci can also cause it
It is always caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b
The diagnosis should be confirmed by throat examination with a tongue depressor
The child should be laid flat to obtain a lateral neck X-ray
The thumbprint sign is seen on an AP neck X-ray
originalOptions: Hib vaccination has markedly reduced Hib epiglottitis, but other organisms such as streptococci and staphylococci can also cause it
It is always caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b
The diagnosis should be confirmed by throat examination with a tongue depressor
The child should be laid flat to obtain a lateral neck X-ray
The thumbprint sign is seen on an AP neck X-ray
questions.correctAnswer: A) Hib vaccination has markedly reduced Hib epiglottitis, but other organisms such as streptococci and staphylococci can also cause it
questions.correctAnswerText: Hib vaccination has markedly reduced Hib epiglottitis, but other organisms such as streptococci and staphylococci can also cause it
questions.explanation: Epiglottitis is not always Hib-related. Throat examination or laying the child flat can precipitate complete obstruction, and the thumbprint sign is seen on the lateral neck film.

questions.text: Which finding indicates total or near-total airway obstruction due to a foreign body in a child?
options: Weak or absent cough with inability to speak or make sounds
Intermittent wheezing with good air movement
originalOptions: Weak or absent cough with inability to speak or make sounds
Intermittent wheezing with good air movement
questions.correctAnswer: A) Weak or absent cough with inability to speak or make sounds
questions.correctAnswerText: Weak or absent cough with inability to speak or make sounds
questions.explanation: Total obstruction is also associated with cyanosis, altered mental status, apnea, and poor or absent air movement. An effective cough indicates mild obstruction.

questions.text: Which combination constitutes the "croup triangle"?
options: Toxic appearance, thick purulent secretions, high fever
originalOptions: Toxic appearance, thick purulent secretions, high fever
questions.correctAnswer: B) Barking cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness
questions.explanation: These three features characterize croup (laryngotracheobronchitis). The other options describe epiglottitis, peritonsillar abscess, bronchiolitis, and bacterial tracheitis respectively.

questions.text: What compression-to-ventilation ratio is used for pediatric CPR with one rescuer?
questions.explanation: A single rescuer uses 30:2 in children, while two rescuers use 15:2 before an advanced airway is placed.

questions.text: The steeple sign on an AP neck radiograph is classically associated with which condition?
questions.explanation: The steeple sign represents subglottic narrowing in croup. Croup remains primarily a clinical diagnosis, and imaging is not routinely required.

questions.text: In the mnemonic FATHER for the differential diagnosis of acute stridor in children, what does "R" represent?
questions.explanation: FATHER stands for Foreign body, Airway burn/anaphylaxis, Tracheitis/trauma, Hypersensitivity, Epiglottitis, and Retropharyngeal abscess. Croup, the most common cause, is usually listed separately.

questions.text: What is the dose of nebulized epinephrine for moderate-to-severe croup?
options: 2.5 mL of 1 mg/mL regardless of age
5 mL of 1 mg/mL (1:1000) L-epinephrine, regardless of age or weight
originalOptions: 2.5 mL of 1 mg/mL regardless of age
5 mL of 1 mg/mL (1:1000) L-epinephrine, regardless of age or weight
questions.correctAnswer: D) 5 mL of 1 mg/mL (1:1000) L-epinephrine, regardless of age or weight
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mL of 1 mg/mL (1:1000) L-epinephrine, regardless of age or weight
questions.explanation: The nebulized dose is 5 mL of 1 mg/mL L-epinephrine (or 0.5 mL of 2.25% racemic epinephrine), followed by observation for rebound symptoms. The IV and IM routes are used for arrest and anaphylaxis, respectively.

questions.text: How is acute laryngospasm managed?
options: IM epinephrine as first-line for all cases
Remove the trigger, call for help, perform a jaw thrust, and give 100% oxygen with continuous positive-pressure ventilation
originalOptions: IM epinephrine as first-line for all cases
Remove the trigger, call for help, perform a jaw thrust, and give 100% oxygen with continuous positive-pressure ventilation
questions.correctAnswer: B) Remove the trigger, call for help, perform a jaw thrust, and give 100% oxygen with continuous positive-pressure ventilation
questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the trigger, call for help, perform a jaw thrust, and give 100% oxygen with continuous positive-pressure ventilation
questions.explanation: Refractory complete laryngospasm may require deepening anesthesia and a neuromuscular blocker such as succinylcholine. IM epinephrine is first-line only when the presentation is anaphylaxis.

questions.text: After help is called for an unresponsive, pulseless adult, what should be done while waiting?
questions.explanation: Immediate high-quality CPR maintains coronary and cerebral perfusion until defibrillation or advanced care is available.

questions.text: Which device analyzes the cardiac rhythm during basic life support and advises whether a shock is needed?
questions.explanation: The AED analyzes the rhythm and advises a shock when indicated. The chest is exposed and dried, pads are attached, the patient is cleared during analysis and shock, and CPR is resumed immediately afterward.

questions.text: Which lateral neck radiographic sign is classically associated with epiglottitis?
questions.explanation: The thumbprint sign reflects a swollen epiglottis. In a toxic child with suspected epiglottitis, imaging must never delay expert airway management.

questions.text: All of the following are considered minimal precautions for preventing the spread of communicable disease during resuscitation, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Minimal barrier precautions consist of a water-impervious gown and leggings, a face mask, and eye protection. Needle-impermeable sterile gloves are not part of the minimal set.

questions.text: Which of the following is the primary treatment goal in a patient with sinus tachycardia?
options: Identify and treat the underlying cause
originalOptions: Identify and treat the underlying cause
questions.correctAnswer: C) Identify and treat the underlying cause
questions.correctAnswerText: Identify and treat the underlying cause
questions.explanation: Sinus tachycardia is a compensatory physiological response (fever, pain, hypovolaemia, anxiety), and the rate settles once the cause is treated. Adenosine and cardioversion are used for reentrant or unstable tachyarrhythmias, and suppressing a compensatory tachycardia can be harmful.

questions.text: After delivering a defibrillation shock to a patient in VF/pulseless VT, what is the IMMEDIATE next step?
options: Resume CPR immediately, starting with chest compressions, for 2 minutes
Check the rhythm on the monitor
originalOptions: Resume CPR immediately, starting with chest compressions, for 2 minutes
Check the rhythm on the monitor
questions.correctAnswer: A) Resume CPR immediately, starting with chest compressions, for 2 minutes
questions.correctAnswerText: Resume CPR immediately, starting with chest compressions, for 2 minutes
questions.explanation: Compressions are resumed without delay after the shock, and the rhythm is reassessed only at the end of the 2-minute cycle. A pulse is checked only if an organized rhythm or signs of ROSC appear.

questions.text: In adult cardiac arrest, what is the dose and timing of epinephrine?
options: 1 mg IV/IO once only, immediately after the first shock
1 mg IV/IO every 10 minutes throughout the arrest
2 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes from the start of the arrest
1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes, given as soon as possible in PEA/asystole and after the second shock in VF/pVT
originalOptions: 1 mg IV/IO once only, immediately after the first shock
1 mg IV/IO every 10 minutes throughout the arrest
2 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes from the start of the arrest
1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes, given as soon as possible in PEA/asystole and after the second shock in VF/pVT
questions.correctAnswer: D) 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes, given as soon as possible in PEA/asystole and after the second shock in VF/pVT
questions.correctAnswerText: 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes, given as soon as possible in PEA/asystole and after the second shock in VF/pVT
questions.explanation: Epinephrine is repeated at a fixed time interval (3–5 minutes), not after a fixed number of cycles or doses. The 0.5 mg IM dose belongs to anaphylaxis.

questions.text: Which drug is the treatment of choice for torsades de pointes?
questions.explanation: Torsades de pointes is treated with IV magnesium sulfate regardless of the serum magnesium level. Amiodarone and procainamide prolong the QT interval and can worsen it, and sodium bicarbonate is reserved for hyperkalaemia, TCA overdose and severe acidosis.

questions.text: In a patient with STEMI in whom timely PCI is not available, which of the following is used for coronary reperfusion?
questions.explanation: Fibrinolytics lyse the occluding thrombus in eligible STEMI when PCI cannot be delivered in time. Aspirin and heparin are antithrombotic adjuncts that do not restore flow, and epinephrine and atropine have no reperfusion role.

questions.text: In the adult VF/pulseless VT algorithm, which statement correctly describes drug administration?
options: Epinephrine every other CPR cycle, and amiodarone after the 3rd and 5th cycles
Epinephrine after every shock, and amiodarone after the first shock
Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes (given after the second shock), and amiodarone or lidocaine for refractory VF/pVT after the third shock
Amiodarone after the first shock, and epinephrine only after the fifth shock
Atropine every 3–5 minutes, and amiodarone after the second shock
originalOptions: Epinephrine every other CPR cycle, and amiodarone after the 3rd and 5th cycles
Epinephrine after every shock, and amiodarone after the first shock
Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes (given after the second shock), and amiodarone or lidocaine for refractory VF/pVT after the third shock
Amiodarone after the first shock, and epinephrine only after the fifth shock
Atropine every 3–5 minutes, and amiodarone after the second shock
questions.correctAnswer: C) Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes (given after the second shock), and amiodarone or lidocaine for refractory VF/pVT after the third shock
questions.correctAnswerText: Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes (given after the second shock), and amiodarone or lidocaine for refractory VF/pVT after the third shock
questions.explanation: Epinephrine is timed by interval, not by counting CPR cycles, and amiodarone (300 mg, then 150 mg) or lidocaine is added for shock-refractory VF/pVT. Drugs never replace high-quality CPR and defibrillation.

questions.text: A 55-year-old man presents with stroke symptoms, and CT shows a multilobar infarct involving more than one-third of the cerebral hemisphere. Which therapy is contraindicated?
options: Keeping the patient NPO until the gag reflex is tested
originalOptions: Keeping the patient NPO until the gag reflex is tested
questions.explanation: A very large brain infarct (multilobar, more than one-third of the hemisphere) is an absolute exclusion to fibrinolytic therapy. Oxygen, glucose monitoring, blood pressure monitoring and keeping the patient NPO are supportive measures that remain appropriate.

questions.text: A 79-year-old patient in supraventricular tachycardia has a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg and altered mental status. What is the next appropriate step?
questions.explanation: Hypotension with altered mental status indicates an unstable tachyarrhythmia, which requires immediate synchronized cardioversion. Carotid massage carries a risk of complications in the elderly, and the drugs listed delay definitive treatment.

questions.text: ______ access is preferred during cardiac arrest because it is easily obtained and does not interrupt CPR.
questions.explanation: Peripheral IV is the preferred first-line route and does not require CPR interruption. The order of access is: 1) peripheral IV, 2) IO if IV is not available (wait only about 90 seconds), 3) central line, 4) cut-down. A central line interrupts CPR and has many complications, and the endotracheal route has poor absorption and is not recommended.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a bradycardic rhythm?
questions.explanation: Atrial fibrillation is an irregularly irregular rhythm usually accompanied by a normal or rapid ventricular response. The AV blocks listed are conduction disorders associated with a slow ventricular rate.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct sequence of electrical conduction in normal sinus rhythm?
options: SA node → Purkinje fibres → AV node → Bundle of His
Purkinje fibres → Bundle of His → AV node → SA node
SA node → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres
AV node → SA node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres
SA node → Bundle of His → AV node → Purkinje fibres
originalOptions: SA node → Purkinje fibres → AV node → Bundle of His
Purkinje fibres → Bundle of His → AV node → SA node
SA node → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres
AV node → SA node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres
SA node → Bundle of His → AV node → Purkinje fibres
questions.correctAnswer: C) SA node → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres
questions.correctAnswerText: SA node → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres
questions.explanation: The impulse arises in the SA node, is delayed at the AV node, and then passes through the Bundle of His and bundle branches to the Purkinje fibres to activate the ventricles.

questions.text: What is the maximum time allowed for the initial simultaneous assessment of breathing and pulse in an unresponsive adult?
questions.explanation: If a definite pulse is not felt within 10 seconds, CPR is started or resumed. The 2-minute interval applies to CPR and rhythm-analysis cycles, not to the initial assessment.

questions.text: Most cases of cardiac arrest in children are preceded by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Paediatric arrest is usually asphyxial, following respiratory failure or shock, whereas primary VF/pVT is proportionally less common than in adults. This is why early oxygenation and ventilation are emphasized in paediatric resuscitation.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the time goals of stroke care from the patient's arrival?
options: ED initial evaluation within 25 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 10 minutes, CT read within 45 minutes
ED initial evaluation within 10 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 25 minutes, CT read within 45 minutes
ED initial evaluation within 10 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 45 minutes, CT read within 25 minutes
ED initial evaluation within 25 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 45 minutes, CT read within 60 minutes
ED initial evaluation within 45 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 25 minutes, CT read within 10 minutes
originalOptions: ED initial evaluation within 25 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 10 minutes, CT read within 45 minutes
ED initial evaluation within 10 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 25 minutes, CT read within 45 minutes
ED initial evaluation within 10 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 45 minutes, CT read within 25 minutes
ED initial evaluation within 25 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 45 minutes, CT read within 60 minutes
ED initial evaluation within 45 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 25 minutes, CT read within 10 minutes
questions.correctAnswer: B) ED initial evaluation within 10 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 25 minutes, CT read within 45 minutes
questions.correctAnswerText: ED initial evaluation within 10 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 25 minutes, CT read within 45 minutes
questions.explanation: The stroke-care goals are: ED evaluation within 10 minutes, neurologic evaluation within 25 minutes, and head CT read within 45 minutes of arrival. Fibrinolytic therapy is then evaluated and given within 60 minutes, and admission to the stroke unit occurs within 3 hours.

questions.text: When should out-of-hospital resuscitation efforts be terminated in adults?
options: After exactly 20 minutes of CPR regardless of rhythm
According to a validated termination-of-resuscitation rule (arrest not witnessed by EMS, no shock delivered, no ROSC) combined with clinical judgment
originalOptions: After exactly 20 minutes of CPR regardless of rhythm
According to a validated termination-of-resuscitation rule (arrest not witnessed by EMS, no shock delivered, no ROSC) combined with clinical judgment
questions.correctAnswer: E) According to a validated termination-of-resuscitation rule (arrest not witnessed by EMS, no shock delivered, no ROSC) combined with clinical judgment
questions.correctAnswerText: According to a validated termination-of-resuscitation rule (arrest not witnessed by EMS, no shock delivered, no ROSC) combined with clinical judgment
questions.explanation: Elapsed time alone is never a sufficient reason to stop. Local protocol, reversible causes (e.g., hypothermia, toxicological arrest) and clinical judgment govern termination.

questions.text: A patient has symptomatic bradycardia (heart rate 32/min, hypotension, altered mental status). What is the first-line medication?
questions.explanation: Atropine 0.5 mg IV, repeated every 3–5 minutes to a maximum of 3 mg, is first-line. Transcutaneous pacing and dopamine or epinephrine infusions are the next options if atropine is ineffective, not simultaneous first-line drugs.

questions.text: All of the following are true regarding the management of tachycardia with a pulse EXCEPT:
options: Five CPR cycles are required before rhythm reassessment
Management is determined primarily by haemodynamic stability
An unstable patient requires synchronized cardioversion
A stable, regular, narrow-complex tachycardia is treated with vagal manoeuvres, then adenosine
A stable, irregular, narrow-complex tachycardia (e.g., atrial fibrillation) is treated with rate control
originalOptions: Five CPR cycles are required before rhythm reassessment
Management is determined primarily by haemodynamic stability
An unstable patient requires synchronized cardioversion
A stable, regular, narrow-complex tachycardia is treated with vagal manoeuvres, then adenosine
A stable, irregular, narrow-complex tachycardia (e.g., atrial fibrillation) is treated with rate control
questions.correctAnswer: A) Five CPR cycles are required before rhythm reassessment
questions.correctAnswerText: Five CPR cycles are required before rhythm reassessment
questions.explanation: A patient with tachycardia has a pulse, so CPR cycles do not apply. The 2-minute CPR cycle and rhythm reassessment belong to pulseless cardiac arrest.

questions.text: The six links of the adult Chain of Survival include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Use of cardiovascular medications as a separate link
originalOptions: Use of cardiovascular medications as a separate link
questions.correctAnswer: D) Use of cardiovascular medications as a separate link
questions.correctAnswerText: Use of cardiovascular medications as a separate link
questions.explanation: The links are recognition and activation of emergency response, high-quality CPR, rapid defibrillation, advanced resuscitation, post-cardiac arrest care, and recovery. Medications are part of advanced resuscitation and are not a separate link.

questions.text: Which elements are included in the ACLS Survey?
questions.correctAnswer: B) Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Differential diagnosis
questions.explanation: The ACLS Survey adds a search for the differential diagnosis (reversible causes) to the airway, breathing and circulation assessment, whereas the BLS Survey focuses on CPR and defibrillation.

questions.text: What is an organized electrical rhythm with no palpable pulse called, and how is it managed?
options: Pulseless VT; epinephrine without a shock
Pulseless electrical activity (PEA); immediate unsynchronized defibrillation
Pulseless electrical activity (PEA); high-quality CPR, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and treatment of reversible causes (H's and T's)
originalOptions: Pulseless VT; epinephrine without a shock
Pulseless electrical activity (PEA); immediate unsynchronized defibrillation
Pulseless electrical activity (PEA); high-quality CPR, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and treatment of reversible causes (H's and T's)
questions.correctAnswer: E) Pulseless electrical activity (PEA); high-quality CPR, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and treatment of reversible causes (H's and T's)
questions.correctAnswerText: Pulseless electrical activity (PEA); high-quality CPR, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and treatment of reversible causes (H's and T's)
questions.explanation: PEA is any organized electrical activity without a pulse, other than VF, pulseless VT and true asystole. It is non-shockable, so shocks are given only if VF/pVT appears.

questions.text: The normal sinus rhythm of the heart originates in the:
questions.explanation: The SA node is the natural pacemaker, and its impulse spreads through the atria to the AV node.

questions.text: What is the primary focus of treating cardiac arrest?
options: Both effective CPR and early defibrillation
originalOptions: Both effective CPR and early defibrillation
questions.correctAnswer: A) Both effective CPR and early defibrillation
questions.correctAnswerText: Both effective CPR and early defibrillation
questions.explanation: High-quality CPR and early defibrillation are the interventions most strongly linked to survival. Drugs and advanced airways are secondary and must not delay them.

questions.text: A 3-year-old child begins breathing at 18 breaths/min after rescue breaths, but the pulse is 50/min despite adequate ventilation and oxygenation. What should you do next?
questions.correctAnswer: D) Begin CPR with chest compressions
questions.explanation: In a child, a heart rate below 60/min despite adequate oxygenation and ventilation reflects inadequate perfusion and requires chest compressions.

questions.text: What age is considered an infant for BLS purposes?
questions.explanation: For BLS, an infant is under 1 year of age and a child is from 1 year to puberty. Adolescents and older are managed with the adult algorithm.

questions.text: What does the QRS complex on the ECG represent?
options: Delay of conduction at the AV node
originalOptions: Delay of conduction at the AV node
questions.explanation: The QRS complex is ventricular depolarization, which triggers ventricular contraction. The T wave represents ventricular repolarization, and the P wave represents atrial depolarization.

questions.text: Which factor is critical to assess in any emergency situation before approaching the patient?
questions.explanation: Scene safety is confirmed first so that the rescuer does not become a second casualty.

questions.text: What is the recommended method to monitor breathing and ventilation during ACLS care?
questions.explanation: Waveform capnography gives continuous objective information on ventilation, confirms endotracheal tube placement and reflects CPR quality. Pulse oximetry and clinical assessment are complementary.

questions.text: What is the role of the second rescuer during a cardiac arrest scenario?
questions.explanation: Any additional rescuer is used according to skill level, including summoning help, retrieving the AED and providing ventilations.

questions.text: Which piece of data is critical to obtain in all patients with acute stroke?
questions.explanation: Eligibility for fibrinolysis depends on the time of symptom onset, which is measured from the time the patient was last seen normal.

questions.text: How often should compressors switch during two-rescuer CPR?
options: About every 2 minutes, with the pause kept as short as possible
originalOptions: About every 2 minutes, with the pause kept as short as possible
questions.correctAnswer: E) About every 2 minutes, with the pause kept as short as possible
questions.correctAnswerText: About every 2 minutes, with the pause kept as short as possible
questions.explanation: Rotating roughly every 2 minutes prevents compressor fatigue, which reduces compression quality. The switch is done during the rhythm check to minimize interruption.

questions.text: Where should a pulse check be performed in an adult?
questions.explanation: The carotid artery is the standard central pulse site in adults and remains palpable in low-flow states. The brachial artery is used in infants.

questions.text: Which of the following is first-line treatment for acute coronary syndrome?
questions.explanation: The initial ACS treatment (MONA: Morphine, Oxygen, Nitroglycerin, Aspirin) includes aspirin, nitroglycerin and morphine together, each with its own conditions (aspirin if no allergy, nitroglycerin if SBP is 90 mmHg or above, morphine if nitrates fail).

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an advanced airway?
questions.explanation: The oropharyngeal airway is a basic airway adjunct that only keeps the tongue off the posterior pharynx in an unconscious patient without a gag reflex.

questions.text: Which of the following is true regarding BLS?
options: It should be mastered before ACLS
It has little impact on survival
It applies only to out-of-hospital arrests
originalOptions: It should be mastered before ACLS
It has little impact on survival
It applies only to out-of-hospital arrests
questions.correctAnswer: B) It should be mastered before ACLS
questions.correctAnswerText: It should be mastered before ACLS
questions.explanation: ACLS providers are expected to have mastered BLS, because high-quality CPR is the foundation of resuscitation and has a major impact on survival.

questions.text: Which sequence best represents the adult Chain of Survival?
options: Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, provide ventilations, defibrillate, recovery
Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, defibrillate, recovery
Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, wait for advanced care, recovery
Call EMS, begin chest compressions, give rescue breaths only, recovery
Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, begin chest compressions, provide early defibrillation, recovery
originalOptions: Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, provide ventilations, defibrillate, recovery
Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, defibrillate, recovery
Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, wait for advanced care, recovery
Call EMS, begin chest compressions, give rescue breaths only, recovery
Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, begin chest compressions, provide early defibrillation, recovery
questions.correctAnswer: E) Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, begin chest compressions, provide early defibrillation, recovery
questions.correctAnswerText: Check responsiveness, call EMS and get an AED, begin chest compressions, provide early defibrillation, recovery
questions.explanation: The emphasis is on early high-quality CPR and early defibrillation between activation of the emergency response and recovery.

questions.text: While one rescuer is performing CPR on an infant, a second rescuer arrives. What should happen next?
options: The second rescuer takes over compressions alone while the first rescuer leaves
The second rescuer waits until the first rescuer is exhausted
The second rescuer activates the emergency response system and retrieves the AED if this has not been done, then assists with two-rescuer CPR
The second rescuer applies AED pads without confirming EMS activation
The first rescuer stops CPR to hand over the infant
originalOptions: The second rescuer takes over compressions alone while the first rescuer leaves
The second rescuer waits until the first rescuer is exhausted
The second rescuer activates the emergency response system and retrieves the AED if this has not been done, then assists with two-rescuer CPR
The second rescuer applies AED pads without confirming EMS activation
The first rescuer stops CPR to hand over the infant
questions.correctAnswer: C) The second rescuer activates the emergency response system and retrieves the AED if this has not been done, then assists with two-rescuer CPR
questions.correctAnswerText: The second rescuer activates the emergency response system and retrieves the AED if this has not been done, then assists with two-rescuer CPR
questions.explanation: Two-rescuer infant CPR uses coordinated roles with a 15:2 ratio, while ensuring that EMS and an AED have been summoned.

questions.text: During adult CPR with an advanced airway in place, what is the ventilation rate?
options: One breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths/min) with continuous chest compressions
originalOptions: One breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths/min) with continuous chest compressions
questions.correctAnswer: A) One breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths/min) with continuous chest compressions
questions.correctAnswerText: One breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths/min) with continuous chest compressions
questions.explanation: With an advanced airway, ventilation is asynchronous and compressions are not paused. The 30:2 ratio applies only without an advanced airway, and excessive ventilation raises intrathoracic pressure and reduces venous return.

questions.text: You are alone with an unresponsive 3-year-old child who is not breathing and appears blue (unwitnessed collapse). What should you do first?
options: Leave immediately to activate EMS and get an AED
Give rescue breaths only for 2 minutes
Place the child in the recovery position
Give about 2 minutes of CPR, then activate EMS and get an AED
Wait for a second rescuer before starting CPR
originalOptions: Leave immediately to activate EMS and get an AED
Give rescue breaths only for 2 minutes
Place the child in the recovery position
Give about 2 minutes of CPR, then activate EMS and get an AED
Wait for a second rescuer before starting CPR
questions.correctAnswer: D) Give about 2 minutes of CPR, then activate EMS and get an AED
questions.correctAnswerText: Give about 2 minutes of CPR, then activate EMS and get an AED
questions.explanation: In an unwitnessed paediatric arrest with a lone rescuer, 2 minutes of CPR comes before leaving to call for help, because paediatric arrest is usually asphyxial and responds to early ventilation and compressions. The recovery position is for a patient who is breathing.

questions.text: Peripheral IV access has failed in a patient in cardiac arrest (e.g., during transport). What is the next step?
options: Central venous access via the femoral vein
Central venous access via the internal jugular vein
Administer all medications through the endotracheal tube
originalOptions: Central venous access via the femoral vein
Central venous access via the internal jugular vein
Administer all medications through the endotracheal tube
questions.explanation: IO access is rapid, works even in shock, and does not interrupt CPR. Central lines require interruption of compressions, and drug absorption through the endotracheal tube is unreliable.

questions.text: An adult has a definite pulse but is not breathing normally. What rescue breathing rate should be used?
options: One breath every 5–6 seconds (10–12 breaths/min), with visible chest rise
originalOptions: One breath every 5–6 seconds (10–12 breaths/min), with visible chest rise
questions.correctAnswer: E) One breath every 5–6 seconds (10–12 breaths/min), with visible chest rise
questions.correctAnswerText: One breath every 5–6 seconds (10–12 breaths/min), with visible chest rise
questions.explanation: For an adult with a pulse who is not breathing normally, start rescue breathing at one breath every 5–6 seconds (10–12 breaths/min) and check the pulse every 2 minutes. With an advanced airway during CPR the rate is one breath every 6 seconds.

questions.text: Which of the following describes high-quality adult CPR?
options: 80 compressions/min at a depth of at least 1 inch
80 compressions/min at a depth of at least 2 inches
100–120 compressions/min at a depth of 2–2.4 inches (5–6 cm)
100 compressions/min at a depth of at least 1 inch
60–80 compressions/min at a depth of 2 inches (5 cm)
originalOptions: 80 compressions/min at a depth of at least 1 inch
80 compressions/min at a depth of at least 2 inches
100–120 compressions/min at a depth of 2–2.4 inches (5–6 cm)
100 compressions/min at a depth of at least 1 inch
60–80 compressions/min at a depth of 2 inches (5 cm)
questions.correctAnswer: C) 100–120 compressions/min at a depth of 2–2.4 inches (5–6 cm)
questions.correctAnswerText: 100–120 compressions/min at a depth of 2–2.4 inches (5–6 cm)
questions.explanation: High-quality CPR also requires full chest recoil, minimal interruptions (no more than 10 seconds) and avoidance of excessive ventilation.

questions.text: What is the single-rescuer adult compression-to-ventilation ratio before an advanced airway is placed?
questions.explanation: The adult ratio is 30:2 until an advanced airway is placed, after which compressions are continuous with one breath every 6 seconds.

questions.text: During high-quality CPR, which ETCO2 range indicates adequate chest compressions?
questions.explanation: An ETCO2 of at least 10–20 mmHg reflects adequate compressions, whereas a persistent value below 10 mmHg suggests poor CPR quality or a low likelihood of ROSC. A sudden rise to 40 mmHg or more suggests ROSC.

questions.text: All of the following are correct regarding basic life support (BLS) EXCEPT:
options: Personal and scene safety must be ensured first
Single-rescuer CPR in a child uses a compression-to-ventilation ratio of 15:2
Two-rescuer CPR in a child uses a ratio of 15:2
The brachial artery is used for the pulse check in infants
An infant is defined as a child under 1 year of age
originalOptions: Personal and scene safety must be ensured first
Single-rescuer CPR in a child uses a compression-to-ventilation ratio of 15:2
Two-rescuer CPR in a child uses a ratio of 15:2
The brachial artery is used for the pulse check in infants
An infant is defined as a child under 1 year of age
questions.correctAnswer: B) Single-rescuer CPR in a child uses a compression-to-ventilation ratio of 15:2
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-rescuer CPR in a child uses a compression-to-ventilation ratio of 15:2
questions.explanation: Single-rescuer paediatric CPR uses the universal 30:2 ratio. The 15:2 ratio is used strictly when two or more trained healthcare rescuers are present to provide optimal ventilation. All other statements are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following is an effect of excessive ventilation during CPR?
options: Increased venous return to the heart
Increased intrathoracic pressure with decreased venous return to the heart
originalOptions: Increased venous return to the heart
Increased intrathoracic pressure with decreased venous return to the heart
questions.correctAnswer: E) Increased intrathoracic pressure with decreased venous return to the heart
questions.correctAnswerText: Increased intrathoracic pressure with decreased venous return to the heart
questions.explanation: Over-ventilation raises intrathoracic pressure, which impedes venous return, lowers cardiac output and coronary perfusion, and reduces the chance of ROSC. It also increases the risk of gastric insufflation and aspiration.

questions.text: PEA includes any pulseless organized rhythm EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: PEA is organized electrical activity without a pulse. VF, pulseless VT and true asystole are managed as separate categories in the cardiac arrest algorithm.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a cause of pulseless electrical activity (PEA)?
questions.explanation: The reversible causes are the H's and T's: hypovolaemia, hypoxia, hydrogen ion (acidosis), hypo-/hyperkalaemia and hypothermia; tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, and thrombosis (pulmonary or coronary). Hyperventilation is not among them.

questions.text: Which medication can be used to treat hypotension in the post-cardiac arrest phase?
questions.explanation: Vasopressor and inotropic support (dopamine; norepinephrine is also used, chosen by haemodynamic profile and local protocol) maintains blood pressure after ROSC. The other drugs are antiarrhythmics or are used for bradycardia and do not treat hypotension.

questions.text: After activating EMS and sending someone for an AED, what is the next action for a lone rescuer with an unresponsive adult who has no pulse?
questions.explanation: An unresponsive adult without a pulse needs CPR, with chest compressions started immediately and ventilations added afterwards.

questions.text: An AED can be used safely in all of the following situations EXCEPT:
options: Victim with an implanted pacemaker (pad placed away from the device)
Victim with a transdermal medication patch (patch removed)
Victim with a hairy chest (excess hair removed before pad application)
Victim lying partially in water, who has not been moved to a dry area
originalOptions: Victim with an implanted pacemaker (pad placed away from the device)
Victim with a transdermal medication patch (patch removed)
Victim with a hairy chest (excess hair removed before pad application)
Victim lying partially in water, who has not been moved to a dry area
questions.correctAnswer: E) Victim lying partially in water, who has not been moved to a dry area
questions.correctAnswerText: Victim lying partially in water, who has not been moved to a dry area
questions.explanation: Water conducts current, so the victim must be moved away from water and the chest dried before pad application. The other situations are safe provided the pad site is adjusted.

questions.text: A patient with a pulse has monomorphic ventricular tachycardia with hypotension and altered mental status. What is the indicated treatment?
questions.explanation: Unstable VT with a pulse requires immediate synchronized cardioversion. Unsynchronized defibrillation is reserved for pulseless VT/VF, and amiodarone is an adjunct for stable or refractory VT.

questions.text: At what age is it preferable to use paediatric AED pads?
questions.correctAnswer: A) Less than 8 years of age
questions.explanation: Paediatric pads or an attenuator are preferred for children under about 8 years (or under about 25 kg). If they are unavailable, adult pads are used rather than withholding the shock.

questions.text: What is the recommended defibrillation energy for monophasic versus biphasic defibrillators?
options: Both use a fixed dose of 150 J
Monophasic 360 J for all shocks; biphasic 120–200 J per manufacturer recommendation (maximum available dose if unknown)
originalOptions: Both use a fixed dose of 150 J
Monophasic 360 J for all shocks; biphasic 120–200 J per manufacturer recommendation (maximum available dose if unknown)
questions.correctAnswer: D) Monophasic 360 J for all shocks; biphasic 120–200 J per manufacturer recommendation (maximum available dose if unknown)
questions.correctAnswerText: Monophasic 360 J for all shocks; biphasic 120–200 J per manufacturer recommendation (maximum available dose if unknown)
questions.explanation: Monophasic devices deliver a fixed 360 J, whereas biphasic devices are more efficient and use lower energy as specified by the manufacturer.

questions.text: During resuscitation for pulseless VT, after two cycles the patient remains pulseless and the monitor now shows an organized SVT-like rhythm. What should be done?
options: Treat as PEA: resume high-quality CPR, give epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and treat reversible causes; shock only if VF/pVT recurs
Give adenosine to convert the rhythm
Deliver an unsynchronized shock because the arrest began as pulseless VT
originalOptions: Treat as PEA: resume high-quality CPR, give epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and treat reversible causes; shock only if VF/pVT recurs
Give adenosine to convert the rhythm
Deliver an unsynchronized shock because the arrest began as pulseless VT
questions.correctAnswer: B) Treat as PEA: resume high-quality CPR, give epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and treat reversible causes; shock only if VF/pVT recurs
questions.correctAnswerText: Treat as PEA: resume high-quality CPR, give epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and treat reversible causes; shock only if VF/pVT recurs
questions.explanation: Treatment follows the current pulseless rhythm, not the preceding one. An organized rhythm without a pulse is PEA and is not shocked.

questions.text: Which of the following are the criteria for applying an AED to a collapsed patient?
options: Unresponsive, not breathing normally, and no definite pulse
originalOptions: Unresponsive, not breathing normally, and no definite pulse
questions.correctAnswer: E) Unresponsive, not breathing normally, and no definite pulse
questions.correctAnswerText: Unresponsive, not breathing normally, and no definite pulse
questions.explanation: The AED is applied as soon as it is available to a patient who meets all three criteria, with minimal interruption of CPR to attach it.

questions.text: The AED advises "Shock." What is the next step?
options: Deliver two additional minutes of CPR before the shock
Ventilate the patient while the shock is delivered
Clear everyone from the patient and deliver the shock
Assume device error and do not deliver the shock
Check for a pulse and then deliver the shock
originalOptions: Deliver two additional minutes of CPR before the shock
Ventilate the patient while the shock is delivered
Clear everyone from the patient and deliver the shock
Assume device error and do not deliver the shock
Check for a pulse and then deliver the shock
questions.correctAnswer: C) Clear everyone from the patient and deliver the shock
questions.correctAnswerText: Clear everyone from the patient and deliver the shock
questions.explanation: Once a shock is advised it should not be delayed for additional CPR or a pulse check, and all rescuers must be clear of the patient when it is delivered.

questions.text: Which listed medication is NOT used in the adult algorithm for persistent VF or pulseless VT?
questions.explanation: Persistent VF/pulseless VT is managed with repeated defibrillation, high-quality CPR, epinephrine, and amiodarone or lidocaine. Atropine is used for symptomatic bradycardia and has no role in shockable arrest. Magnesium sulfate is reserved for pulseless torsades de pointes, so it was removed from the options to avoid ambiguity.

questions.text: What are the proper steps for operating an AED?
options: Power on, attach electrode pads, shock the patient, analyze the rhythm
Power on, analyze the rhythm, attach electrode pads, shock the patient
Power on, shock the patient, attach electrode pads, analyze the rhythm
Power on, attach electrode pads, analyze the rhythm, shock the patient
Attach electrode pads, shock the patient, power on, analyze the rhythm
originalOptions: Power on, attach electrode pads, shock the patient, analyze the rhythm
Power on, analyze the rhythm, attach electrode pads, shock the patient
Power on, shock the patient, attach electrode pads, analyze the rhythm
Power on, attach electrode pads, analyze the rhythm, shock the patient
Attach electrode pads, shock the patient, power on, analyze the rhythm
questions.correctAnswer: D) Power on, attach electrode pads, analyze the rhythm, shock the patient
questions.correctAnswerText: Power on, attach electrode pads, analyze the rhythm, shock the patient
questions.explanation: The AED needs power and attached pads before it can analyze the rhythm, and a shock is delivered only if analysis finds a shockable rhythm.

questions.text: How is refractory ventricular fibrillation managed in the adult cardiac arrest algorithm?
options: Stop CPR and give epinephrine alone
Continue high-quality CPR with repeated defibrillation, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and amiodarone or lidocaine (typically after the third shock), while treating reversible causes
Give atropine as the primary antiarrhythmic
originalOptions: Stop CPR and give epinephrine alone
Continue high-quality CPR with repeated defibrillation, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and amiodarone or lidocaine (typically after the third shock), while treating reversible causes
Give atropine as the primary antiarrhythmic
questions.correctAnswer: B) Continue high-quality CPR with repeated defibrillation, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and amiodarone or lidocaine (typically after the third shock), while treating reversible causes
questions.correctAnswerText: Continue high-quality CPR with repeated defibrillation, epinephrine every 3–5 minutes, and amiodarone or lidocaine (typically after the third shock), while treating reversible causes
questions.explanation: Drugs are added to, and never replace, CPR and defibrillation. Synchronized cardioversion is for rhythms with a pulse, and atropine and adenosine have no role in VF.

questions.text: What does AED stand for?
questions.explanation: An AED analyzes the cardiac rhythm and delivers a shock if a shockable rhythm is detected.

questions.text: What is the first step after a shockable rhythm is detected on the defibrillator?
options: Deliver the shock and immediately resume CPR
originalOptions: Deliver the shock and immediately resume CPR
questions.correctAnswer: C) Deliver the shock and immediately resume CPR
questions.correctAnswerText: Deliver the shock and immediately resume CPR
questions.explanation: The shock is delivered promptly and CPR resumed at once, without pausing for a pulse check or drug administration.

questions.text: When should the rhythm be rechecked after a shock delivered by an AED?
options: After one 2-minute cycle of CPR, or whenever the AED prompts a rhythm analysis
originalOptions: After one 2-minute cycle of CPR, or whenever the AED prompts a rhythm analysis
questions.correctAnswer: A) After one 2-minute cycle of CPR, or whenever the AED prompts a rhythm analysis
questions.correctAnswerText: After one 2-minute cycle of CPR, or whenever the AED prompts a rhythm analysis
questions.explanation: CPR resumes immediately after the shock and the rhythm is reassessed about every 2 minutes. A pulse is checked only if an organized rhythm or signs of ROSC appear, and CPR is not paused after every 30 compressions.

questions.text: Where are standard anterolateral AED pads placed?
options: Both pads on the anterior chest, side by side
Right lower chest and left upper chest
Directly over the sternum, one above the other
Right upper chest (below the right clavicle) and left lower lateral chest (below the left armpit)
Both pads on the left lateral chest
originalOptions: Both pads on the anterior chest, side by side
Right lower chest and left upper chest
Directly over the sternum, one above the other
Right upper chest (below the right clavicle) and left lower lateral chest (below the left armpit)
Both pads on the left lateral chest
questions.correctAnswer: D) Right upper chest (below the right clavicle) and left lower lateral chest (below the left armpit)
questions.correctAnswerText: Right upper chest (below the right clavicle) and left lower lateral chest (below the left armpit)
questions.explanation: This placement directs the current through the heart. A pad must not be placed directly over an implanted device, and a wet chest must be dried.

questions.text: Which of the following, by itself, is NOT a sign of haemodynamic instability in a patient with atrial flutter?
questions.correctAnswer: B) A high ventricular rate alone
questions.explanation: Instability is defined by hypotension or shock, altered consciousness, ischaemic chest pain and acute pulmonary oedema. The rate must be interpreted together with perfusion and symptoms.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a sign of instability in a patient with a tachyarrhythmia?
questions.explanation: Instability features are hypotension, decreased level of consciousness, signs of shock, severe chest pain and pulmonary oedema (acute heart failure). Hypertension alone, without symptoms, is not a sign of instability.

questions.text: All of the following are true regarding paediatric versus adult airway and chest anatomy EXCEPT:
options: The airway is narrowest at the subglottic/cricoid area
The cervical spine is relatively straight
