questions.explanation: Schizencephaly clefts are actually lined by grey matter (heterotopic cortex), not white matter. Laterality, symptom severity, and the presence of pial-ependymal communication in both types are all accurate characteristics of the condition.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: All of the following are intramedullary lesions, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Schwannoma is an intradural extramedullary tumor arising from a nerve root sheath, unlike astrocytoma, ependymoma, hemangioblastoma, and ganglioglioma, which are intramedullary.

questions.text: All of the following appear hyperintense on T2 MRI, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Air produces a signal void and appears hypointense on all MRI sequences, unlike fatty marrow, late subacute hematoma, choroid plexus papilloma, and GBM, which are typically T2 hyperintense.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT found in hyperacute brain ischemia?
options: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
originalOptions: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.correctAnswer: E) Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.correctAnswerText: Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.explanation: These are late/chronic infarct changes (>3 weeks); the hyperacute stage (0–6 hours) instead shows subtle grey-white loss, cortical hypodensity, gyral effacement, and loss of the insular ribbon sign.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the parietal bones with the occipital bone?
questions.explanation: The lambdoid suture joins both parietal bones with the occipital bone posteriorly; coronal joins frontal to parietal, sagittal joins the two parietals, and metopic joins the two frontal bones.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the frontal and parietal bones?
questions.explanation: The coronal suture joins the frontal and parietal bones, distinct from the squamosal suture which joins the temporal and parietal bones, the metopic suture which joins the two frontal bones, the sagittal suture which joins the two parietal bones, and the lambdoid suture which joins the occipital and parietal bones.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the two parietal bones?
questions.explanation: The sagittal suture runs in the midline joining the two parietal bones to each other.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the two frontal bones?
questions.explanation: The metopic suture is the embryological midline suture between the two frontal bones, which normally fuses in early childhood.

questions.text: Which of the following radiologic features, if present, is supportive of the diagnosis of Sturge-Weber syndrome?
options: Restriction on DWI in both PCA territories
originalOptions: Restriction on DWI in both PCA territories
questions.explanation: Sturge-Weber syndrome classically shows gyriform ("tram-track") cortical/subcortical calcification underlying the leptomeningeal angioma; the other features belong to different conditions (MS, tuberous sclerosis).
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the Circle of Willis is FALSE?
options: The superior cerebellar artery (SCA) arises from the distal basilar artery
The Circle of Willis provides collateral circulation between anterior and posterior circulation
The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid artery to the posterior cerebral artery
The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
originalOptions: The superior cerebellar artery (SCA) arises from the distal basilar artery
The Circle of Willis provides collateral circulation between anterior and posterior circulation
The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid artery to the posterior cerebral artery
The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
questions.correctAnswer: D) The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
questions.correctAnswerText: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
questions.explanation: AICA is a branch of the proximal basilar artery; the distal vertebral artery instead gives rise to PICA. SCA does arise from the distal basilar artery, and the Circle of Willis does provide interhemispheric collateral flow.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding cranial nerve involvement in multiple sclerosis?
options: The trigeminal nerve (CN5) can be affected
The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
The abducens nerve (CN6) can be affected
Optic nerve involvement (optic neuritis) is common
originalOptions: The trigeminal nerve (CN5) can be affected
The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
The abducens nerve (CN6) can be affected
Optic nerve involvement (optic neuritis) is common
questions.correctAnswer: B) The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
questions.correctAnswerText: The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
questions.explanation: Optic neuritis (CN2) is the most common cranial nerve manifestation of MS, followed by CN5/6; oculomotor involvement is not the classic pattern.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about MS lesion characteristics is TRUE?
options: Active plaques characteristically do not enhance with contrast
Diffuse cerebral atrophy is an early MS finding
T1-hypointense "black hole" lesions indicate a better prognosis
Enhancement never occurs in MS lesions
T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
originalOptions: Active plaques characteristically do not enhance with contrast
Diffuse cerebral atrophy is an early MS finding
T1-hypointense "black hole" lesions indicate a better prognosis
Enhancement never occurs in MS lesions
T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
questions.correctAnswer: E) T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
questions.correctAnswerText: T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
questions.explanation: T1 hypointensity reflects irreversible axonal loss; active plaques classically DO enhance (reflecting blood-brain barrier breakdown), and diffuse atrophy is typically a late finding.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about primary CNS lymphoma is FALSE?
options: It is typically hyperdense on non-contrast CT
It shows restricted diffusion on DWI
The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
It shows homogeneous enhancement in immunocompetent patients
originalOptions: It is typically hyperdense on non-contrast CT
It shows restricted diffusion on DWI
The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
It shows homogeneous enhancement in immunocompetent patients
questions.correctAnswer: C) The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
questions.correctAnswerText: The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
questions.explanation: Primary CNS lymphoma is highly cellular and restricts diffusion, so its ADC value is typically LOWER, not higher, than normal brain.

questions.text: Which of the following anatomical relationships is CORRECT?
options: The claustrum lies lateral to the insula
The hippocampus lies anterosuperior to the amygdala
The uncus forms the lateral border of the temporal lobe
The claustrum lies medial to the putamen, separated by the internal capsule
originalOptions: The claustrum lies lateral to the insula
The hippocampus lies anterosuperior to the amygdala
The uncus forms the lateral border of the temporal lobe
The claustrum lies medial to the putamen, separated by the internal capsule
questions.correctAnswer: A) The claustrum lies lateral to the insula
questions.correctAnswerText: The claustrum lies lateral to the insula
questions.explanation: The claustrum is a thin sheet of grey matter lateral to the insula (separated by the extreme capsule); the hippocampus lies posteroinferior (not anterosuperior) to the amygdala, and the uncus is the medial (not lateral) temporal border.

questions.text: On T1-weighted MRI, which of the following statements about basal ganglia signal is TRUE?
options: The putamen is hyperintense relative to the globus pallidus
The caudate is hyperintense relative to the thalamus
The globus pallidus is isointense to the putamen
The globus pallidus is hyperintense relative to the putamen
originalOptions: The putamen is hyperintense relative to the globus pallidus
The caudate is hyperintense relative to the thalamus
The globus pallidus is isointense to the putamen
The globus pallidus is hyperintense relative to the putamen
questions.correctAnswer: D) The globus pallidus is hyperintense relative to the putamen
questions.correctAnswerText: The globus pallidus is hyperintense relative to the putamen
questions.explanation: On T1-weighted MRI, the globus pallidus normally appears relatively hyperintense compared with the putamen — a useful anatomical landmark.

questions.text: Which of the following locations is NOT typical for hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage?
questions.explanation: Hypertensive ICH classically occurs in deep structures (basal ganglia, thalamus, pons, cerebellum) supplied by small penetrating vessels; a lobar location like the frontal lobe instead suggests another etiology (e.g., amyloid angiopathy, AVM, tumor).

questions.text: Which stage of hemorrhage is classically hyperintense on both T1 and T2-weighted MRI due to extracellular methemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Late subacute hemorrhage (extracellular methemoglobin) is T1 and T2 hyperintense; early subacute (intracellular methemoglobin) is T1 hyperintense but T2 hypointense, and acute/chronic stages are T2 hypointense.

questions.text: Regarding cerebral sinus thrombosis, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Sinus thrombosis is an occlusion of arterial channels in the cranial cavity
The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
The dura typically does not enhance
A hypodense sinus is seen on non-contrast CT
originalOptions: Sinus thrombosis is an occlusion of arterial channels in the cranial cavity
The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
The dura typically does not enhance
A hypodense sinus is seen on non-contrast CT
questions.correctAnswer: C) The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
questions.correctAnswerText: The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
questions.explanation: The empty delta sign — a triangular filling defect surrounded by enhancing dura — is classically seen on contrast-enhanced imaging; sinus thrombosis is a venous (not arterial) occlusion, acute thrombus typically does NOT enhance, the dura DOES enhance, and non-contrast CT shows a hyperdense (not hypodense) sinus.

questions.text: Regarding subdural hematoma, which of the following is TRUE?
options: It does not cross the falx cerebri
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
originalOptions: It does not cross the falx cerebri
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
questions.correctAnswer: A) It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.correctAnswerText: It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.explanation: Subdural hematoma is confined by the falx cerebri and tentorium but CAN cross suture lines (opposite epidural hematoma); it is typically caused by bridging vein tears (not the middle meningeal artery) and has a crescentic (not lenticular) shape.

questions.text: Regarding extradural (epidural) hematoma, which of the following is FALSE?
options: It does not cross the falx cerebri
There is a history of trauma
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery
originalOptions: It does not cross the falx cerebri
There is a history of trauma
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery
questions.correctAnswer: A) It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.correctAnswerText: It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.explanation: Epidural hematoma CAN cross the falx cerebri but does NOT cross cranial sutures (opposite the pattern of subdural hematoma); the other listed features are true.

questions.text: Which one of the following is a common radiologic feature of diffuse brain edema?
questions.explanation: Diffuse cerebral edema effaces the sulci and narrows the ventricles/basal cisterns; the brain typically appears diffusely hypodense (not hyperdense) except for the relatively dense-appearing cerebellum.

questions.text: Identify the labeled structure. [img: Radiologynanatomyuncusbrain.png ]
options: Anterior Horn of the Lateral Ventricle
originalOptions: Anterior Horn of the Lateral Ventricle
questions.explanation: I don't know what to write; there's no explanation :)

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the corpus callosum?
questions.explanation: The thalamus is a deep grey matter nucleus located centrally in the brain, distinct from the components of the corpus callosum which is a major white matter tract anatomically divided into the rostrum, genu, body, and splenium.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapancreatitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows a diffusely enlarged, edematous pancreas with peripancreatic fat stranding, the classic acute pancreatitis pattern; a discrete mass (adenocarcinoma) is not seen.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumobilia.png ]
questions.explanation: The gas is centrally located within the biliary tree near the porta hepatis; portal venous gas classically extends to within 2 cm of the liver capsule (peripheral), which distinguishes it from pneumobilia.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumoperitoneum.png ]
questions.explanation: Free intraperitoneal air is seen outlining the bowel loops and under the diaphragm, diagnostic of pneumoperitoneum rather than a fluid- or obstruction-related process.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaportalvenousgas.png ]
questions.explanation: The tiny branching gas foci extend to the peripheral 2 cm of the liver, characteristic of portal venous gas; pneumobilia by contrast is centrally distributed near the porta hepatis.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyahydronephrosis.png ]
questions.explanation: The coronal CT shows dilatation of the left renal collecting system (pelvicalyceal dilation) without a discrete simple fluid collection, consistent with hydronephrosis rather than an isolated stone or cyst.

questions.text: Not true about achalasia?
options: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
originalOptions: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.correctAnswer: D) Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.correctAnswerText: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.explanation: Anterior tracheal displacement/bowing from the dilated esophagus is a lateral-view finding, not a frontal-view finding, making this statement false.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyamidgutvolvulus.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows the classic whirlpool sign of the superior mesenteric vessels and mesentery twisting around each other, diagnostic of midgut volvulus (from malrotation).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaappendicitisct.png ]
questions.explanation: The coronal CT shows an appendicolith with a dilated, thick-walled appendix and surrounding fat stranding, diagnostic of acute appendicitis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaachalasia.png ]
questions.explanation: The barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering smoothly to a "bird-beak" narrowing at the gastroesophageal junction, the classic finding of achalasia.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyarenalstonehydronephrosis.png ]
questions.correctAnswer: A) Obstructing renal stone with hydronephrosis
questions.explanation: The CT shows a calculus with upstream dilatation of the collecting system, consistent with an obstructing stone causing hydronephrosis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyasmallbowelobstruction.png ]
questions.explanation: The supine film shows multiple centrally located dilated loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full lumen width, typical of small (not large) bowel obstruction.

questions.text: Which statement is wrong about pyloric stenosis?
options: A longitudinal measurement > 7 mm alone is the defining diagnostic criterion
Pyloric canal length is usually 15–17 mm
Single pyloric wall thickness > 3 mm is diagnostic
originalOptions: A longitudinal measurement > 7 mm alone is the defining diagnostic criterion
Pyloric canal length is usually 15–17 mm
Single pyloric wall thickness > 3 mm is diagnostic
questions.correctAnswer: A) A longitudinal measurement > 7 mm alone is the defining diagnostic criterion
questions.correctAnswerText: A longitudinal measurement > 7 mm alone is the defining diagnostic criterion
questions.explanation: The accepted diagnostic criteria are muscle wall thickness > 3 mm and canal length > 15–17 mm; a "> 7 mm" longitudinal measurement is not the recognized standalone criterion.

questions.text: Which statement is wrong about colonic intussusception?
options: About 95% of cases occur in children
Most commonly due to a benign tumor in adults
Ileocolic type is the most common location
originalOptions: About 95% of cases occur in children
Most commonly due to a benign tumor in adults
Ileocolic type is the most common location
questions.correctAnswer: B) Most commonly due to a benign tumor in adults
questions.correctAnswerText: Most commonly due to a benign tumor in adults
questions.explanation: In adult colonic intussusception, a malignant tumor (such as primary adenocarcinoma) is the most common lead point rather than a benign lesion, making this statement false.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides. || In adults, over 80% of cases have a clear structural cause, which is mostly benign (85–90%) in the small bowel but mainly malignant (50–65%) in the colon and large intestine. || In children, up to 90% of cases are idiopathic, meaning they have no clear cause and are usually triggered by swollen lymph tissue from a viral infection.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyagallstonesmri.png ]
questions.explanation: The MRI/MRCP shows the gallbladder packed with multiple calculi, the defining finding for cholelithiasis (gallstones); the dilated CBD with ductal stones represents an associated complication rather than the primary diagnosis being tested.

questions.text: Wrong about Wilms tumor?
options: Most common renal tumor of childhood
Lung metastases are less common than bone metastases
Presents as a painless abdominal mass
originalOptions: Most common renal tumor of childhood
Lung metastases are less common than bone metastases
Presents as a painless abdominal mass
questions.correctAnswer: B) Lung metastases are less common than bone metastases
questions.correctAnswerText: Lung metastases are less common than bone metastases
questions.explanation: The lungs are the most common site of metastasis in Wilms tumor (not less common than bone) , bone metastases are actually rare.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: What is the best first imaging modality for a pregnant patient with a palpable breast lump?
questions.explanation: Ultrasound uses no ionizing radiation and is the modality of choice for symptomatic pregnant or young (<30 years) patients. It also distinguishes cystic from solid lesions and can guide biopsy. Mammography and CT use radiation, and MRI needs gadolinium, so none of them is first-line.

questions.text: Which of the following features suggests a malignant breast mass on imaging?
options: Oval shape with posterior acoustic enhancement
Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
Coarse popcorn-like calcification within the mass
originalOptions: Oval shape with posterior acoustic enhancement
Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
Coarse popcorn-like calcification within the mass
questions.correctAnswer: C) Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
questions.correctAnswerText: Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
questions.explanation: Irregular shape and spiculated or indistinct margins are the most suspicious mass features for malignancy. Round or oval circumscribed masses are usually benign (cyst or fibroadenoma). Fat density suggests a lipoma or hamartoma, and popcorn calcification suggests an involuting fibroadenoma.

questions.text: A palpable mass is located at the 5 o'clock position in the right breast. Which quadrant is this?
questions.explanation: In the right breast, 9 o'clock is lateral, so 3–6 o'clock is the lower inner quadrant and 6–9 is the lower outer. The 5 o'clock position therefore lies in the lower inner quadrant.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about mammography is FALSE?
options: Axillary lymph nodes with central lucency may be benign
Sensitivity of mammography is reduced in dense breasts
Dense breast tissue in young women requires further evaluation
Spiculated masses are suspicious for malignancy
originalOptions: Axillary lymph nodes with central lucency may be benign
Sensitivity of mammography is reduced in dense breasts
Dense breast tissue in young women requires further evaluation
Spiculated masses are suspicious for malignancy
questions.explanation: Fine pleomorphic calcifications are a suspicious morphology. The typically benign types are skin, vascular, popcorn, rod-like, round or punctate, rim, and milk of calcium.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the BI-RADS classification is FALSE?
options: BI-RADS 3 indicates a probably benign finding
originalOptions: BI-RADS 3 indicates a probably benign finding
questions.explanation: BI-RADS 5 is highly suggestive of malignancy (>95%), so it is not benign. BI-RADS 2 is benign and BI-RADS 3 is probably benign.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycheartfailure.png ]
questions.explanation: Cardiomegaly with cephalization, Kerley B lines and interstitial/alveolar edema indicates heart failure. Bilateral bronchopneumonia gives patchy consolidation without cephalization or Kerley B lines.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpulmonaryembolism.png ]
questions.explanation: A filling defect within the pulmonary artery on contrast CT (CTPA) is diagnostic of pulmonary embolism. Aortic pathologies show an intimal flap or aortic dilatation with normally opacified pulmonary arteries.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpleuraleffusion.png ]
questions.explanation: Homogeneous opacity with a meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle indicates pleural effusion. Pneumonia shows air bronchograms without a meniscus, and pneumothorax is radiolucent.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpneumothorax.png ]
questions.explanation: Right-sided pneumothorax with almost complete collapse of the right lung. Mediastinal shift to the left, splayed right ribs and mild right diaphragm depression indicate increased right pleural pressure. A thin white visceral pleural line with no lung markings peripheral to it and a radiolucent pleural space is diagnostic of pneumothorax. Effusion and consolidation produce opacity, and collapse is a volume-loss opacity rather than a lucent air space.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycaorticdissection.png ]
questions.explanation: Contrast CT shows an intimal flap separating a true and a false lumen. An aneurysm is a fusiform dilatation without a flap, and pulmonary embolism gives filling defects in the pulmonary arteries.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyclingularpneumonia.png ]
questions.explanation: Air-space opacity obscuring the left heart border, sitting anterior to the left major fissure on the lateral view, is lingular pneumonia. The left lung has no middle lobe or minor fissure, and left lower lobe pneumonia would obscure the left hemidiaphragm.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycconsolidationxray.png ]
questions.explanation: Right upper lobe consolidation. The air-space opacification has a straight lower border confirming it's right upper lobe location.
questions.note: السؤال اللي كان لدفعة ايريس بحكوا كانت الصورة middle lobe

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycrightupperlobecollapse.png ]
questions.explanation: A triangular right upper zone opacity with an elevated horizontal fissure and elevated right hilum shows volume loss, so it is collapse. Pneumothorax is lucent, effusion shows a meniscus, and consolidation preserves lobar volume and does not displace the fissure.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycleftlowerlobecollapse.png ]
questions.explanation: Triangular density behind the heart. The left hilum is inferiorly displaced. Volume loss in the left hemithorax. Pneumothorax is lucent, effusion shows a meniscus, and consolidation preserves lobar volume.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycsarcoidosis.png ]
questions.explanation: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. No lung infiltrations are shown. No fibrosis. The plain film demonstrates stage 1 sarcoidosis (i.e. bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy).

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding Wilms tumor?
options: It is the most common primary renal malignancy of childhood
It typically presents as a large solid intrarenal mass
It may extend into the renal vein and inferior vena cava
Calcification is seen in only a minority of cases
originalOptions: It is the most common primary renal malignancy of childhood
It typically presents as a large solid intrarenal mass
It may extend into the renal vein and inferior vena cava
Calcification is seen in only a minority of cases
questions.explanation: The lung is the most common site of Wilms metastasis, so calling lung metastases rare is the false statement. Bone metastases are characteristic of neuroblastoma, not Wilms.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding Wilms tumor?
options: It arises from the renal parenchyma
Lung metastases are less common than bone metastases
It may extend into the renal vein and inferior vena cava
It is the most common renal malignancy in children
originalOptions: It arises from the renal parenchyma
Lung metastases are less common than bone metastases
It may extend into the renal vein and inferior vena cava
It is the most common renal malignancy in children
questions.correctAnswer: B) Lung metastases are less common than bone metastases
questions.correctAnswerText: Lung metastases are less common than bone metastases
questions.explanation: Wilms metastasizes mainly to the lung, and bone metastases are uncommon. Frequent bone metastases point to neuroblastoma, the usual distractor.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding this shoulder finding? [img: Radiologymanteriorshoulderdislocation.png ]
options: Anterior shoulder dislocation is the most common type
Caused by forced abduction, external rotation, and extension
Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
Can cause axillary artery or nerve injury
originalOptions: Anterior shoulder dislocation is the most common type
Caused by forced abduction, external rotation, and extension
Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
Can cause axillary artery or nerve injury
questions.correctAnswer: C) Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
questions.correctAnswerText: Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
questions.explanation: In anterior shoulder dislocation, the humeral head is displaced anteriorly and inferiorly (medially), not superiorly, distinguishing it from luxatio erecta (inferior dislocation).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymankylosingspondylitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The spine radiograph shows syndesmophytic fusion (bamboo spine appearance), a hallmark of ankylosing spondylitis rather than the asymmetric joint-space narrowing of OA or RA.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymddh.png ]
questions.explanation: The image shows a shallow acetabulum with a small, laterally decentered femoral epiphysis in a young child, classic for Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) rather than the older-child presentations of Perthes or SCFE.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymnonossifyingfibroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A multiloculated lucent metaphyseal lesion with a sclerotic rim, larger than 3 cm and eccentrically placed near the physis, is a non-ossifying fibroma.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymanteriorshoulderdislocation.png ]
questions.explanation: The humeral head is displaced anteriorly and inferiorly relative to the glenoid, the most common (95%) type of shoulder dislocation.

questions.text: Identify the diagnosis shown in the image: [img: Radiologymmedialmeniscustear.png ]
questions.explanation: Abnormal high T2 signal interrupting the surface of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus indicates a tear at this location.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymfibrousdysplasia.png ]
questions.explanation: A "ground-glass" matrix replacing normal bone architecture on CT is the classic appearance of fibrous dysplasia.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymsupracondylarfracture.png ]
questions.explanation: A fracture line through the distal humeral metaphysis just above the condyles, the most common elbow fracture in children, defines a supracondylar fracture.

questions.text: Identify the diagnosis shown in the image: [img: Radiologymradialheadfracture.png ]
questions.explanation: A fracture line at the radial head with a positive fat pad sign is the most common cause of an adult elbow effusion.

questions.text: In Lesser-trochanter avulsion fracture, which muscle is affected?
questions.explanation: The iliopsoas inserts on the lesser trochanter, making it the muscle responsible for lesser trochanteric avulsion fractures.
questions.note: Mentioned in Coronary Sheet , Slide 32 Anatomy of Pelvis ||| In Endorphin exam , the question was : An avulsion fracture is most likely associated with contraction of which muscle?

questions.text: Identify the Salter-Harris type in this fracture : [img: Radiologymsalter2harris.png ]
questions.explanation: Physeal fracture of the distal tibia. It is a fracture that extends through the growth plate (physis) and down through the epiphysis into the joint space. This specific intra-articular extension through the epiphysis makes it a type III Salter-Harris fracture.

questions.text: Recalled hand radiograph diagnosis. [img: Radiologymrheumatoidarthritis.png ]
questions.explanation: Typical changes of rheumatoid arthritis of the hands with prominent metacarpophalangeal osteopenia, erosions very marked within the carpus and radiocarpal/ulnocarpal joints. DIP sparing.

questions.text: What is the age of the hemorrhage shown on this MRI? [img: Radiologynacutehemorrhage.png ]
questions.explanation: The signal pattern corresponds to deoxyhemoglobin, characteristic of the acute stage (1–3 days), distinguishing it from hyperacute (oxyhemoglobin) and later stages.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynspondylodiscitis.png ]
questions.explanation: Enhancing vertebral endplates with an irregular, destroyed disc space is the classic MRI appearance of spondylodiscitis, unlike degenerative disease (no enhancement) or an isolated epidural abscess (disc usually spared).

questions.text: Which artery supplies the infarcted territory shown in this image? [img: Radiologynacainfarct.png ]
questions.explanation: The infarct involves the medial frontal lobe, the classic ACA distribution, unlike the lateral hemispheric MCA territory or the occipital PCA territory.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmultiplesclerosis.png ]
questions.explanation: Periventricular/callososeptal ovoid lesions oriented perpendicular to the ventricles (Dawson's fingers) are the classic MRI hallmark of MS.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]
questions.explanation: Loss of grey-white differentiation with a "dense cerebellum sign" and sulcal effacement are classic for diffuse cerebral edema.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologynleftsubacutesubduralhemorrhage.png ]
questions.explanation: Huge isodense subdural hematoma causing gross compression to the left hemisphere and midline shift to right.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologynchoroidplexuspapilloma.png ]
questions.explanation: A lobulated, intensely and homogeneously enhancing intraventricular mass with hydrocephalus is characteristic of choroid plexus papilloma, unlike the posterior fossa location of medulloblastoma or the suprasellar cystic/calcified appearance of craniopharyngioma.

questions.text: Identify the diagnosis in the recalled image. [img: Radiologynvestibularschwannoma.png ]
questions.explanation: A cerebellopontine angle mass centered on/expanding the internal auditory canal with heterogeneous signal favors vestibular schwannoma (also known as acoustic neuroma), unlike meningioma, which has a broad dural base and more homogeneous appearance.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmaxillarysinusitis.png ]
questions.explanation: Mucosal thickening with an air-fluid level localized to the maxillary sinus confirms maxillary sinusitis rather than involvement of another sinus or a soft-tissue mass.

questions.text: Regarding posterior cranial fossa tumors in children, which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Ependymomas typically arise from the fourth ventricle
Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant posterior fossa tumor in children
The cystic component of a posterior fossa tumor is never enhanced
Pilocytic astrocytoma often has a cyst with an enhancing mural nodule
originalOptions: Ependymomas typically arise from the fourth ventricle
Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant posterior fossa tumor in children
The cystic component of a posterior fossa tumor is never enhanced
Pilocytic astrocytoma often has a cyst with an enhancing mural nodule
questions.correctAnswer: C) The cystic component of a posterior fossa tumor is never enhanced
questions.correctAnswerText: The cystic component of a posterior fossa tumor is never enhanced
questions.explanation: In pediatric posterior fossa tumors such as pilocytic astrocytoma, the cyst wall or an associated mural nodule commonly DOES enhance, making the "never enhanced" statement false.

questions.text: Regarding posterior cranial fossa tumors in children, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Ependymomas typically show no cystic components
Cystic components in posterior fossa tumors usually enhance with contrast
Ependymomas are located outside the ventricular system
originalOptions: Ependymomas typically show no cystic components
Cystic components in posterior fossa tumors usually enhance with contrast
Ependymomas are located outside the ventricular system
questions.correctAnswer: A) Ependymomas arise from the ventricles
questions.explanation: Ependymomas classically arise from the ependymal lining of the ventricular system (most often the fourth ventricle), unlike the false statement that they are extraventricular.

questions.text: Which brain tumor is characteristically associated with a "butterfly" pattern on imaging?
questions.explanation: GBM classically spreads across the corpus callosum, producing a bilateral, symmetric "butterfly glioma" appearance not typical of the other tumors.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapancreatitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows a diffusely enlarged, edematous pancreas with peripancreatic fat stranding, the classic acute pancreatitis pattern; a discrete mass (adenocarcinoma) is not seen.

questions.text: In this labeled axial CT image, what does structure "3" represent? [img: Radiologyaleftrenalvein.png ]
questions.explanation: In this labeled slice the numbered structures correspond to liver, gallbladder, and left renal vein, consistent with the vein's typical course anterior to the aorta toward the IVC, the characteristic path of the left renal vein (it crosses anterior to the aorta, unlike the renal artery which lies posterior to the vein).
questions.note: 1. Liver || 2. Gallbladder || 3. Left renal vein

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyasigmoidvolvulus.png ]
questions.explanation: The classic "coffee bean" sign, a markedly dilated ahaustral gas-filled loop arising from the pelvis and pointing toward the RUQ, identifies sigmoid volvulus. Cecal volvulus arises in the RLQ with the haustral pattern maintained, and a generic large bowel obstruction lacks the coffee-bean loop.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumobilia.png ]
questions.explanation: The gas is centrally located within the biliary tree near the porta hepatis; portal venous gas classically extends to within 2 cm of the liver capsule (peripheral), which distinguishes it from pneumobilia.

questions.text: What is the name of this radiological sign? [img: Radiologyafootballsign.png ]
questions.explanation: A massive pneumoperitoneum outlines the entire abdominal cavity in an oval, football-like shape on a supine film, which is the football sign (seen especially in neonates/infants).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycheartfailure.png ]
questions.explanation: Cardiomegaly with cephalization, Kerley B lines and interstitial/alveolar edema indicates heart failure. Bilateral bronchopneumonia gives patchy consolidation without cephalization or Kerley B lines.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycrightmiddlelobepneumonia.png ]
questions.explanation: Air-space opacity that obscures the right heart border (silhouette sign) localizes to the right middle lobe. Right lower lobe pneumonia obscures the right hemidiaphragm instead, and collapse would show volume loss.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpulmonaryembolism.png ]
questions.explanation: A filling defect within the pulmonary artery on contrast CT (CTPA) is diagnostic of pulmonary embolism. Aortic pathologies show an intimal flap or aortic dilatation with normally opacified pulmonary arteries.

questions.text: What is WRONG regarding this condition? [img: Radiologycaorticdissection.png ]
options: Blood enters the medial layer through a tear in the intima
It typically occurs in normotensive young patients
CT angiography of the aorta is the investigation of choice
Risk factors include Marfan syndrome, Turner syndrome and pregnancy
originalOptions: Blood enters the medial layer through a tear in the intima
It typically occurs in normotensive young patients
CT angiography of the aorta is the investigation of choice
Risk factors include Marfan syndrome, Turner syndrome and pregnancy
questions.correctAnswer: B) It typically occurs in normotensive young patients
questions.correctAnswerText: It typically occurs in normotensive young patients
questions.explanation: This is Aortic Dissection. Most dissections occur in elderly hypertensive patients. Young patients are affected only with predisposing conditions such as connective tissue disease. The other statements are true.

questions.text: Which of the following is the LEAST likely cause of the pathology seen on this CT? [img: Radiologycconsolidationct.png ]
questions.explanation: Consolidation results from alveoli filled with pus, blood, protein or transudate. Squamous cell carcinoma typically forms a (cavitating) mass or obstructs a bronchus rather than filling alveoli. The alveolar-filling cell tumour that causes consolidation is bronchoalveolar carcinoma.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding this lesion? [img: Radiologymnonossifyingfibroma.png ]
options: Most common benign non-ossifying fibrous lesion of bone
originalOptions: Most common benign non-ossifying fibrous lesion of bone
questions.explanation: Non-ossifying fibroma is a benign fibrous cortical lesion with a sclerotic rim and NO periosteal reaction; a sunburst pattern implies an aggressive process (e.g., osteosarcoma), which contradicts the benign nature of NOF.
questions.note: عندما جاء السؤال لدفعة ايورتا كان مصحوب بصورة ، أما عندما جاء لدفعة ايريس فكان بدون صورة لكن كان بالسؤال : Non-ossifying fibroma

questions.text: What is the name of this bone? [img: Radiologymanatomynavicular.png ]
questions.explanation: The navicular is the medially positioned tarsal bone articulating proximally with the talar head and distally with the cuneiforms, distinguishing it from the more laterally placed cuboid and the proximal talus.

questions.text: Which stage of Salter-Harris fracture is shown? [img: Radiologymsalter3harris.png ]
questions.explanation: The fracture plane runs along the growth plate and extends down through the epiphysis into the joint while sparing the metaphysis — the defining pattern of a Salter-Harris type III injury, which carries a poorer prognosis due to epiphyseal/articular involvement.

questions.text: What is the structure injured in this image? [img: Radiologymquadricepstendon.png ]
questions.explanation: The lesion is at the tendon superior to the patella (quadriceps insertion), consistent with a ruptured quadriceps tendon; the PCL and meniscus are intra-articular structures not visualized in this location.

questions.text: What is the earliest sign of this condition? [img: Radiologymearliestsignofsacroiliitis.png ]
questions.explanation: Sacroiliitis (initial widening followed by erosions and sclerosis of the SI joints) is the earliest manifestation of ankylosing spondylitis; the dagger and bamboo spine signs reflect late-stage spinal ligamentous ossification and fusion.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding this shoulder finding? [img: Radiologymanteriorshoulderdislocation.png ]
options: Anterior shoulder dislocation is the most common type
Caused by forced abduction, external rotation, and extension
Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
Can cause axillary artery or nerve injury
originalOptions: Anterior shoulder dislocation is the most common type
Caused by forced abduction, external rotation, and extension
Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
Can cause axillary artery or nerve injury
questions.correctAnswer: C) Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
questions.correctAnswerText: Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
questions.explanation: In anterior shoulder dislocation, the humeral head is displaced anteriorly and inferiorly (medially), not superiorly, distinguishing it from luxatio erecta (inferior dislocation).

questions.text: What is FALSE about this fracture? [img: Radiologymbucklefracture.png ]
options: Bulging of the cortex from axial loading
Common in the distal radius metaphysis in children
originalOptions: Bulging of the cortex from axial loading
Common in the distal radius metaphysis in children
questions.correctAnswer: A) Complete fracture through the bone
questions.explanation: A buckle (torus) fracture is an incomplete fracture with cortical bulging from axial compression, so describing it as a complete fracture is false.

questions.text: Which structure is consistently HYPERDENSE on a normal, unenhanced brain CT regardless of patient age?
questions.explanation: The lenses are dense on every CT due to their protein content, unlike falx, choroid plexus, pineal, and basal ganglia calcifications, which are age-dependent and inconsistent.

questions.text: Which MRI sequence is shown in this image, where CSF is suppressed (dark) while periventricular lesions remain bright? [img: Radiologynflairsequence.png ]
questions.explanation: FLAIR nulls the CSF signal while preserving T2 hyperintensity of white matter lesions, unlike standard T2 (CSF bright) or T1 (different grey/white contrast).

questions.text: What is the age of the hemorrhage shown on this MRI? [img: Radiologynacutehemorrhage.png ]
questions.explanation: The signal pattern corresponds to deoxyhemoglobin, characteristic of the acute stage (1–3 days), distinguishing it from hyperacute (oxyhemoglobin) and later stages.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a recognized cause of diffuse cerebral edema? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]
questions.explanation: Migraine is not a cause of diffuse cerebral edema; drug overdose, hypertensive emergency (PRES), anoxic injury, and trauma are all recognized causes of diffuse brain swelling.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus?
questions.explanation: A colloid cyst at the foramen of Monro physically obstructs CSF flow (non-communicating hydrocephalus); SAH, meningitis, and meningeal carcinomatosis impair CSF absorption (communicating), and choroid plexus papilloma causes communicating hydrocephalus via CSF overproduction.

questions.text: What is the name of the part of the corpus callosum indicated by the number 5? [img: Radiologynanatomysplenium.png ]
questions.correctAnswer: C) Splenium of the corpus callosum
questions.explanation: The arrow (5) points to the posterior, bulbous portion of the corpus callosum — the splenium — distinct from the genu (anterior) and body (mid-portion).
questions.note: 1. Rostrum || 2. Genu || 3. Body || 4. Isthmus || 5. Splenium

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding craniopharyngioma is FALSE?
options: There is no calcification in the adamantinomatous subtype
The adamantinomatous subtype is more common in children (5–15 years)
The papillary subtype occurs mainly in adults and is usually solid
Calcification is uncommon in the papillary subtype
originalOptions: There is no calcification in the adamantinomatous subtype
The adamantinomatous subtype is more common in children (5–15 years)
The papillary subtype occurs mainly in adults and is usually solid
Calcification is uncommon in the papillary subtype
questions.correctAnswer: A) There is no calcification in the adamantinomatous subtype
questions.correctAnswerText: There is no calcification in the adamantinomatous subtype
questions.explanation: The adamantinomatous subtype shows calcification in ~90% of cases, making this statement false; calcification is instead rare in the adult papillary subtype.

questions.text: This type of edema occurs in all of the following EXCEPT: [img: Radiologynvasogenicedema.png ]
questions.explanation: Vasogenic edema surrounds tumors and abscesses (lymphoma, abscess, GBM) due to blood-brain barrier disruption; ischemic stroke instead produces cytotoxic edema from cellular swelling.

questions.text: Which statement regarding intussusception is incorrect?
options: The prolapsed part is the intussusceptum and the receiving segment the intussuscipiens
The majority occur after 3 week of birth
Invagination of one part of intestine into an adjacent/distal bowel segment
originalOptions: The prolapsed part is the intussusceptum and the receiving segment the intussuscipiens
The majority occur after 3 week of birth
Invagination of one part of intestine into an adjacent/distal bowel segment
questions.correctAnswer: C) The majority occur after 3 week of birth
questions.correctAnswerText: The majority occur after 3 week of birth
questions.explanation: About 95% of intussusceptions occur in children, usually after the first three months of life (after 3 months not 3 weeks). The other statements correctly describe the mechanism, terminology, and ultrasound appearance.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyadiverticulitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows sigmoid diverticula with adjacent pericolic fat stranding and mild bowel wall thickening, the classic appearance of diverticulitis rather than isolated diverticulosis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaportalvenousgas.png ]
questions.explanation: The tiny branching gas foci extend to the peripheral 2 cm of the liver, characteristic of portal venous gas; pneumobilia by contrast is centrally distributed near the porta hepatis.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a typical radiologic feature of appendicitis?
questions.explanation: In acute appendicitis the appendiceal wall is thickened and enhancing, not normal/thin; a normal wall thickness argues against the diagnosis.

questions.text: All are signs of pneumoperitoneum except:
questions.explanation: The bird-beak sign is a feature of achalasia, not pneumoperitoneum; the other four are all recognized radiographic signs of free intraperitoneal air.

questions.text: Which of the following features suggests a malignant breast mass on imaging?
options: Oval shape with posterior acoustic enhancement
Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
Coarse popcorn-like calcification within the mass
originalOptions: Oval shape with posterior acoustic enhancement
Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
Coarse popcorn-like calcification within the mass
questions.correctAnswer: C) Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
questions.correctAnswerText: Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
questions.explanation: Irregular shape and spiculated or indistinct margins are the most suspicious mass features for malignancy. Round or oval circumscribed masses are usually benign (cyst or fibroadenoma). Fat density suggests a lipoma or hamartoma, and popcorn calcification suggests an involuting fibroadenoma.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding BI-RADS?
options: BI-RADS 0 indicates an incomplete assessment that needs additional imaging
BI-RADS 6 indicates the presence of a benign lesion
BI-RADS 3 carries a <2% probability of malignancy
BI-RADS 4 is suspicious, and biopsy should be considered
originalOptions: BI-RADS 0 indicates an incomplete assessment that needs additional imaging
BI-RADS 6 indicates the presence of a benign lesion
BI-RADS 3 carries a <2% probability of malignancy
BI-RADS 4 is suspicious, and biopsy should be considered
questions.correctAnswer: B) BI-RADS 6 indicates the presence of a benign lesion
questions.correctAnswerText: BI-RADS 6 indicates the presence of a benign lesion
questions.explanation: BI-RADS 6 is a known, biopsy-proven malignancy, not a benign lesion. The other statements are correct.

questions.text: What are the standard views of screening mammography?
questions.explanation: The standard views are bilateral CC and MLO. True lateral, spot, magnification, and axillary views are supplementary.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of bronchiectasis?
options: Cylindrical type is the commonest form, with tram-track and signet ring signs
Varicose type shows a beaded appearance
Cystic type shows cyst-like bronchi extending to the pleural surface
Bronchial wall thickening with mucoid impaction
originalOptions: Cylindrical type is the commonest form, with tram-track and signet ring signs
Varicose type shows a beaded appearance
Cystic type shows cyst-like bronchi extending to the pleural surface
Bronchial wall thickening with mucoid impaction
questions.correctAnswer: C) Reversible dilatation of the bronchi
questions.explanation: Bronchiectasis is irreversible, permanent dilatation of the bronchial tree. The other options describe its subtypes and associated findings.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpleuraleffusion.png ]
questions.explanation: Homogeneous opacity with a meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle indicates pleural effusion. Pneumonia shows air bronchograms without a meniscus, and pneumothorax is radiolucent.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT seen in heart failure on chest radiography?
questions.explanation: Heart failure typically causes cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio >50%), not a small heart. Edema, effusion, cephalization and Kerley B lines are all typical.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of lung collapse?
options: Mediastinal shift toward the affected side
Displacement of the fissures toward the collapsed lobe
Triangular opacity with its apex pointing to the hilum
originalOptions: Mediastinal shift toward the affected side
Displacement of the fissures toward the collapsed lobe
Triangular opacity with its apex pointing to the hilum
questions.explanation: Loss of lung volume is the cardinal feature of collapse. Preserved volume points to consolidation instead.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycaorticdissection.png ]
questions.explanation: Contrast CT shows an intimal flap separating a true and a false lumen. An aneurysm is a fusiform dilatation without a flap, and pulmonary embolism gives filling defects in the pulmonary arteries.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycconsolidationct.png ]
questions.explanation: Air-space opacification with air bronchograms and preserved lung volume is consolidation. Atelectasis shows volume loss, and effusion shows a meniscus without air bronchograms.

questions.text: Which is NOT a feature of a simple bone cyst?
questions.explanation: Unicameral (simple) bone cysts are centrally located within the metaphysis of long bones, not peripheral; they are otherwise well-defined, radiolucent, benign lesions with a narrow zone of transition.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteochondroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A bony projection with cortical and medullary continuity with the parent bone, arising from the metaphysis and pointing away from the joint, is characteristic of osteochondroma (cartilage-capped exostosis).

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT typically involved in non-traumatic fractures of child abuse?
questions.explanation: Parietal bone fractures are low-specificity findings often due to accidental trauma, whereas metaphyseal corner, posterior rib, and scapular fractures are pathognomonic or highly specific for non-accidental injury.

questions.text: What is the name of the labelled tarsal bone? [img: Radiologymanatomycuboid.png ]
questions.explanation: The cuboid is the laterally positioned tarsal bone articulating with the calcaneus proximally and the 4th/5th metatarsals distally, distinguishing it from the medially located navicular and cuneiforms.

questions.text: Hyperparathyroidism causes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hyperparathyroidism causes bone resorption and osteopenia, not increased bone mass; osteosclerosis is not a feature of this disease.

questions.text: Which statement regarding cerebral venous sinus thrombosis is CORRECT?
options: The cavernous sinus is the most common site
Both cytotoxic and vasogenic edema can be seen
Sinus thrombosis does not cause hemorrhage
The vein of Labbé drains into the superior sagittal sinus
originalOptions: The cavernous sinus is the most common site
Both cytotoxic and vasogenic edema can be seen
Sinus thrombosis does not cause hemorrhage
The vein of Labbé drains into the superior sagittal sinus
questions.correctAnswer: B) Both cytotoxic and vasogenic edema can be seen
questions.correctAnswerText: Both cytotoxic and vasogenic edema can be seen
questions.explanation: Raised venous pressure first causes vasogenic edema, progressing to cytotoxic edema if venous infarction occurs. The superior sagittal sinus (not cavernous) is the most common site, hemorrhage is common, and the vein of Labbé drains into the transverse sinus.

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT show restricted diffusion on MRI (DWI)?
questions.explanation: Lymphoma, abscess, epidermoid cyst, and acute ischemia characteristically restrict diffusion; acute hemorrhage's DWI signal is variable and not a classic cause of true restricted diffusion.

questions.text: A brain MRI lesion is isointense on T1 and hyperintense on T2. What stage of hemorrhage is most likely?
questions.explanation: Intracellular oxyhemoglobin in the hyperacute stage is T1 isointense and T2 hyperintense; acute (deoxyhemoglobin) blood is instead T2 hypointense.

questions.text: Which basal-ganglia blood-supply statement is INCORRECT?
options: The anterior limb of the internal capsule is supplied by the choroidal artery
The caudate is supplied by the medial lenticulostriate artery
The putamen and globus pallidus are supplied by the lateral lenticulostriate artery
The thalamus is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery
originalOptions: The anterior limb of the internal capsule is supplied by the choroidal artery
The caudate is supplied by the medial lenticulostriate artery
The putamen and globus pallidus are supplied by the lateral lenticulostriate artery
The thalamus is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery
questions.correctAnswer: A) The anterior limb of the internal capsule is supplied by the choroidal artery
questions.correctAnswerText: The anterior limb of the internal capsule is supplied by the choroidal artery
questions.explanation: The anterior limb of the internal capsule is supplied by the medial lenticulostriate arteries and the recurrent artery of Heubner; the anterior choroidal artery instead supplies the posterior limb/retrolentiform region.

questions.text: Identify the labeled structure. [img: Radiologynanatomyuncusbrain.png ]
options: Anterior Horn of the Lateral Ventricle
originalOptions: Anterior Horn of the Lateral Ventricle
questions.explanation: I don't know what to write; there's no explanation :)

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapancreatitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows a diffusely enlarged, edematous pancreas with peripancreatic fat stranding, the classic acute pancreatitis pattern; a discrete mass (adenocarcinoma) is not seen.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a typical radiological feature of achalasia?
options: Bird-beak appearance at the gastroesophageal junction
Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
originalOptions: Bird-beak appearance at the gastroesophageal junction
Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
questions.explanation: The dilated, food- and fluid-filled esophagus produces mediastinal widening (a convex opacity overlapping the right mediastinum), so narrowing is the false feature. The other options are recognized findings.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about radiologic imaging is incorrect?
options: Female ovarian assessment requires an empty urinary bladder
Ultrasound is effective for evaluating the biliary and urinary systems
Single contrast enema uses only barium without air
Free intraperitoneal air can be seen under the diaphragm on an erect chest X-ray
originalOptions: Female ovarian assessment requires an empty urinary bladder
Ultrasound is effective for evaluating the biliary and urinary systems
Single contrast enema uses only barium without air
Free intraperitoneal air can be seen under the diaphragm on an erect chest X-ray
questions.correctAnswer: A) Female ovarian assessment requires an empty urinary bladder
questions.correctAnswerText: Female ovarian assessment requires an empty urinary bladder
questions.explanation: Transabdominal pelvic/ovarian ultrasound requires a FULL bladder as an acoustic window, not an empty one; the other statements are correct.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaachalasia.png ]
questions.explanation: The barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering smoothly to a "bird-beak" narrowing at the gastroesophageal junction, the classic finding of achalasia.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyasmallbowelobstruction.png ]
questions.explanation: The supine film shows multiple centrally located dilated loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full lumen width, typical of small (not large) bowel obstruction.

questions.text: Which artery is most likely shown? [img: Radiologyasuperiormesentericartery.png ]
questions.explanation: The arrow points to a single anterior aortic branch arising at approximately the L1 level, just below the celiac trunk, the typical origin of the SMA.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyagallstonexray.png ]
questions.explanation: The abdominal x-ray shows rounded, faintly calcified opacities in the right upper quadrant overlying the expected gallbladder location, consistent with radiopaque gallstones.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a typical radiologic feature of acute pancreatitis?
questions.correctAnswer: B) Smooth outline of the pancreas
questions.explanation: Acute pancreatitis causes irregular, fuzzy pancreatic borders due to inflammation and edema, not a smooth outline.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding abdominal vasculature is false?
options: Renal arteries are paired vessels that arise superior to the gonadal arteries
The IVC passes through the diaphragm at the T8 level
The hindgut is supplied by the superior mesenteric artery
The IVC has a retroperitoneal course within the abdomen
originalOptions: Renal arteries are paired vessels that arise superior to the gonadal arteries
The IVC passes through the diaphragm at the T8 level
The hindgut is supplied by the superior mesenteric artery
The IVC has a retroperitoneal course within the abdomen
questions.correctAnswer: C) The hindgut is supplied by the superior mesenteric artery
questions.correctAnswerText: The hindgut is supplied by the superior mesenteric artery
questions.explanation: The hindgut is supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery, not the SMA (which supplies the midgut); the other statements are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about pneumobilia is false?
options: Pneumobilia refers to the presence of gas in the biliary tree
Most commonly seen after endoscopic procedures
originalOptions: Pneumobilia refers to the presence of gas in the biliary tree
Most commonly seen after endoscopic procedures
questions.correctAnswer: D) It appears peripherally on CT
questions.explanation: Pneumobilia is centrally distributed near the porta hepatis on CT; it is portal venous gas that characteristically extends peripherally to the liver capsule.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about hiatal hernias is false?
options: Rolling hernias are more common than sliding hernias
Sliding hernias are often associated with gastroesophageal reflux
Rolling hernias increase the risk of volvulus
In sliding hernias, the gastroesophageal junction moves above the diaphragm
originalOptions: Rolling hernias are more common than sliding hernias
Sliding hernias are often associated with gastroesophageal reflux
Rolling hernias increase the risk of volvulus
In sliding hernias, the gastroesophageal junction moves above the diaphragm
questions.correctAnswer: A) Rolling hernias are more common than sliding hernias
questions.correctAnswerText: Rolling hernias are more common than sliding hernias
questions.explanation: Sliding hernias account for over 90% of cases and are far more common than rolling (paraesophageal) hernias, making this statement false.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about CT findings in acute appendicitis is false?
options: Dilated appendix with a distended lumen (> 6 mm)
An appendicolith is always present, and its absence excludes the diagnosis
originalOptions: Dilated appendix with a distended lumen (> 6 mm)
An appendicolith is always present, and its absence excludes the diagnosis
questions.correctAnswer: B) An appendicolith is always present, and its absence excludes the diagnosis
questions.correctAnswerText: An appendicolith is always present, and its absence excludes the diagnosis
questions.explanation: An appendicolith may be identified in some cases but is not required, so its absence does not exclude appendicitis. A dilated lumen, thickened enhancing wall, cecal apex thickening, and fat stranding are the recognized CT findings.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the small intestine is incorrect?
options: Jejunum shows more prominent folds than ileum
Valvulae conniventes span the entire lumen of the small intestine
Functional ileus can present with a discrete transition point
originalOptions: Jejunum shows more prominent folds than ileum
Valvulae conniventes span the entire lumen of the small intestine
Functional ileus can present with a discrete transition point
questions.correctAnswer: C) Functional ileus can present with a discrete transition point
questions.correctAnswerText: Functional ileus can present with a discrete transition point
questions.explanation: Functional (adynamic) ileus shows diffuse bowel dilatation without a discrete transition point, unlike mechanical obstruction; a discrete transition point argues against ileus.

questions.text: What is the best first imaging modality for a pregnant patient with a palpable breast lump?
questions.explanation: Ultrasound uses no ionizing radiation and is the modality of choice for symptomatic pregnant or young (<30 years) patients. It also distinguishes cystic from solid lesions and can guide biopsy. Mammography and CT use radiation, and MRI needs gadolinium, so none of them is first-line.

questions.text: Which of the following features suggests a malignant breast mass on imaging?
options: Oval shape with posterior acoustic enhancement
Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
Coarse popcorn-like calcification within the mass
originalOptions: Oval shape with posterior acoustic enhancement
Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
Coarse popcorn-like calcification within the mass
questions.correctAnswer: C) Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
questions.correctAnswerText: Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
questions.explanation: Irregular shape and spiculated or indistinct margins are the most suspicious mass features for malignancy. Round or oval circumscribed masses are usually benign (cyst or fibroadenoma). Fat density suggests a lipoma or hamartoma, and popcorn calcification suggests an involuting fibroadenoma.

questions.text: A palpable mass is located at the 5 o'clock position in the right breast. Which quadrant is this?
questions.explanation: In the right breast, 9 o'clock is lateral, so 3–6 o'clock is the lower inner quadrant and 6–9 is the lower outer. The 5 o'clock position therefore lies in the lower inner quadrant.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about mammography is FALSE?
options: Axillary lymph nodes with central lucency may be benign
Sensitivity of mammography is reduced in dense breasts
Dense breast tissue in young women requires further evaluation

Spiculated masses are suspicious for malignancy
questions.explanation: Fine pleomorphic calcifications are a suspicious morphology. The typically benign types are skin, vascular, popcorn, rod-like, round or punctate, rim, and milk of calcium.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpleuraleffusion.png ]

The PA view is the best general technique for the lungs, mediastinum and great vessels

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpneumothorax.png ]

questions.explanation: CTPA (which utilizes intravenous contrast) directly shows filling defects in the pulmonary arteries, and the chest X-ray is often normal. V/Q scan is only an alternative when contrast is contraindicated.

questions.text: All of the following are seen in heart failure EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Heart failure causes pulmonary edema, cardiomegaly, effusions and Kerley B lines. Pneumothorax is not part of it.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycthoracicaorticaneurysm.jpg ]

questions.text: Which of the following statements about air bronchograms is FALSE?

They are typical in lung collapse
They represent patent airways outlined by air within opacified lung
