questions.explanation: Lobar collapse results from luminal obstruction (foreign body, mucus plug), mural lesions (carcinoma) or extrinsic compression. Bullous emphysema does not obstruct the supplying bronchus.

questions.text: Which of the following is hyperdense on CT scan?
questions.explanation: Iodinated contrast is markedly hyperdense on CT. Fluid, fat, chronic blood, and air are iso- to hypodense.

questions.text: Regarding MRI, which of the following is FALSE?
options: Its image resolution is higher than that of ultrasound
It is a cross-sectional imaging modality
Contrast allergy is a relative contraindication for contrasted images
The quality of MRI images is lower in the chest region than in the brain region
originalOptions: Its image resolution is higher than that of ultrasound
It is a cross-sectional imaging modality
Contrast allergy is a relative contraindication for contrasted images
The quality of MRI images is lower in the chest region than in the brain region
questions.explanation: MRI uses a strong magnet and radiofrequency waves, with no ionizing radiation. Radiographs and CT are the modalities that use it.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about Pediatric MSK?
options: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a collagen type II disease
Rachitic rosary occurs at the posterior rib end
In SCFE the femoral head slips anteriorly and laterally
DDH shows a shallow acetabulum with cephalic subluxation or dislocation of the femoral head
In Perthes disease the femoral head is small and lucent
originalOptions: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a collagen type II disease
Rachitic rosary occurs at the posterior rib end
In SCFE the femoral head slips anteriorly and laterally
DDH shows a shallow acetabulum with cephalic subluxation or dislocation of the femoral head
In Perthes disease the femoral head is small and lucent
questions.correctAnswer: D) DDH shows a shallow acetabulum with cephalic subluxation or dislocation of the femoral head
questions.correctAnswerText: DDH shows a shallow acetabulum with cephalic subluxation or dislocation of the femoral head
questions.explanation: This accurately describes the acetabular dysplasia and superior femoral head displacement seen in DDH; OI is actually a type I collagen defect, and in Perthes the femoral head is sclerotic (not lucent).

questions.text: What is the most common type of Salter-Harris fracture?
questions.explanation: Salter-Harris type II accounts for approximately 75% of physeal fractures, making it by far the most common subtype.

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT occur in the metaphysis in a skeletally mature individual?
questions.explanation: Giant cell tumor of bone classically occurs in the epiphysis extending to the subchondral bone in skeletally mature patients, unlike the other listed metaphyseal lesions.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT seen in ankylosing spondylitis?
questions.explanation: Ankylosing spondylitis produces enthesophytes, syndesmophytes, ligament ossification, and dural ectasia; spinal canal stenosis is not a classic direct radiologic feature of this disease.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about arthritis?
options: In septic arthritis, post-contrast fat-saturated T1 shows synovial thickening
Syndesmophytes run perpendicular to the spine
In osteoarthritis, sclerosis occurs with severe osteopenia
In rheumatoid arthritis, marginal erosions occur at the medial aspect of the MCP joints
Joint space and bone density are normal in septic arthritis
originalOptions: In septic arthritis, post-contrast fat-saturated T1 shows synovial thickening
Syndesmophytes run perpendicular to the spine
In osteoarthritis, sclerosis occurs with severe osteopenia
In rheumatoid arthritis, marginal erosions occur at the medial aspect of the MCP joints
Joint space and bone density are normal in septic arthritis
questions.correctAnswer: A) In septic arthritis, post-contrast fat-saturated T1 shows synovial thickening
questions.correctAnswerText: In septic arthritis, post-contrast fat-saturated T1 shows synovial thickening
questions.explanation: MRI in septic arthritis shows synovial thickening on post-contrast fat-saturated T1; syndesmophytes actually run parallel (not perpendicular) to the spine, and RA erosions occur at the radial (not medial) MCP aspect.

questions.text: Regarding avulsion fractures, which of the following is TRUE?
questions.explanation: The adductor muscle group originates from the pubic symphysis/pubic rami, making this the correct pairing; hamstrings actually attach at the ischial tuberosity and rectus femoris at the AIIS.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about aneurysmal bone cyst?
options: Metaphyseal location with multiple fluid-fluid level cysts
Solid periosteal reaction is always present
Occurs almost exclusively in elderly patients
originalOptions: Metaphyseal location with multiple fluid-fluid level cysts
Solid periosteal reaction is always present
Occurs almost exclusively in elderly patients
questions.correctAnswer: B) Metaphyseal location with multiple fluid-fluid level cysts
questions.correctAnswerText: Metaphyseal location with multiple fluid-fluid level cysts
questions.explanation: ABC is an eccentric expansile metaphyseal lesion showing multiple blood-filled cystic spaces with fluid-fluid levels from layering blood products of different ages.

questions.text: All of the following can present in neurofibromatosis type 2, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Multiple cutaneous/subcutaneous neurofibromas are a hallmark of NF1, not NF2; NF2 instead features bilateral vestibular schwannomas, meningiomas, and intramedullary ependymomas.

questions.text: Which of the following is a white matter structure?
questions.explanation: The corona radiata is composed of white matter projection fibers; the others are all grey matter structures.

questions.text: All of the following are true about schizencephaly, EXCEPT:
options: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
It can be unilateral or bilateral
Open-lip schizencephaly presents with more symptoms than closed-lip
There is pial communication in closed-lip schizencephaly
originalOptions: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
It can be unilateral or bilateral
Open-lip schizencephaly presents with more symptoms than closed-lip
There is pial communication in closed-lip schizencephaly
questions.correctAnswer: A) It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
questions.correctAnswerText: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
questions.explanation: Schizencephaly clefts are actually lined by grey matter (heterotopic cortex), not white matter. Laterality, symptom severity, and the presence of pial-ependymal communication in both types are all accurate characteristics of the condition.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: All of the following are intramedullary lesions, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Schwannoma is an intradural extramedullary tumor arising from a nerve root sheath, unlike astrocytoma, ependymoma, hemangioblastoma, and ganglioglioma, which are intramedullary.

questions.text: All of the following appear hyperintense on T2 MRI, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Air produces a signal void and appears hypointense on all MRI sequences, unlike fatty marrow, late subacute hematoma, choroid plexus papilloma, and GBM, which are typically T2 hyperintense.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT found in hyperacute brain ischemia?
options: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
originalOptions: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.correctAnswer: E) Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.correctAnswerText: Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.explanation: These are late/chronic infarct changes (>3 weeks); the hyperacute stage (0–6 hours) instead shows subtle grey-white loss, cortical hypodensity, gyral effacement, and loss of the insular ribbon sign.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the parietal bones with the occipital bone?
questions.explanation: The lambdoid suture joins both parietal bones with the occipital bone posteriorly; coronal joins frontal to parietal, sagittal joins the two parietals, and metopic joins the two frontal bones.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the frontal and parietal bones?
questions.explanation: The coronal suture joins the frontal and parietal bones, distinct from the squamosal suture which joins the temporal and parietal bones, the metopic suture which joins the two frontal bones, the sagittal suture which joins the two parietal bones, and the lambdoid suture which joins the occipital and parietal bones.

questions.text: Regarding abdominal calcifications, which one of the following is TRUE?
options: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Bilateral adrenal calcifications seen at the level of L5 usually
Eighty five percent of gall bladder stones seen on CT Scan
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
originalOptions: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Bilateral adrenal calcifications seen at the level of L5 usually
Eighty five percent of gall bladder stones seen on CT Scan
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
questions.correctAnswer: D) Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
questions.correctAnswerText: Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
questions.explanation: Approximately 85% of urinary/renal stones are radio-opaque and visible on plain radiograph (X-ray); phleboliths are small venous (not arterial) calcifications, and adrenal glands lie much higher than L5.

questions.text: Regarding Free air in the abdomen, which of following is TRUE?
options: History of abdominal surgery within one month is an indication of pneumoperitoneum
The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
originalOptions: History of abdominal surgery within one month is an indication of pneumoperitoneum
The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
questions.correctAnswer: E) Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
questions.correctAnswerText: Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
questions.explanation: An erect chest film is the most sensitive plain radiograph for detecting free subdiaphragmatic gas; the falciform ligament sign actually supports (not lowers) the diagnosis, and portal venous gas is peripheral, not central.

questions.text: Regarding bowel obstruction, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Sigmoid volvulus usually extends to the left upper quadrant
Two air fluid levels of 3 cm width each apply the definition of obstruction
originalOptions: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Sigmoid volvulus usually extends to the left upper quadrant
Two air fluid levels of 3 cm width each apply the definition of obstruction
questions.correctAnswer: A) Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
questions.correctAnswerText: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
questions.explanation: The "3-6-9 rule" sets the large bowel dilatation threshold at 6 cm, so 8 cm exceeds this; the cecal threshold is actually 9 cm, and adhesions (not hernia) are the overall most common cause of small bowel obstruction.

questions.text: Regarding abdomen anatomy, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of the pancreas
The right adrenal gland lies more superiorly than the left adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The third part of the duodenum passes between liver and pancreas
The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
originalOptions: The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of the pancreas
The right adrenal gland lies more superiorly than the left adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The third part of the duodenum passes between liver and pancreas
The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
questions.correctAnswer: E) The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
questions.correctAnswerText: The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
questions.explanation: The IMA arises from the anterior aorta at the level of L3. The portal vein forms posterior (not anterior) to the pancreatic neck, the left (not right) adrenal gland sits more superiorly, and the left (not right) renal vein is the longer vessel.

questions.text: All of the following can cause lobar collapse EXCEPT:
options: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
originalOptions: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.correctAnswer: E) Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.correctAnswerText: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.explanation: Lobar collapse results from luminal obstruction (foreign body, mucus plug), mural lesions (carcinoma) or extrinsic compression. Bullous emphysema does not obstruct the supplying bronchus.

questions.text: An infant is suspected of having left-sided foreign body aspiration. Which of the following chest views is NOT helpful?
questions.explanation: With a check-valve obstruction, the affected lung fails to deflate on expiration or when the affected side is dependent (left lateral decubitus). A right lateral decubitus view gives no additional information for a left-sided foreign body.

questions.text: Regarding the pathology seen on the provided image, which of the following is TRUE? [img: Radiologyclobarconsolidation.png ]
options: Mediastinal shift to the same side aids the diagnosis of consolidation
The presence of air bronchograms aids the diagnosis of collapse
Lobar consolidation is usually bordered by a lung fissure
Clear outline of adjacent structures aids the diagnosis of pleural fluid
Volume loss of the affected lobe is the hallmark of consolidation
originalOptions: Mediastinal shift to the same side aids the diagnosis of consolidation
The presence of air bronchograms aids the diagnosis of collapse
Lobar consolidation is usually bordered by a lung fissure
Clear outline of adjacent structures aids the diagnosis of pleural fluid
Volume loss of the affected lobe is the hallmark of consolidation
questions.correctAnswer: C) Lobar consolidation is usually bordered by a lung fissure
questions.correctAnswerText: Lobar consolidation is usually bordered by a lung fissure
questions.explanation: Lobar consolidation is sharply demarcated by the fissure. Shift toward the lesion and volume loss suggest collapse, and effusion obscures adjacent structures.

questions.text: Regarding the provided image, what is the best management for the pathology seen? [img: Radiologycpneumoniamanagement.png ]
questions.explanation: The image shows consolidation from bacterial pneumonia, which is treated with antibiotics. A chest tube is for pneumothorax or empyema, and diuretics are for pulmonary edema in heart failure.

questions.text: Regarding pneumothorax, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Mediastinal shift to the left is usually associated with left tension pneumothorax
Cavitary neoplasms are the usual cause of primary pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
Primary spontaneous pneumothorax typically occurs in short elderly women
originalOptions: Mediastinal shift to the left is usually associated with left tension pneumothorax
Cavitary neoplasms are the usual cause of primary pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
Primary spontaneous pneumothorax typically occurs in short elderly women
questions.correctAnswer: D) The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
questions.correctAnswerText: The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
questions.explanation: Air collects anteriorly and superiorly, so the tube is placed there. Laceration causes an ipsilateral pneumothorax, tension pushes the mediastinum away, and primary spontaneous pneumothorax affects tall young patients.

questions.text: Regarding the ALARA principle, which of the following is FALSE?
options: It is an abbreviation for "As Low As Reasonably Achievable"
It aims to achieve the best diagnostic result at the lowest reasonable radiation dose
It ensures the use of large radiation doses to achieve better diagnostic results
Commitment to it lowers radiation-induced physical harm to patients
There is a consensus between clinicians and radiologists to apply it
originalOptions: It is an abbreviation for "As Low As Reasonably Achievable"
It aims to achieve the best diagnostic result at the lowest reasonable radiation dose
It ensures the use of large radiation doses to achieve better diagnostic results
Commitment to it lowers radiation-induced physical harm to patients
There is a consensus between clinicians and radiologists to apply it
questions.correctAnswer: C) It ensures the use of large radiation doses to achieve better diagnostic results
questions.correctAnswerText: It ensures the use of large radiation doses to achieve better diagnostic results
questions.explanation: ALARA means keeping the dose as low as reasonably achievable while preserving diagnostic quality, the opposite of using large doses.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: Regarding MRI, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Cost of imaging is one of its limitations
Metallic foreign bodies are safe if small in size
It is the first diagnostic modality used for assessing pelvic fractures
The signal of a material depends on its helium atom content
originalOptions: Cost of imaging is one of its limitations
Metallic foreign bodies are safe if small in size
It is the first diagnostic modality used for assessing pelvic fractures
The signal of a material depends on its helium atom content
questions.correctAnswer: A) Cost of imaging is one of its limitations
questions.correctAnswerText: Cost of imaging is one of its limitations
questions.explanation: MRI is more expensive than CT and takes longer to acquire. Pacemakers and metal implants are contraindications, and MRI signal depends on hydrogen, not helium. Fractures are assessed first with radiographs or CT.

questions.text: All of the following statements are FALSE EXCEPT:
options: CT iodine-based contrast is safely used in patients with advanced renal failure
The radiation exposure dose is measured in milliamperes
PACS is the system used for archiving and communication in the radiology department
Ionizing radiation is safer than non-ionizing radiation
originalOptions: CT iodine-based contrast is safely used in patients with advanced renal failure
The radiation exposure dose is measured in milliamperes
PACS is the system used for archiving and communication in the radiology department
Ionizing radiation is safer than non-ionizing radiation
questions.correctAnswer: D) PACS is the system used for archiving and communication in the radiology department
questions.correctAnswerText: PACS is the system used for archiving and communication in the radiology department
questions.explanation: PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) stores and transmits images, so it is the only true statement. Iodinated contrast risks renal injury, and non-ionizing modalities are safer than ionizing ones.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: Regarding CT scan, which of the following is FALSE?
options: The quality of CT images is lower in bone-containing body parts
It is a cross-sectional imaging modality
Thyroid disease is a relative contraindication for contrasted images
Its image resolution is higher than that of ultrasound
originalOptions: The quality of CT images is lower in bone-containing body parts
It is a cross-sectional imaging modality
Thyroid disease is a relative contraindication for contrasted images
Its image resolution is higher than that of ultrasound
questions.correctAnswer: B) The quality of CT images is lower in bone-containing body parts
questions.correctAnswerText: The quality of CT images is lower in bone-containing body parts
questions.explanation: CT is the best modality for bone, so image quality is not lower in bone-containing regions. Iodinated contrast can induce thyrotoxicosis, which makes thyroid disease a relative contraindication.

questions.text: The demonstration of an abnormal fat pad in an adult suggests which of the following?
questions.explanation: The most common cause of an elbow fat pad sign (joint effusion) in adults is a radial head fracture, whereas supracondylar fracture is the classic pediatric cause.

questions.text: What is the most common type of Salter-Harris fracture?
questions.explanation: Salter-Harris type II accounts for approximately 75% of physeal fractures, making it by far the most common subtype.

questions.text: Punched-out erosion with sclerotic margins is a typical radiological finding in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Well-defined "punched-out" erosions with sclerotic, overhanging margins are pathognomonic for gout, unlike the ill-defined marginal erosions of RA.

questions.text: Regarding non-accidental trauma, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Epiphyseal corner fracture is highly specific for child abuse
Extradural hematoma is one of the most common brain findings
Infants are at greatest risk of abuse
Anterior rib fracture is highly specific for child abuse
Skeletal survey is not recommended in cases of suspected child abuse
originalOptions: Epiphyseal corner fracture is highly specific for child abuse
Extradural hematoma is one of the most common brain findings
Infants are at greatest risk of abuse
Anterior rib fracture is highly specific for child abuse
Skeletal survey is not recommended in cases of suspected child abuse
questions.correctAnswer: C) Infants are at greatest risk of abuse
questions.correctAnswerText: Infants are at greatest risk of abuse
questions.explanation: Non-ambulatory infants are at highest risk of NAI; note that it is the metaphyseal (not epiphyseal) corner fracture and posterior (not anterior) rib fractures that are highly specific.

questions.text: Regarding ankylosing spondylitis, which of the following is FALSE?
options: Sacroiliitis is a late radiological manifestation
It is a disease of young adults
Interspinous ligament ossification gives a "dagger spine" appearance
originalOptions: Sacroiliitis is a late radiological manifestation
It is a disease of young adults
Interspinous ligament ossification gives a "dagger spine" appearance
questions.correctAnswer: A) Sacroiliitis is a late radiological manifestation
questions.correctAnswerText: Sacroiliitis is a late radiological manifestation
questions.explanation: Sacroiliitis is typically the FIRST radiological manifestation of ankylosing spondylitis, not a late one.

questions.text: Which of the following is the earliest radiological finding in rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.explanation: Fusiform periarticular soft tissue swelling (from effusion/tenosynovitis) can be the earliest or only radiographic finding in RA, preceding visible marginal erosions.

questions.text: Regarding osteosarcoma, which of the following is FALSE?
options: Primary osteosarcoma typically occurs in young patients
Secondary osteosarcoma occurs in the elderly
Commonly associated with an aggressive periosteal reaction
originalOptions: Primary osteosarcoma typically occurs in young patients
Secondary osteosarcoma occurs in the elderly
Commonly associated with an aggressive periosteal reaction
questions.correctAnswer: B) Typically occurs in the epiphysis
questions.explanation: Osteosarcoma most commonly arises in the metadiaphysis/metaphysis around the knee, not the epiphysis, making this statement false.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a recognized cause of diffuse cerebral edema? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]
questions.explanation: Migraine is not a cause of diffuse cerebral edema; drug overdose, hypertensive emergency (PRES), anoxic injury, and trauma are all recognized causes of diffuse brain swelling.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus?
questions.explanation: A colloid cyst at the foramen of Monro physically obstructs CSF flow (non-communicating hydrocephalus); SAH, meningitis, and meningeal carcinomatosis impair CSF absorption (communicating), and choroid plexus papilloma causes communicating hydrocephalus via CSF overproduction.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the two parietal bones?
questions.explanation: The sagittal suture runs in the midline joining the two parietal bones to each other.

questions.text: Regarding cerebral sinus thrombosis, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Sinus thrombosis is an occlusion of arterial channels in the cranial cavity
The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
The dura typically does not enhance
A hypodense sinus is seen on non-contrast CT
originalOptions: Sinus thrombosis is an occlusion of arterial channels in the cranial cavity
The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
The dura typically does not enhance
A hypodense sinus is seen on non-contrast CT
questions.correctAnswer: C) The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
questions.correctAnswerText: The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
questions.explanation: The empty delta sign — a triangular filling defect surrounded by enhancing dura — is classically seen on contrast-enhanced imaging; sinus thrombosis is a venous (not arterial) occlusion, acute thrombus typically does NOT enhance, the dura DOES enhance, and non-contrast CT shows a hyperdense (not hypodense) sinus.

questions.text: Regarding subdural hematoma, which of the following is TRUE?
options: It does not cross the falx cerebri
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
originalOptions: It does not cross the falx cerebri
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
questions.correctAnswer: A) It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.correctAnswerText: It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.explanation: Subdural hematoma is confined by the falx cerebri and tentorium but CAN cross suture lines (opposite epidural hematoma); it is typically caused by bridging vein tears (not the middle meningeal artery) and has a crescentic (not lenticular) shape.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumobilia.png ]
questions.explanation: The gas is centrally located within the biliary tree near the porta hepatis; portal venous gas classically extends to within 2 cm of the liver capsule (peripheral), which distinguishes it from pneumobilia.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumoperitoneum.png ]
questions.explanation: Free intraperitoneal air is seen outlining the bowel loops and under the diaphragm, diagnostic of pneumoperitoneum rather than a fluid- or obstruction-related process.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyahydronephrosis.png ]
questions.explanation: The coronal CT shows dilatation of the left renal collecting system (pelvicalyceal dilation) without a discrete simple fluid collection, consistent with hydronephrosis rather than an isolated stone or cyst.

questions.text: Not true about achalasia?
options: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
originalOptions: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.correctAnswer: D) Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.correctAnswerText: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.explanation: Anterior tracheal displacement/bowing from the dilated esophagus is a lateral-view finding, not a frontal-view finding, making this statement false.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaappendicitisus.jpg ]
questions.explanation: The imaging (Ultrasound) shows a dilated, non-compressible appendix with periappendiceal fluid/fat stranding ± appendicolith, the classic combination for acute appendicitis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaleftrenalstone.png ]
questions.explanation: A well-defined, rounded radiopaque calcification overlying the renal shadow on KUB is most consistent with a renal calculus rather than a pelvic phlebolith or lymph node calcification.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaureterstone.png ]
questions.explanation: The calcification lies along the expected course of the ureter (from renal pelvis to bladder), distinguishing it from a phlebolith, which sits in the pelvis away from this line.

questions.text: Which imaging modality and plane is shown in this image? [img: Radiologyacoronalctabdomen.png ]
questions.correctAnswer: B) Coronal CT abdomen with contrast
questions.explanation: The image demonstrates the liver, kidneys, and spine in a coronal (frontal) cross-sectional plane typical of coronal reformatted contrast-enhanced CT.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyamidgutvolvulus.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows the classic whirlpool sign of the superior mesenteric vessels and mesentery twisting around each other, diagnostic of midgut volvulus (from malrotation).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyagallstoneus.png ]
questions.explanation: Ultrasound shows a hyperechoic intraluminal focus with posterior acoustic shadowing within the gallbladder, the classic appearance of a gallstone.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaachalasia.png ]
questions.explanation: The barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering smoothly to a "bird-beak" narrowing at the gastroesophageal junction, the classic finding of achalasia.

questions.text: Which of the following is false regarding achalasia?
options: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
originalOptions: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
questions.explanation: Achalasia produces marked esophageal dilatation, not a normal-caliber esophagus, making this the false statement.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyagastriccancer.png ]
questions.explanation: The barium meal shows an irregular, ulcerated mass with abnormal mucosal folds, a pattern typical of malignant gastric ulceration rather than a benign ulcer.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapcos.png ]
questions.explanation: Transvaginal ultrasound in this recalled station shows multiple small peripheral follicles ("string of pearls") in an enlarged ovary, characteristic of polycystic ovary syndrome.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycheartfailure.png ]
questions.explanation: Cardiomegaly with cephalization, Kerley B lines and interstitial/alveolar edema indicates heart failure. Bilateral bronchopneumonia gives patchy consolidation without cephalization or Kerley B lines.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycrightmiddlelobepneumonia.png ]
questions.explanation: Air-space opacity that obscures the right heart border (silhouette sign) localizes to the right middle lobe. Right lower lobe pneumonia obscures the right hemidiaphragm instead, and collapse would show volume loss.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpleuraleffusion.png ]
questions.explanation: Homogeneous opacity with a meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle indicates pleural effusion. Pneumonia shows air bronchograms without a meniscus, and pneumothorax is radiolucent.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycconsolidationxray.png ]
questions.explanation: Right upper lobe consolidation. The air-space opacification has a straight lower border confirming it's right upper lobe location.
questions.note: السؤال اللي كان لدفعة ايريس بحكوا كانت الصورة middle lobe

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteochondroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A bony projection with cortical and medullary continuity with the parent bone, arising from the metaphysis and pointing away from the joint, is characteristic of osteochondroma (cartilage-capped exostosis).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymankylosingspondylitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The spine radiograph shows syndesmophytic fusion (bamboo spine appearance), a hallmark of ankylosing spondylitis rather than the asymmetric joint-space narrowing of OA or RA.

questions.text: Identify the fracture shown in the image: [img: Radiologymclaviclefracture.png ]
questions.explanation: There is a comminuted fracture of the distal third of the clavicle. The proximal fractured fragment is displaced superiorly, with mild skin tenting. The distal  fractured fragment is displaced inferiorly . There is pseudo-widening of the acromioclavicular joint space. However the coracoclavicular and sternoclavicular joint space alignment is maintained. The inferior border of acromion is not in the same line as the inferior border of distal clavicle, this is suspicious for acromioclavicular joint disruption. No associated other bone fractures. Adjacent soft tissue thickening is seen.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteoarthritis.jpg ]
questions.explanation: There is moderate narrowing predominantly involving the medial tibio-femoral and significant narrowing of the lateral patellofemoral compartments. There are moderate marginal osteophytes. There is mild subchondral sclerosis on the right and left. There is moderate pointing of the tibial spines on the right and left. There is a moderate joint effusion on the right and left. There is varus deformity at the knee.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymnonossifyingfibroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A multiloculated lucent metaphyseal lesion with a sclerotic rim, larger than 3 cm and eccentrically placed near the physis, is a non-ossifying fibroma.

questions.text: What is the most likely fracture shown in the image? [img: Radiologymintertrochantericfracture.png ]
questions.explanation: The fracture line courses between the greater and lesser trochanters, distinguishing it from a subcapital neck fracture, which occurs proximal to this region.

questions.text: Identify the fracture shown in the image: [img: Radiologymsubtrochantericfracture.jpg ]
questions.explanation: Oblique view of the right pelvis demonstrates a comminuted subtrochanteric fracture (inferior to the greater and lesser trochanters). The proximal fragment appears abducted. The lesser trochanter is itself fractured and separated from the femur.

questions.text: Identify the fracture shown in the image: [img: Radiologym5thmetatarsalfracture.png ]
questions.correctAnswer: D) Fracture of the 5th metatarsal base
questions.explanation: A true fracture at the proximal 5th metatarsal is transverse, whereas the normal apophysis runs longitudinally — a key distinguishing feature.

questions.text: Fallen fragment sign is seen in which of the following lesions?
questions.explanation: A pathological fracture through a simple bone cyst allows a bony fragment to settle dependently within the fluid-filled cavity, producing the fallen fragment sign.

questions.text: Which artery supplies the infarcted territory shown in this image? [img: Radiologynacainfarct.png ]
questions.explanation: The infarct involves the medial frontal lobe, the classic ACA distribution, unlike the lateral hemispheric MCA territory or the occipital PCA territory.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynepiduralhematomaacute.png ]
questions.explanation: A biconvex, lentiform hyperdense extra-axial collection is the classic CT appearance of acute epidural hematoma, distinct from the crescentic shape of subdural hematoma.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynintraventricularhemorrhage.png ]
questions.explanation: An acute intracerebral haemorrhage is centred in the basal ganglia of the right hemisphere with the extension of blood into both lateral ventricles (intraventricular haemorrhage), third & fourth ventricles as well as the foramina of Luschka and Magendie. There is no hydrocephalus at this stage.

questions.text: Identify the neuroanatomical structures labeled 1, 2, and 4 on this axial brain CT, respectively. [img: Radiologynanatomy1brain.png ]
questions.explanation: This labeled axial CT correctly places the frontal lobe label on the patient's left side while the caudate head and thalamus labels are both on the right side.
questions.note: 1. Frontal lobe || 2. Caudate || 3. Parietal lobe || 4. Thalamus || 5. Internal capsule

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmcainfarct.png ]
questions.explanation: DWI hyperintensity with ADC hypointensity (true restricted diffusion) confirms acute ischemic infarction, unlike chronic infarct (facilitated diffusion) or vasogenic edema (no restriction). Here, ADC (Apparent Diffusion Coefficient) map acts as a mirror image to confirm true tissue ischemia by turning dark.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynposteriorischemia.png ]
questions.explanation: Hypodensity in the posterior/occipital vascular distribution reflects posterior circulation (PCA/vertebrobasilar) ischemia rather than an anterior circulation or hemorrhagic process.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynsubarachnoidhemorrhage.png ]
questions.explanation: Subarachnoid hemorrhage along the right central sulcus. Hyperdense material filling the basal cisterns and sulci (rather than a discrete extra-axial collection or intraventricular clot) is characteristic of diffuse SAH.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynskullfracture.png ]
questions.explanation: Axial CT bone window show left parietal bone fracture.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynsubduralhemorrhage.png ]
questions.explanation: Non-contrast head CT reveals hyperdense extra-axial collection overlying the right hemisphere consistent with acute subdural hematoma. A crescentic extra-axial collection that can cross suture lines is classic for subdural hemorrhage, distinguishing it from the biconvex/lentiform epidural hematoma.

questions.text: Which is not a typical finding in acute cholecystitis on ultrasound?
questions.explanation: Acute cholecystitis classically shows a thickened (>3 mm), edematous gallbladder wall; a thin, normal wall argues against the diagnosis.

questions.text: Wrong about appendicitis?
options: Most common cause of acute abdomen in young patients
Can present with periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant
A fecalith may be seen as an appendicolith
Less common in the pediatric age group
originalOptions: Most common cause of acute abdomen in young patients
Can present with periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant
A fecalith may be seen as an appendicolith
Less common in the pediatric age group
questions.correctAnswer: D) Less common in the pediatric age group
questions.correctAnswerText: Less common in the pediatric age group
questions.explanation: Appendicitis is actually common in children and young adults, not less common in this age group, making this statement false.

questions.text: False about volvulus?
options: Midgut volvulus shows a whirlpool sign
Sigmoid volvulus shows a coffee bean sign
Volvulus is twisting of the bowel around its mesentery
originalOptions: Midgut volvulus shows a whirlpool sign
Sigmoid volvulus shows a coffee bean sign
Volvulus is twisting of the bowel around its mesentery
questions.correctAnswer: B) Cecal volvulus has no haustration
questions.explanation: Cecal volvulus generally maintains a haustral pattern, unlike sigmoid volvulus which is typically ahaustral, making this statement false.

questions.text: All are signs of pneumoperitoneum except:
questions.explanation: The bird-beak sign is a feature of achalasia, not pneumoperitoneum; the other four are all recognized radiographic signs of free intraperitoneal air.

questions.text: Regarding abdomen anatomy, which of the following is wrong?
options: The second part of the duodenum passes between the liver and pancreas
The inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
The superior mesenteric artery is at the level of T11, above the celiac axis
The renal arteries arise at approximately L1–L2
originalOptions: The second part of the duodenum passes between the liver and pancreas
The inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
The superior mesenteric artery is at the level of T11, above the celiac axis
The renal arteries arise at approximately L1–L2
questions.correctAnswer: C) The superior mesenteric artery is at the level of T11, above the celiac axis
questions.correctAnswerText: The superior mesenteric artery is at the level of T11, above the celiac axis
questions.explanation: The celiac trunk (T12) actually arises above the SMA (L1), so stating the SMA is at T11 "above" the celiac axis reverses the correct order; the IMA at L3 and renal arteries at L1–L2 are both correct as stated.

questions.text: Which clock-face statement for a right-breast mass is FALSE?
options: The right lower-inner quadrant corresponds to 3–6 o'clock
The right lower-outer quadrant corresponds to 6–9 o'clock
The right upper-inner quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
The right upper-outer quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
A right-breast lesion at 5 o'clock lies in the lower-inner quadrant
originalOptions: The right lower-inner quadrant corresponds to 3–6 o'clock
The right lower-outer quadrant corresponds to 6–9 o'clock
The right upper-inner quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
The right upper-outer quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
A right-breast lesion at 5 o'clock lies in the lower-inner quadrant
questions.correctAnswer: C) The right upper-inner quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
questions.correctAnswerText: The right upper-inner quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
questions.explanation: In the right breast, 9 o'clock is lateral, so 9–12 o'clock is the upper-outer quadrant. The upper-inner quadrant is 12–3 o'clock.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about air bronchograms is FALSE?
options: They are commonly seen in lung consolidation
They are present in alveolar disease
They are absent in pleural effusion
They are typical in lung collapse
They represent patent airways outlined by air within opacified lung
originalOptions: They are commonly seen in lung consolidation
They are present in alveolar disease
They are absent in pleural effusion
They are typical in lung collapse
They represent patent airways outlined by air within opacified lung
questions.correctAnswer: D) They are typical in lung collapse
questions.correctAnswerText: They are typical in lung collapse
questions.explanation: Air bronchograms characterize consolidation and alveolar disease. They are not a typical feature of collapse, which is defined by volume loss with crowded bronchi.

questions.text: Regarding pneumothorax, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The chest tube should be inserted posterosuperiorly at the affected side
The affected lung shows increased lucency in tension pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted posteroinferiorly at the affected side
The chest tube should be placed anteroinferiorly at the affected side
The mediastinum shifts toward the side of the tension pneumothorax
originalOptions: The chest tube should be inserted posterosuperiorly at the affected side
The affected lung shows increased lucency in tension pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted posteroinferiorly at the affected side
The chest tube should be placed anteroinferiorly at the affected side
The mediastinum shifts toward the side of the tension pneumothorax
questions.correctAnswer: B) The affected lung shows increased lucency in tension pneumothorax
questions.correctAnswerText: The affected lung shows increased lucency in tension pneumothorax
questions.explanation: Tension pneumothorax gives a hyperlucent hemithorax with a collapsed lung. The mediastinum shifts away from it, and the tube is placed anterosuperiorly, not posteriorly or inferiorly.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about stage II sarcoidosis is WRONG?
options: Hilar lymph node enlargement is present
Nodal enlargement with pleural effusion is the defining feature
Reticulonodular opacities may involve the upper zones
originalOptions: Hilar lymph node enlargement is present
Nodal enlargement with pleural effusion is the defining feature
Reticulonodular opacities may involve the upper zones
questions.correctAnswer: B) Nodal enlargement with pleural effusion is the defining feature
questions.correctAnswerText: Nodal enlargement with pleural effusion is the defining feature
questions.explanation: Stage II is defined by nodal enlargement plus parenchymal disease. Pleural effusion is not a staging criterion.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding cavitation in post-primary tuberculosis?
options: It is more likely to occur than in primary TB
It develops mainly in the posterior segments of the upper lobes
The superior segment of the lower lobe can also be involved
It develops years after the primary infection, often with decreased immunity
It typically occurs in the posterior basal segments of the lower lobes
originalOptions: It is more likely to occur than in primary TB
It develops mainly in the posterior segments of the upper lobes
The superior segment of the lower lobe can also be involved
It develops years after the primary infection, often with decreased immunity
It typically occurs in the posterior basal segments of the lower lobes
questions.correctAnswer: E) It typically occurs in the posterior basal segments of the lower lobes
questions.correctAnswerText: It typically occurs in the posterior basal segments of the lower lobes
questions.explanation: Post-primary cavities occur in the posterior segments of the upper lobes (~85%) and the superior segment of the lower lobe. The posterior basal segments are not typical.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding pleural effusion?
options: Blunting of the costophrenic angle is seen
A meniscus is seen on erect frontal films
A lateral decubitus view with the affected side down is the most sensitive projection
It appears lucent (radiolucent) on chest radiograph
A large effusion causes mediastinal shift away from the effusion
originalOptions: Blunting of the costophrenic angle is seen
A meniscus is seen on erect frontal films
A lateral decubitus view with the affected side down is the most sensitive projection
It appears lucent (radiolucent) on chest radiograph
A large effusion causes mediastinal shift away from the effusion
questions.correctAnswer: D) It appears lucent (radiolucent) on chest radiograph
questions.correctAnswerText: It appears lucent (radiolucent) on chest radiograph
questions.explanation: Fluid is soft-tissue density, so an effusion appears as an opacity (white). Pneumothorax is the pleural pathology that appears lucent.

questions.text: Which of the following is INCORRECT regarding child abuse injuries?
options: Metaphyseal corner fractures are highly specific for abuse
Posterior rib fractures are strongly associated with intentional injury
Epidural hematoma is more specific for abuse than subdural hematoma
Scapular fractures carry a high specificity for physical abuse
originalOptions: Metaphyseal corner fractures are highly specific for abuse
Posterior rib fractures are strongly associated with intentional injury
Epidural hematoma is more specific for abuse than subdural hematoma
Scapular fractures carry a high specificity for physical abuse
questions.correctAnswer: C) Epidural hematoma is more specific for abuse than subdural hematoma
questions.correctAnswerText: Epidural hematoma is more specific for abuse than subdural hematoma
questions.explanation: Subdural hematomas (not epidural) are highly specific and characteristic of non-accidental trauma, while metaphyseal corner, posterior rib, and scapular fractures are well-established indicators of child abuse.

questions.text: Hyperparathyroidism causes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hyperparathyroidism causes bone resorption and osteopenia, not increased bone mass; osteosclerosis is not a feature of this disease.

questions.text: Periosteal reaction is seen in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fibrous cortical defect is a quiescent benign lesion that does not incite a periosteal reaction, unlike infection, healing fractures, or osteoid osteoma.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding radiologic features of gout?
questions.explanation: Gout characteristically preserves the joint space until late in the disease course; early joint space narrowing is instead a feature of inflammatory arthropathies like RA.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding ankylosing spondylitis?
options: Interspinous ligament ossification gives a "dagger spine" appearance
originalOptions: Interspinous ligament ossification gives a "dagger spine" appearance
questions.explanation: Ankylosing spondylitis has a male predilection of about 3:1 or more, making "more common in females" the false statement.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG about osteoarthritis?
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis characteristically produces asymmetric joint-space narrowing, unlike the symmetric pattern seen in rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the Circle of Willis is FALSE?
options: The superior cerebellar artery (SCA) arises from the distal basilar artery
The Circle of Willis provides collateral circulation between anterior and posterior circulation
The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid artery to the posterior cerebral artery
The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
originalOptions: The superior cerebellar artery (SCA) arises from the distal basilar artery
The Circle of Willis provides collateral circulation between anterior and posterior circulation
The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid artery to the posterior cerebral artery
The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
questions.correctAnswer: D) The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
questions.correctAnswerText: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
questions.explanation: AICA is a branch of the proximal basilar artery; the distal vertebral artery instead gives rise to PICA. SCA does arise from the distal basilar artery, and the Circle of Willis does provide interhemispheric collateral flow.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding cranial nerve involvement in multiple sclerosis?
options: The trigeminal nerve (CN5) can be affected
The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
The abducens nerve (CN6) can be affected
Optic nerve involvement (optic neuritis) is common
originalOptions: The trigeminal nerve (CN5) can be affected
The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
The abducens nerve (CN6) can be affected
Optic nerve involvement (optic neuritis) is common
questions.correctAnswer: B) The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
questions.correctAnswerText: The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
questions.explanation: Optic neuritis (CN2) is the most common cranial nerve manifestation of MS, followed by CN5/6; oculomotor involvement is not the classic pattern.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about MS lesion characteristics is TRUE?
options: Active plaques characteristically do not enhance with contrast
Diffuse cerebral atrophy is an early MS finding
T1-hypointense "black hole" lesions indicate a better prognosis
Enhancement never occurs in MS lesions
T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
originalOptions: Active plaques characteristically do not enhance with contrast
Diffuse cerebral atrophy is an early MS finding
T1-hypointense "black hole" lesions indicate a better prognosis
Enhancement never occurs in MS lesions
T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
questions.correctAnswer: E) T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
questions.correctAnswerText: T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
questions.explanation: T1 hypointensity reflects irreversible axonal loss; active plaques classically DO enhance (reflecting blood-brain barrier breakdown), and diffuse atrophy is typically a late finding.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about primary CNS lymphoma is FALSE?
options: It is typically hyperdense on non-contrast CT
It shows restricted diffusion on DWI
The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
It shows homogeneous enhancement in immunocompetent patients
originalOptions: It is typically hyperdense on non-contrast CT
It shows restricted diffusion on DWI
The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
It shows homogeneous enhancement in immunocompetent patients
questions.correctAnswer: C) The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
questions.correctAnswerText: The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
questions.explanation: Primary CNS lymphoma is highly cellular and restricts diffusion, so its ADC value is typically LOWER, not higher, than normal brain.

questions.text: Which of the following anatomical relationships is CORRECT?
options: The claustrum lies lateral to the insula
The hippocampus lies anterosuperior to the amygdala
The uncus forms the lateral border of the temporal lobe
The claustrum lies medial to the putamen, separated by the internal capsule
originalOptions: The claustrum lies lateral to the insula
The hippocampus lies anterosuperior to the amygdala
The uncus forms the lateral border of the temporal lobe
The claustrum lies medial to the putamen, separated by the internal capsule
questions.correctAnswer: A) The claustrum lies lateral to the insula
questions.correctAnswerText: The claustrum lies lateral to the insula
questions.explanation: The claustrum is a thin sheet of grey matter lateral to the insula (separated by the extreme capsule); the hippocampus lies posteroinferior (not anterosuperior) to the amygdala, and the uncus is the medial (not lateral) temporal border.

questions.text: On T1-weighted MRI, which of the following statements about basal ganglia signal is TRUE?
options: The putamen is hyperintense relative to the globus pallidus
The caudate is hyperintense relative to the thalamus
The globus pallidus is isointense to the putamen
The globus pallidus is hyperintense relative to the putamen
originalOptions: The putamen is hyperintense relative to the globus pallidus
The caudate is hyperintense relative to the thalamus
The globus pallidus is isointense to the putamen
The globus pallidus is hyperintense relative to the putamen
questions.correctAnswer: D) The globus pallidus is hyperintense relative to the putamen
questions.correctAnswerText: The globus pallidus is hyperintense relative to the putamen
questions.explanation: On T1-weighted MRI, the globus pallidus normally appears relatively hyperintense compared with the putamen — a useful anatomical landmark.

questions.text: Which of the following locations is NOT typical for hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage?
questions.explanation: Hypertensive ICH classically occurs in deep structures (basal ganglia, thalamus, pons, cerebellum) supplied by small penetrating vessels; a lobar location like the frontal lobe instead suggests another etiology (e.g., amyloid angiopathy, AVM, tumor).

questions.text: Which stage of hemorrhage is classically hyperintense on both T1 and T2-weighted MRI due to extracellular methemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Late subacute hemorrhage (extracellular methemoglobin) is T1 and T2 hyperintense; early subacute (intracellular methemoglobin) is T1 hyperintense but T2 hypointense, and acute/chronic stages are T2 hypointense.

questions.text: In this labeled axial CT, structure "3" corresponds to which organ? [img: Radiologyaabdominalanatomyleftkidney.png ]
questions.explanation: I don't know what to write; there's no explanation :)
questions.note: 1. Liver || 2. Gallbladder || 3. Left kidney

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyarenalstonehydronephrosis.png ]
questions.correctAnswer: A) Obstructing renal stone with hydronephrosis
questions.explanation: The CT shows a calculus with upstream dilatation of the collecting system, consistent with an obstructing stone causing hydronephrosis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpleuraleffusion.png ]
questions.explanation: Homogeneous opacity with a meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle indicates pleural effusion. Pneumonia shows air bronchograms without a meniscus, and pneumothorax is radiolucent.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyclingularpneumonia.png ]
questions.explanation: Air-space opacity obscuring the left heart border, sitting anterior to the left major fissure on the lateral view, is lingular pneumonia. The left lung has no middle lobe or minor fissure, and left lower lobe pneumonia would obscure the left hemidiaphragm.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymddh.png ]
questions.explanation: The image shows a shallow acetabulum with a small, laterally decentered femoral epiphysis in a young child, classic for Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) rather than the older-child presentations of Perthes or SCFE.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymperthesdisease.png ]
questions.explanation: Femoral head deformity and flattening with widening of joint space and blurring of the physeal plate on the left.

questions.text: Identify the fracture shown in the image: [img: Radiologymcollesfracture.png ]
questions.explanation: Extra-articular transverse fracture of the distal radius with dorsal angulation, ulnar styloid fracture and soft tissue oedema.

questions.text: Which stage of hemorrhage is classically hyperintense on both T1 and T2-weighted MRI due to extracellular methemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Late subacute hemorrhage (extracellular methemoglobin) is T1 and T2 hyperintense; early subacute (intracellular methemoglobin) is T1 hyperintense but T2 hypointense, and acute/chronic stages are T2 hypointense.

questions.text: In this labeled axial CT image, what does structure "3" represent? [img: Radiologyaleftrenalvein.png ]
questions.explanation: In this labeled slice the numbered structures correspond to liver, gallbladder, and left renal vein, consistent with the vein's typical course anterior to the aorta toward the IVC, the characteristic path of the left renal vein (it crosses anterior to the aorta, unlike the renal artery which lies posterior to the vein).
questions.note: 1. Liver || 2. Gallbladder || 3. Left renal vein

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaappendicitisct.png ]
questions.explanation: The coronal CT shows an appendicolith with a dilated, thick-walled appendix and surrounding fat stranding, diagnostic of acute appendicitis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycaorticdissection.png ]
questions.explanation: Contrast CT shows an intimal flap separating a true and a false lumen. An aneurysm is a fusiform dilatation without a flap, and pulmonary embolism gives filling defects in the pulmonary arteries.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyclingularpneumonia.png ]
questions.explanation: Air-space opacity obscuring the left heart border, sitting anterior to the left major fissure on the lateral view, is lingular pneumonia. The left lung has no middle lobe or minor fissure, and left lower lobe pneumonia would obscure the left hemidiaphragm.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymankylosingspondylitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The spine radiograph shows syndesmophytic fusion (bamboo spine appearance), a hallmark of ankylosing spondylitis rather than the asymmetric joint-space narrowing of OA or RA.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteoarthritis.jpg ]
questions.explanation: There is moderate narrowing predominantly involving the medial tibio-femoral and significant narrowing of the lateral patellofemoral compartments. There are moderate marginal osteophytes. There is mild subchondral sclerosis on the right and left. There is moderate pointing of the tibial spines on the right and left. There is a moderate joint effusion on the right and left. There is varus deformity at the knee.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteoidosteoma.png ]
questions.explanation: A sclerotic lesion with a well-defined lucent nidus less than 2 cm at the femoral neck is classic for osteoid osteoma; larger size (>2cm) would favor osteoblastoma.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]
questions.explanation: Loss of grey-white differentiation with a "dense cerebellum sign" and sulcal effacement are classic for diffuse cerebral edema.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmcainfarct.png ]
questions.explanation: DWI hyperintensity with ADC hypointensity (true restricted diffusion) confirms acute ischemic infarction, unlike chronic infarct (facilitated diffusion) or vasogenic edema (no restriction). Here, ADC (Apparent Diffusion Coefficient) map acts as a mirror image to confirm true tissue ischemia by turning dark.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyasigmoidvolvulus.png ]
questions.explanation: The classic "coffee bean" sign, a markedly dilated ahaustral gas-filled loop arising from the pelvis and pointing toward the RUQ, identifies sigmoid volvulus. Cecal volvulus arises in the RLQ with the haustral pattern maintained, and a generic large bowel obstruction lacks the coffee-bean loop.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumoperitoneum.png ]
questions.explanation: Free intraperitoneal air is seen outlining the bowel loops and under the diaphragm, diagnostic of pneumoperitoneum rather than a fluid- or obstruction-related process.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyahydronephrosis.png ]
questions.explanation: The coronal CT shows dilatation of the left renal collecting system (pelvicalyceal dilation) without a discrete simple fluid collection, consistent with hydronephrosis rather than an isolated stone or cyst.

questions.text: In this labeled axial CT, structure "3" corresponds to which organ? [img: Radiologyaabdominalanatomyleftkidney.png ]
questions.explanation: I don't know what to write; there's no explanation :)
questions.note: 1. Liver || 2. Gallbladder || 3. Left kidney

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpleuraleffusion.png ]
questions.explanation: Homogeneous opacity with a meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle indicates pleural effusion. Pneumonia shows air bronchograms without a meniscus, and pneumothorax is radiolucent.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycaorticdissection.png ]
questions.explanation: Contrast CT shows an intimal flap separating a true and a false lumen. An aneurysm is a fusiform dilatation without a flap, and pulmonary embolism gives filling defects in the pulmonary arteries.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycrightupperlobecollapse.png ]
questions.explanation: A triangular right upper zone opacity with an elevated horizontal fissure and elevated right hilum shows volume loss, so it is collapse. Pneumothorax is lucent, effusion shows a meniscus, and consolidation preserves lobar volume and does not displace the fissure.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymperthesdisease.png ]
questions.explanation: Femoral head deformity and flattening with widening of joint space and blurring of the physeal plate on the left.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]
questions.explanation: Loss of grey-white differentiation with a "dense cerebellum sign" and sulcal effacement are classic for diffuse cerebral edema.

questions.text: Regarding bowel obstruction, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Cecal volvulus usually extends to the right upper quadrant
Descending colon diameter of 5 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
More than three air-fluid levels, each >2.5 cm in width, support bowel obstruction
originalOptions: Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Cecal volvulus usually extends to the right upper quadrant
Descending colon diameter of 5 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
More than three air-fluid levels, each >2.5 cm in width, support bowel obstruction
questions.correctAnswer: E) More than three air-fluid levels, each >2.5 cm in width, support bowel obstruction
questions.correctAnswerText: More than three air-fluid levels, each >2.5 cm in width, support bowel obstruction
questions.explanation: Multiple (more than three) air-fluid levels exceeding 2.5 cm in width is a standard supportive criterion for bowel obstruction; the cecal dilatation threshold is 9 cm, and cecal volvulus extends toward the epigastrium/left upper quadrant, not the right.

questions.text: Regarding free air in the abdomen, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
History of abdominal surgery within one week is a cause of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Supine chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
originalOptions: The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
History of abdominal surgery within one week is a cause of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Supine chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
questions.correctAnswer: C) History of abdominal surgery within one week is a cause of pneumoperitoneum
questions.correctAnswerText: History of abdominal surgery within one week is a cause of pneumoperitoneum
questions.explanation: Residual post-operative free air can persist for several days after abdominal surgery, so recent surgery is a recognized cause of pneumoperitoneum. The falciform ligament sign supports pneumoperitoneum, portal venous gas is peripheral, and it is the erect (not supine) chest film that is the most sensitive.

questions.text: Regarding abdominal calcifications, which one of the following is TRUE?
options: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen lucent on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
Ninety five percent of gall bladder stones seen on Ultrasound imaging
Pelvic calcification seen medial to the sacroiliac joint usually represents appendicolith
originalOptions: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen lucent on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
Ninety five percent of gall bladder stones seen on Ultrasound imaging
Pelvic calcification seen medial to the sacroiliac joint usually represents appendicolith
questions.correctAnswer: D) Ninety five percent of gall bladder stones seen on Ultrasound imaging
questions.correctAnswerText: Ninety five percent of gall bladder stones seen on Ultrasound imaging
questions.explanation: Ultrasound detects the vast majority (~95%) of gallstones regardless of their radiographic composition; phleboliths are venous (not arterial), and most renal stones are radiopaque (not lucent) on plain film.

questions.text: Regarding abdomen anatomy, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L2
The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile and pancreatic ducts
The right adrenal gland lies more superiorly than the left adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of pancreas
originalOptions: The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L2
The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile and pancreatic ducts
The right adrenal gland lies more superiorly than the left adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of pancreas
questions.correctAnswer: B) The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile and pancreatic ducts
questions.correctAnswerText: The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile and pancreatic ducts
questions.explanation: The major duodenal papilla, where the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct join and empty, is located in the second (descending) part of the duodenum. The IMA arises at L3, the left adrenal gland actually sits at a more superior level than the right adrenal gland (T11-L1 vs T12-L1), the left renal vein is longer than right, and the portal vein forms posterior to the pancreatic neck.

questions.text: Regarding BI-RADS breast classification, which of the following is FALSE?
options: BI-RADS 3 represents a probably benign finding and needs follow-up
BI-RADS 0 represents an incomplete study and needs additional imaging
BI-RADS 1 represents a negative study with no evidence of abnormalities
originalOptions: BI-RADS 3 represents a probably benign finding and needs follow-up
BI-RADS 0 represents an incomplete study and needs additional imaging
BI-RADS 1 represents a negative study with no evidence of abnormalities
questions.explanation: BI-RADS 2 is a benign finding. Biopsy-proven malignancy is BI-RADS 6.

questions.text: All of the following can cause lobar collapse EXCEPT:
options: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
originalOptions: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.correctAnswer: E) Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.correctAnswerText: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.explanation: Lobar collapse results from luminal obstruction (foreign body, mucus plug), mural lesions (carcinoma) or extrinsic compression. Bullous emphysema does not obstruct the supplying bronchus.

questions.text: An infant is suspected of having left-sided foreign body aspiration. Which of the following chest views is NOT helpful?
questions.explanation: With a check-valve obstruction, the affected lung fails to deflate on expiration or when the affected side is dependent (left lateral decubitus). A right lateral decubitus view gives no additional information for a left-sided foreign body.

questions.text: Regarding pneumothorax, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The chest tube should be inserted posterosuperiorly at the affected side
The affected lung shows increased lucency in tension pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted posteroinferiorly at the affected side
The chest tube should be placed anteroinferiorly at the affected side
The mediastinum shifts toward the side of the tension pneumothorax
originalOptions: The chest tube should be inserted posterosuperiorly at the affected side
The affected lung shows increased lucency in tension pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted posteroinferiorly at the affected side
The chest tube should be placed anteroinferiorly at the affected side
The mediastinum shifts toward the side of the tension pneumothorax
questions.correctAnswer: B) The affected lung shows increased lucency in tension pneumothorax
questions.correctAnswerText: The affected lung shows increased lucency in tension pneumothorax
questions.explanation: Tension pneumothorax gives a hyperlucent hemithorax with a collapsed lung. The mediastinum shifts away from it, and the tube is placed anterosuperiorly, not posteriorly or inferiorly.

questions.text: Regarding normal appearances on chest imaging, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The left main bronchus is shorter and steeper than the right main bronchus
The heart base consists of the right atrium shadow
The right vascular bulge at the third intercostal space represents the aortic knob
The right pulmonary artery arches over the right main bronchus
The right hemidiaphragm is normally higher than the left (up to about 2 cm)
originalOptions: The left main bronchus is shorter and steeper than the right main bronchus
The heart base consists of the right atrium shadow
The right vascular bulge at the third intercostal space represents the aortic knob
The right pulmonary artery arches over the right main bronchus
The right hemidiaphragm is normally higher than the left (up to about 2 cm)
questions.correctAnswer: E) The right hemidiaphragm is normally higher than the left (up to about 2 cm)
questions.correctAnswerText: The right hemidiaphragm is normally higher than the left (up to about 2 cm)
questions.explanation: The liver normally elevates the right hemidiaphragm. The left main bronchus is longer and more horizontal, and the aortic knob lies on the left.

questions.text: Regarding MRI, which of the following is FALSE?
options: Its image resolution is higher than that of ultrasound
It is a cross-sectional imaging modality
Contrast allergy is a relative contraindication for contrasted images
The quality of MRI images is lower in the chest region than in the brain region
originalOptions: Its image resolution is higher than that of ultrasound
It is a cross-sectional imaging modality
Contrast allergy is a relative contraindication for contrasted images
The quality of MRI images is lower in the chest region than in the brain region
questions.explanation: MRI uses a strong magnet and radiofrequency waves, with no ionizing radiation. Radiographs and CT are the modalities that use it.

questions.text: Reducing the kV from 90 to 70 in a radiograph, with image density maintained, will generally:
options: Decrease the contrast between air and soft tissue
originalOptions: Decrease the contrast between air and soft tissue
questions.explanation: Lowering kV reduces beam penetration, so mAs must be increased to keep the same image density, and patient dose rises. Contrast between tissues improves rather than falls at lower kV.

questions.text: Regarding Hounsfield's scale, which one of the following is TRUE?

questions.correctAnswerText: Splenic parenchymal density measures about 65 HU
