questions.text: Fallen fragment sign is seen in which of the following lesions?
questions.explanation: A pathological fracture through a simple bone cyst allows a bony fragment to settle dependently within the fluid-filled cavity, producing the fallen fragment sign.

questions.text: What is the most common type of Salter-Harris fracture?
questions.explanation: Salter-Harris type II accounts for approximately 75% of physeal fractures, making it by far the most common subtype.

questions.text: The demonstration of an abnormal fat pad in a pediatric patient suggests which of the following?
questions.explanation: Supracondylar fracture is the classic pediatric cause of an elbow joint effusion (fat pad sign), whereas radial head fracture is the typical adult cause.

questions.text: Paravertebral ossification (bamboo spine) is a typical radiological finding in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Diffuse syndesmophytic fusion of the spine producing the bamboo spine appearance is a hallmark of ankylosing spondylitis.

questions.text: Which of the following imaging features is usually present in osteosarcoma?
options: Well-defined lucent nidus with central ossification
originalOptions: Well-defined lucent nidus with central ossification
questions.explanation: Osteosarcoma is an aggressive lesion with a wide, ill-defined zone of transition; rings and arcs, ground glass, and a lucent nidus instead describe chondroid, fibrous dysplastic, and osteoid osteoma lesions respectively.

questions.text: Regarding fibrous cortical defect, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Fibrous cortical defect is a malignant bony lesion
Most common benign bony lesion in elderly patients
originalOptions: Fibrous cortical defect is a malignant bony lesion
Most common benign bony lesion in elderly patients
questions.explanation: As a quiescent benign lesion, fibrous cortical defect elicits no periosteal reaction; it is histologically identical to non-ossifying fibroma (not osteoblastoma) and is most common in children, not the elderly.

questions.text: Regarding avulsion fractures, which of the following is TRUE?
questions.correctAnswer: A) Sartorius – anterior superior iliac spine
questions.explanation: The sartorius originates from the ASIS, making this the correct pairing; hamstrings actually attach at the ischial tuberosity and rectus femoris at the AIIS.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus?
questions.explanation: A colloid cyst at the foramen of Monro physically obstructs CSF flow (non-communicating hydrocephalus); SAH, meningitis, and meningeal carcinomatosis impair CSF absorption (communicating), and choroid plexus papilloma causes communicating hydrocephalus via CSF overproduction.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a cause of restriction on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)?
questions.explanation: Arachnoid cysts contain simple CSF-like fluid and do not restrict diffusion, unlike abscesses, acute ischemia, high-grade tumors, and post-ictal states.

questions.text: What is the most common spinal cord tumor in adults?
questions.explanation: Ependymoma is the most common intramedullary spinal cord tumor in adults, whereas astrocytoma predominates in children.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT found in hyperacute brain ischemia?
options: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
originalOptions: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.correctAnswer: E) Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.correctAnswerText: Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.explanation: These are late/chronic infarct changes (>3 weeks); the hyperacute stage (0–6 hours) instead shows subtle grey-white loss, cortical hypodensity, gyral effacement, and loss of the insular ribbon sign.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the two frontal bones?
questions.explanation: The metopic suture is the embryological midline suture between the two frontal bones, which normally fuses in early childhood.

questions.text: Which of the following radiologic features, if present, is supportive of the diagnosis of Sturge-Weber syndrome?
options: Restriction on DWI in both PCA territories
originalOptions: Restriction on DWI in both PCA territories
questions.explanation: Sturge-Weber syndrome classically shows gyriform ("tram-track") cortical/subcortical calcification underlying the leptomeningeal angioma; the other features belong to different conditions (MS, tuberous sclerosis).
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: Regarding extradural (epidural) hematoma, which of the following is FALSE?
options: It does not cross the falx cerebri
There is a history of trauma
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery

There is a history of trauma

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.explanation: Epidural hematoma CAN cross the falx cerebri but does NOT cross cranial sutures (opposite the pattern of subdural hematoma); the other listed features are true.

questions.text: Which one of the following is a common radiologic feature of diffuse brain edema?
questions.explanation: Diffuse cerebral edema effaces the sulci and narrows the ventricles/basal cisterns; the brain typically appears diffusely hypodense (not hyperdense) except for the relatively dense-appearing cerebellum.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapancreatitis.png ]

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyasigmoidvolvulus.png ]
questions.explanation: The classic "coffee bean" sign, a markedly dilated ahaustral gas-filled loop arising from the pelvis and pointing toward the RUQ, identifies sigmoid volvulus. Cecal volvulus arises in the RLQ with the haustral pattern maintained, and a generic large bowel obstruction lacks the coffee-bean loop.

questions.text: What is the name of this radiological sign? [img: Radiologyafootballsign.png ]
questions.explanation: A massive pneumoperitoneum outlines the entire abdominal cavity in an oval, football-like shape on a supine film, which is the football sign (seen especially in neonates/infants).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumoperitoneum.png ]
questions.explanation: Free intraperitoneal air is seen outlining the bowel loops and under the diaphragm, diagnostic of pneumoperitoneum rather than a fluid- or obstruction-related process.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyadiverticulitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows sigmoid diverticula with adjacent pericolic fat stranding and mild bowel wall thickening, the classic appearance of diverticulitis rather than isolated diverticulosis.

questions.text: Most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyacolorectalcancer.png ]
questions.explanation: The contrast enema shows eccentric, irregular annular narrowing of the colon (the apple-core sign), typical of colorectal carcinoma. Intussusception appears as an occluding mass prolapsing into the lumen (coiled-spring sign), not an annular stricture.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaappendicitisus.jpg ]
questions.explanation: The imaging (Ultrasound) shows a dilated, non-compressible appendix with periappendiceal fluid/fat stranding ± appendicolith, the classic combination for acute appendicitis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaleftrenalstone.png ]
questions.explanation: A well-defined, rounded radiopaque calcification overlying the renal shadow on KUB is most consistent with a renal calculus rather than a pelvic phlebolith or lymph node calcification.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaureterstone.png ]
questions.explanation: The calcification lies along the expected course of the ureter (from renal pelvis to bladder), distinguishing it from a phlebolith, which sits in the pelvis away from this line.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyamidgutvolvulus.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows the classic whirlpool sign of the superior mesenteric vessels and mesentery twisting around each other, diagnostic of midgut volvulus (from malrotation).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyagallstoneus.png ]
questions.explanation: Ultrasound shows a hyperechoic intraluminal focus with posterior acoustic shadowing within the gallbladder, the classic appearance of a gallstone.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaappendicitisct.png ]
questions.explanation: The coronal CT shows an appendicolith with a dilated, thick-walled appendix and surrounding fat stranding, diagnostic of acute appendicitis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyacecalvolvulus.png ]
questions.explanation: The x-ray shows a massively dilated loop of large bowel extending from the right lower quadrant toward the epigastrium, with the haustral pattern maintained, consistent with cecal volvulus.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyacholecystitisus.jpg ]
questions.explanation: Ultrasound shows a gallstone with a thickened, edematous gallbladder wall, consistent with acute calculous cholecystitis rather than simple biliary colic.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyacholecystitisct.jpg ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows a thickened, enhancing gallbladder wall with a pericholecystic rim of fluid.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaachalasia.png ]
questions.explanation: The barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering smoothly to a "bird-beak" narrowing at the gastroesophageal junction, the classic finding of achalasia.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyacalcifiedfibroid.jpg ]
questions.explanation: A coarse, popcorn-like calcification in the pelvis in the uterine region is the classic appearance of a calcified leiomyoma. A phlebolith is small and round with a central lucency, and a bladder stone is a rounded intravesical density.
questions.note: Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) are the most common benign solid uterine tumors of myometrial origin, commonly found incidentally. They can be evaluated via US, MRI, CT, and classically present as "popcorn calcification" on X-ray when calcified.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyarenalstonehydronephrosis.png ]
questions.correctAnswer: A) Obstructing renal stone with hydronephrosis
questions.explanation: The CT shows a calculus with upstream dilatation of the collecting system, consistent with an obstructing stone causing hydronephrosis.

questions.text: The arrow (labeled 42) in this axial contrast CT points to which structure? [img: Radiologyaabdominalanatomygallbladder.png ]
questions.explanation: The labeled structure sits in the right upper quadrant along the undersurface of the liver, the typical anatomical position of the gallbladder.

questions.explanation: Calcifications located bilaterally in the suprarenal regions, above the kidneys, correspond to calcified adrenal glands. Renal calculi lie within the renal outlines, and splenic granulomas are scattered in the left upper quadrant.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaascites.jpg ]

questions.correctAnswer: C) The left adrenal gland is higher than the right adrenal gland

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycheartfailure.png ]
questions.explanation: Cardiomegaly with cephalization, Kerley B lines and interstitial/alveolar edema indicates heart failure. Bilateral bronchopneumonia gives patchy consolidation without cephalization or Kerley B lines.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycrightmiddlelobepneumonia.png ]
questions.explanation: Air-space opacity that obscures the right heart border (silhouette sign) localizes to the right middle lobe. Right lower lobe pneumonia obscures the right hemidiaphragm instead, and collapse would show volume loss.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpleuraleffusion.png ]
questions.explanation: Homogeneous opacity with a meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle indicates pleural effusion. Pneumonia shows air bronchograms without a meniscus, and pneumothorax is radiolucent.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the cardiac position finding on this adult chest radiograph? [img: Radiologycdextrocardia.png ]
questions.explanation: Dextrocardia is identified when the cardiac apex and the bulk of the heart silhouette point toward the right side of the chest instead of the left. In this radiograph, the heart silhouette is clearly positioned within the right hemithorax. Notice that the aortic arch is on the left and there is an intestinal/gastric gas bubble on the left, which stands in contrast to situs inversus totalis where both the thoracic and abdominal organs are completely mirrored.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycrightupperlobecollapse.png ]
questions.explanation: A triangular right upper zone opacity with an elevated horizontal fissure and elevated right hilum shows volume loss, so it is collapse. Pneumothorax is lucent, effusion shows a meniscus, and consolidation preserves lobar volume and does not displace the fissure.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyctensionpneumothorax.png ]
questions.explanation: Mobile chest x-ray shows a large right tension pneumothorax with a hyper-expanded hemithorax, splayed ribs, flattened diaphragm, and leftward mediastinal shift. Both lungs show consolidation, preventing further collapse of the right lung. This diagnosis is confirmed because a simple pneumothorax causes no mediastinal shift, while a pleural effusion would appear opaque rather than hyperlucent. Additionally, isolated lung collapse pulls the mediastinum toward the affected side instead of pushing it away, and a diaphragmatic hernia would typically display herniated abdominal contents rather than an empty air space.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycsarcoidosis.png ]
questions.explanation: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. No lung infiltrations are shown. No fibrosis. The plain film demonstrates stage 1 sarcoidosis (i.e. bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy).

questions.text: What is the main finding on this chest radiograph? [img: Radiologycunilateralhilarenlargement.png ]

Sarcoidosis classically gives symmetric bilateral hilar nodes, and ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is typical of childhood primary TB.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteochondroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A bony projection with cortical and medullary continuity with the parent bone, arising from the metaphysis and pointing away from the joint, is characteristic of osteochondroma (cartilage-capped exostosis).

questions.text: What is the name of the labelled carpal bone (Number 6) ? [img: Radiologymanatomycapitate.png ]
questions.explanation: The capitate is the largest carpal bone, centrally located in the distal carpal row, distinguishing it from the hamate (ulnar side), lunate (proximal row), and trapezoid (radial side).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymankylosingspondylitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The spine radiograph shows syndesmophytic fusion (bamboo spine appearance), a hallmark of ankylosing spondylitis rather than the asymmetric joint-space narrowing of OA or RA.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymddh.png ]
questions.explanation: The image shows a shallow acetabulum with a small, laterally decentered femoral epiphysis in a young child, classic for Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) rather than the older-child presentations of Perthes or SCFE.

questions.text: Identify the fracture shown in the image: [img: Radiologymclaviclefracture.png ]

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteoarthritis.jpg ]

There is a moderate joint effusion on the right and left. There is varus deformity at the knee.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymnonossifyingfibroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A multiloculated lucent metaphyseal lesion with a sclerotic rim, larger than 3 cm and eccentrically placed near the physis, is a non-ossifying fibroma.

questions.text: What is the most likely fracture shown in the image? [img: Radiologymintertrochantericfracture.png ]
questions.explanation: The fracture line courses between the greater and lesser trochanters, distinguishing it from a subcapital neck fracture, which occurs proximal to this region.

questions.text: Fallen fragment sign is seen in which of the following lesions?
questions.explanation: A pathological fracture through a simple bone cyst allows a bony fragment to settle dependently within the fluid-filled cavity, producing the fallen fragment sign.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymperthesdisease.png ]
questions.explanation: Femoral head deformity and flattening with widening of joint space and blurring of the physeal plate on the left.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymrickets.png ]
questions.explanation: Cupping, splaying, and fraying of the metaphysis in a child is diagnostic of rickets, the pediatric counterpart of osteomalacia.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteosarcoma.png ]
questions.explanation: A metadiaphyseal lesion with dense sclerotic tumor osteoid and an aggressive periosteal reaction is characteristic of osteosarcoma.

questions.text: Identify the fracture shown in the image: [img: Radiologymcollesfracture.png ]

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmeningioma.png ]

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmultiplesclerosis.png ]

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynepiduralhematomaacute.png ]

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynposteriorischemia.png ]

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynsubarachnoidhemorrhage.png ]

allQuestions.text: Which plain radiograph is the most sensitive for detecting free air under the diaphragm?
allQuestions.explanation: Free gas rises to collect under the diaphragm in the erect position, so the erect chest film is the most sensitive plain radiograph for pneumoperitoneum. Supine abdominal and KUB films miss it, and the lateral view is reserved for patients who cannot stand.
allQuestions.note: While lecture slides generally state "Erect chest radiograph," the modifier "expiratory" included in question banks to emphasize maximized sensitivity for detecting small amounts of subdiaphragmatic free air.

allQuestions.explanation: The MRI/MRCP shows the gallbladder packed with multiple calculi, the defining finding for cholelithiasis (gallstones); the dilated CBD with ductal stones represents an associated complication rather than the primary diagnosis being tested.

allQuestions.explanation: The barium meal shows an irregular, ulcerated mass with abnormal mucosal folds, a pattern typical of malignant gastric ulceration rather than a benign ulcer.

allQuestions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

allQuestions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyabilateraladrenalcalcification.png ]
allQuestions.explanation: Calcifications located bilaterally in the suprarenal regions, above the kidneys, correspond to calcified adrenal glands. Renal calculi lie within the renal outlines, and splenic granulomas are scattered in the left upper quadrant.

allQuestions.text: Regarding abdominal calcifications, which one of the following is TRUE?
options: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Bilateral adrenal calcifications seen at the level of L5 usually
Eighty five percent of gall bladder stones seen on CT Scan
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone

Eighty five percent of gall bladder stones seen on CT Scan

The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
allQuestions.explanation: Approximately 85% of urinary/renal stones are radio-opaque and visible on plain radiograph (X-ray); phleboliths are small venous (not arterial) calcifications, and adrenal glands lie much higher than L5.

allQuestions.text: Regarding Free air in the abdomen, which of following is TRUE?
options: History of abdominal surgery within one month is an indication of pneumoperitoneum
The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
originalOptions: History of abdominal surgery within one month is an indication of pneumoperitoneum
The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
allQuestions.explanation: An erect chest film is the most sensitive plain radiograph for detecting free subdiaphragmatic gas; the falciform ligament sign actually supports (not lowers) the diagnosis, and portal venous gas is peripheral, not central.

allQuestions.text: Regarding bowel obstruction, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Sigmoid volvulus usually extends to the left upper quadrant
Two air fluid levels of 3 cm width each apply the definition of obstruction
originalOptions: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Sigmoid volvulus usually extends to the left upper quadrant
Two air fluid levels of 3 cm width each apply the definition of obstruction
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
allQuestions.explanation: The "3-6-9 rule" sets the large bowel dilatation threshold at 6 cm, so 8 cm exceeds this; the cecal threshold is actually 9 cm, and adhesions (not hernia) are the overall most common cause of small bowel obstruction.

allQuestions.text: Regarding bowel obstruction, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Cecal volvulus usually extends to the right upper quadrant
Descending colon diameter of 5 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
More than three air-fluid levels, each >2.5 cm in width, support bowel obstruction
originalOptions: Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Cecal volvulus usually extends to the right upper quadrant
Descending colon diameter of 5 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
More than three air-fluid levels, each >2.5 cm in width, support bowel obstruction
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) More than three air-fluid levels, each >2.5 cm in width, support bowel obstruction
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: More than three air-fluid levels, each >2.5 cm in width, support bowel obstruction
allQuestions.explanation: Multiple (more than three) air-fluid levels exceeding 2.5 cm in width is a standard supportive criterion for bowel obstruction; the cecal dilatation threshold is 9 cm, and cecal volvulus extends toward the epigastrium/left upper quadrant, not the right.

allQuestions.text: Regarding free air in the abdomen, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
History of abdominal surgery within one week is a cause of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Supine chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
originalOptions: The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
History of abdominal surgery within one week is a cause of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Supine chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) History of abdominal surgery within one week is a cause of pneumoperitoneum
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: History of abdominal surgery within one week is a cause of pneumoperitoneum
allQuestions.explanation: Residual post-operative free air can persist for several days after abdominal surgery, so recent surgery is a recognized cause of pneumoperitoneum. The falciform ligament sign supports pneumoperitoneum, portal venous gas is peripheral, and it is the erect (not supine) chest film that is the most sensitive.

allQuestions.text: Regarding abdominal calcifications, which one of the following is TRUE?
options: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen lucent on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
Ninety five percent of gall bladder stones seen on Ultrasound imaging
Pelvic calcification seen medial to the sacroiliac joint usually represents appendicolith
originalOptions: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen lucent on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
Ninety five percent of gall bladder stones seen on Ultrasound imaging
Pelvic calcification seen medial to the sacroiliac joint usually represents appendicolith
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) Ninety five percent of gall bladder stones seen on Ultrasound imaging
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Ninety five percent of gall bladder stones seen on Ultrasound imaging
allQuestions.explanation: Ultrasound detects the vast majority (~95%) of gallstones regardless of their radiographic composition; phleboliths are venous (not arterial), and most renal stones are radiopaque (not lucent) on plain film.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of sigmoid volvulus, as opposed to cecal volvulus?
options: Dilated loop arising in the right lower quadrant
Dilated loop arising in the pelvis and extending toward the right upper quadrant
Distal colon is collapsed with distended small bowel
originalOptions: Dilated loop arising in the right lower quadrant
Dilated loop arising in the pelvis and extending toward the right upper quadrant
Distal colon is collapsed with distended small bowel
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) Dilated loop arising in the pelvis and extending toward the right upper quadrant
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Dilated loop arising in the pelvis and extending toward the right upper quadrant
allQuestions.explanation: Sigmoid volvulus arises in the pelvis (left lower quadrant) and points toward the RUQ, is ahaustral, and shows few air-fluid levels. Cecal volvulus arises in the RLQ and extends toward the epigastrium or LUQ, with haustra maintained, a collapsed distal colon, and a single air-fluid level.

allQuestions.text: The "3-6-9 rule" refers to the approximate maximum normal diameter (in cm) of which structures, respectively?
options: Small bowel (3 cm), large bowel (6 cm), cecum (9 cm)
Small bowel (6 cm), large bowel (9 cm), cecum (3 cm)
Small bowel (3 cm), cecum (6 cm), large bowel (9 cm)
Small bowel (9 cm), large bowel (6 cm), cecum (3 cm)
originalOptions: Small bowel (3 cm), large bowel (6 cm), cecum (9 cm)
Small bowel (6 cm), large bowel (9 cm), cecum (3 cm)
Small bowel (3 cm), cecum (6 cm), large bowel (9 cm)
Small bowel (9 cm), large bowel (6 cm), cecum (3 cm)
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Small bowel (3 cm), large bowel (6 cm), cecum (9 cm)
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Small bowel (3 cm), large bowel (6 cm), cecum (9 cm)
allQuestions.explanation: The 3-6-9 rule gives the approximate upper limits of normal caliber for the small bowel (3 cm), large bowel (6 cm), and cecum (9 cm) — exceeding these thresholds raises concern for bowel dilatation/obstruction.

allQuestions.text: Which imaging modality is considered the gold standard for detecting gallbladder stones?
allQuestions.explanation: Ultrasound is highly sensitive for gallstones, appearing as echogenic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing, and is far more sensitive than plain radiograph (which only shows ~15–20% of stones) or CT (which can miss cholesterol stones).

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic finding of small bowel obstruction, as opposed to large bowel obstruction?
options: Centrally located dilated loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full width of the lumen
Haustral folds crossing only part of the lumen
Fecal loading within the dilated bowel segment
originalOptions: Centrally located dilated loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full width of the lumen
Haustral folds crossing only part of the lumen
Fecal loading within the dilated bowel segment
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Centrally located dilated loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full width of the lumen
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Centrally located dilated loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full width of the lumen
allQuestions.explanation: Small bowel lies centrally and shows valvulae conniventes that span the entire lumen diameter, distinguishing it from large bowel, which lies peripherally and shows haustral folds crossing only part of the lumen.

allQuestions.text: Simultaneous visualization of gas within the bowel lumen and gas outlining the outer bowel wall (the double-wall/Rigler sign) is a sign of which of the following?
allQuestions.explanation: Gas outlining both the inner (intraluminal) and outer (extraluminal/peritoneal) surfaces of the bowel wall is the Rigler (double-wall) sign, indicating free intraperitoneal air from a perforated viscus.

allQuestions.text: What is the best imaging modality for evaluating suspected appendicitis in an adult?
allQuestions.explanation: CT with IV contrast has the highest sensitivity (94–98%) and specificity (up to 97%) for appendicitis in adults and also identifies alternative causes of abdominal pain; ultrasound is preferred first-line in children and pregnant patients but is more operator-dependent and less sensitive overall.

allQuestions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaascites.jpg ]
allQuestions.explanation: The axial CT scan of the abdomen shows low density ascitic fluid surrounding the liver, spleen and stomach.

allQuestions.text: Regarding abdomen anatomy, which of the following is wrong?
options: The second part of the duodenum passes between the liver and pancreas
The inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
The superior mesenteric artery is at the level of T11, above the celiac axis
The renal arteries arise at approximately L1–L2
originalOptions: The second part of the duodenum passes between the liver and pancreas
The inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
The superior mesenteric artery is at the level of T11, above the celiac axis
The renal arteries arise at approximately L1–L2
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The superior mesenteric artery is at the level of T11, above the celiac axis
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The superior mesenteric artery is at the level of T11, above the celiac axis
allQuestions.explanation: The celiac trunk (T12) actually arises above the SMA (L1), so stating the SMA is at T11 "above" the celiac axis reverses the correct order; the IMA at L3 and renal arteries at L1–L2 are both correct as stated.

allQuestions.text: Regarding abdomen anatomy, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of the pancreas
The right adrenal gland lies more superiorly than the left adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The third part of the duodenum passes between liver and pancreas
The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
originalOptions: The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of the pancreas
The right adrenal gland lies more superiorly than the left adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The third part of the duodenum passes between liver and pancreas
The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
allQuestions.explanation: The IMA arises from the anterior aorta at the level of L3. The portal vein forms posterior (not anterior) to the pancreatic neck, the left (not right) adrenal gland sits more superiorly, and the left (not right) renal vein is the longer vessel.

allQuestions.text: Regarding abdomen anatomy, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L2
The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile and pancreatic ducts
The right adrenal gland lies more superiorly than the left adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of pancreas
originalOptions: The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L2
The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile and pancreatic ducts
The right adrenal gland lies more superiorly than the left adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of pancreas
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile and pancreatic ducts
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile and pancreatic ducts
allQuestions.explanation: The major duodenal papilla, where the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct join and empty, is located in the second (descending) part of the duodenum. The IMA arises at L3, the left adrenal gland actually sits at a more superior level than the right adrenal gland (T11-L1 vs T12-L1), the left renal vein is longer than right, and the portal vein forms posterior to the pancreatic neck.

allQuestions.text: Regarding abdomen anatomy, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L2
The left renal vein passes posterior to the aorta to reach the inferior vena cava
The left adrenal gland is higher than the right adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of the pancreas
originalOptions: The inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L2
The left renal vein passes posterior to the aorta to reach the inferior vena cava
The left adrenal gland is higher than the right adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of the pancreas
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The left adrenal gland is higher than the right adrenal gland
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The left adrenal gland is higher than the right adrenal gland
allQuestions.explanation: The left adrenal gland sits at a slightly higher (more cephalad) level than the right adrenal gland (T11-L1 vs T12-L1). The IMA arises at L3, the left renal vein is the longer vein and crosses anterior to the aorta, and the portal vein forms posterior to the pancreatic neck.

allQuestions.text: Probably benign breast lesion that requires short-interval follow-up is which BI-RADS category?
allQuestions.explanation: BI-RADS 3 means probably benign (<2% risk of malignancy), and short-interval follow-up is suggested. BI-RADS 2 is definitely benign (0%) and needs no short-interval follow-up. BI-RADS 4A is already suspicious (2–9%) and biopsy is considered.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is a feature of a benign axillary lymph node on mammography?
options: Large, rounded shape without a hilum
originalOptions: Large, rounded shape without a hilum
allQuestions.explanation: A normal or benign node is small and bean-shaped with a fatty hilum, which appears as central lucency. Loss of the hilum, rounding, increased density, and irregular margins all suggest malignancy.

allQuestions.text: What is the best first imaging modality for a pregnant patient with a palpable breast lump?
allQuestions.explanation: Ultrasound uses no ionizing radiation and is the modality of choice for symptomatic pregnant or young (<30 years) patients. It also distinguishes cystic from solid lesions and can guide biopsy. Mammography and CT use radiation, and MRI needs gadolinium, so none of them is first-line.

allQuestions.text: Which mammographic calcification morphology carries the highest suspicion of malignancy?
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) Fine linear / fine linear branching
allQuestions.explanation: Thin, irregular, branching calcifications (<0.5 mm) suggest deposition within a duct and carry the highest suspicion. Fine pleomorphic and amorphous are also suspicious but less so. Popcorn-like (involuting fibroadenoma) and rim calcifications are typically benign.
allQuestions.batchName: Iris Mini-OSCE (Group A) / Iris Mini-OSCE (Group D)

allQuestions.text: Which of the following features suggests a malignant breast mass on imaging?
options: Oval shape with posterior acoustic enhancement
Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
Coarse popcorn-like calcification within the mass
originalOptions: Oval shape with posterior acoustic enhancement
Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
Coarse popcorn-like calcification within the mass
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Irregular shape with spiculated, indistinct, or obscured margins
allQuestions.explanation: Irregular shape and spiculated or indistinct margins are the most suspicious mass features for malignancy. Round or oval circumscribed masses are usually benign (cyst or fibroadenoma). Fat density suggests a lipoma or hamartoma, and popcorn calcification suggests an involuting fibroadenoma.
allQuestions.batchName: Coronary Mini-OSCE (Group C) / Iris Mini-OSCE (Group A) / Iris Mini-OSCE (Group D) / Iris Final / Endorphin Final / Aorta Final

allQuestions.text: A palpable mass is located at the 5 o'clock position in the right breast. Which quadrant is this?
allQuestions.explanation: In the right breast, 9 o'clock is lateral, so 3–6 o'clock is the lower inner quadrant and 6–9 is the lower outer. The 5 o'clock position therefore lies in the lower inner quadrant.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following statements about mammography is FALSE?
options: Axillary lymph nodes with central lucency may be benign
Sensitivity of mammography is reduced in dense breasts
Dense breast tissue in young women requires further evaluation
Spiculated masses are suspicious for malignancy
originalOptions: Axillary lymph nodes with central lucency may be benign
Sensitivity of mammography is reduced in dense breasts
Dense breast tissue in young women requires further evaluation
Spiculated masses are suspicious for malignancy
allQuestions.explanation: Fine pleomorphic calcifications are a suspicious morphology. The typically benign types are skin, vascular, popcorn, rod-like, round or punctate, rim, and milk of calcium.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding BI-RADS?
options: BI-RADS 0 indicates an incomplete assessment that needs additional imaging
BI-RADS 6 indicates the presence of a benign lesion
BI-RADS 3 carries a <2% probability of malignancy
BI-RADS 4 is suspicious, and biopsy should be considered
originalOptions: BI-RADS 0 indicates an incomplete assessment that needs additional imaging
BI-RADS 6 indicates the presence of a benign lesion
BI-RADS 3 carries a <2% probability of malignancy
BI-RADS 4 is suspicious, and biopsy should be considered
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) BI-RADS 6 indicates the presence of a benign lesion
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: BI-RADS 6 indicates the presence of a benign lesion
allQuestions.explanation: BI-RADS 6 is a known, biopsy-proven malignancy, not a benign lesion. The other statements are correct.
allQuestions.batchName: Coronary Mini-OSCE (Group C) / Iris Mini-OSCE (Group C) / Iris Mini-OSCE (Group D)

allQuestions.text: Which of the following statements about the BI-RADS classification is FALSE?
options: BI-RADS 3 indicates a probably benign finding
originalOptions: BI-RADS 3 indicates a probably benign finding
allQuestions.explanation: BI-RADS 5 is highly suggestive of malignancy (>95%), so it is not benign. BI-RADS 2 is benign and BI-RADS 3 is probably benign.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding mammography?
options: A spiculated mass is suspicious for malignancy
Simple cysts appear non-echoic on ultrasound
Coarse heterogeneous calcifications are 0.5–1 mm and are suspicious
A left breast lower inner lesion lies at 6–9 o'clock
A fibroadenoma is BI-RADS 2 and needs follow-up
originalOptions: A spiculated mass is suspicious for malignancy
Simple cysts appear non-echoic on ultrasound

A left breast lower inner lesion lies at 6–9 o'clock
A fibroadenoma is BI-RADS 2 and needs follow-up
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) A fibroadenoma is BI-RADS 2 and needs follow-up
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: A fibroadenoma is BI-RADS 2 and needs follow-up
allQuestions.explanation: BI-RADS 2 is a benign finding with routine screening only. Short-interval follow-up belongs to BI-RADS 3 (probably benign).

allQuestions.text: Regarding BI-RADS breast classification, which of the following is FALSE?
options: BI-RADS 3 represents a probably benign finding and needs follow-up
BI-RADS 0 represents an incomplete study and needs additional imaging
BI-RADS 1 represents a negative study with no evidence of abnormalities
originalOptions: BI-RADS 3 represents a probably benign finding and needs follow-up

allQuestions.explanation: BI-RADS 2 is a benign finding. Biopsy-proven malignancy is BI-RADS 6.

allQuestions.text: Which clock-face statement for a right-breast mass is FALSE?
options: The right lower-inner quadrant corresponds to 3–6 o'clock
The right lower-outer quadrant corresponds to 6–9 o'clock
The right upper-inner quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
The right upper-outer quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
A right-breast lesion at 5 o'clock lies in the lower-inner quadrant

The right upper-inner quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock

A right-breast lesion at 5 o'clock lies in the lower-inner quadrant
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The right upper-inner quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The right upper-inner quadrant corresponds to 9–12 o'clock
allQuestions.explanation: In the right breast, 9 o'clock is lateral, so 9–12 o'clock is the upper-outer quadrant. The upper-inner quadrant is 12–3 o'clock.

allQuestions.text: What are the standard views of screening mammography?
allQuestions.explanation: The standard views are bilateral CC and MLO. True lateral, spot, magnification, and axillary views are supplementary.

allQuestions.text: A palpable mass is located at the 8 o'clock position in the right breast. Which quadrant is this?
allQuestions.explanation: In the right breast, 6–9 o'clock is the lower-outer quadrant. The lower-inner quadrant is 3–6 o'clock.

allQuestions.text: Why is detection of an abnormality on mammography more difficult in dense breasts, as in young women?
options: Most abnormalities are radiolucent and are masked by fibroglandular tissue
Fibroglandular tissue attenuates fewer X-rays than fat
Fatty tissue appears white and hides small lesions
Calcifications become radiolucent within dense tissue
Most abnormalities are opaque, so a white lesion is lost on a white (dense) background
originalOptions: Most abnormalities are radiolucent and are masked by fibroglandular tissue
Fibroglandular tissue attenuates fewer X-rays than fat
Fatty tissue appears white and hides small lesions
Calcifications become radiolucent within dense tissue
Most abnormalities are opaque, so a white lesion is lost on a white (dense) background
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) Most abnormalities are opaque, so a white lesion is lost on a white (dense) background
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Most abnormalities are opaque, so a white lesion is lost on a white (dense) background
allQuestions.explanation: Most abnormalities are radio-opaque, and dense tissue appears white. In fatty breasts (older patients) the background is black, so the same lesion is easy to see.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following mammographic calcifications is suspicious for malignancy?
options: Skin calcification with a lucent center
originalOptions: Skin calcification with a lucent center
allQuestions.explanation: Fine pleomorphic calcifications (<0.5 mm with discrete, varied shapes) are a suspicious morphology. The other options are typically benign.

allQuestions.text: Which axillary lymph node feature on mammography suggests malignancy?
options: Large, rounded, hyperdense node without a fatty hilum
Small oval node with a fatty hilum
Thin cortex with a preserved fatty hilum
Small, stable intramammary node with a fatty hilum
originalOptions: Large, rounded, hyperdense node without a fatty hilum
Small oval node with a fatty hilum
Thin cortex with a preserved fatty hilum
Small, stable intramammary node with a fatty hilum
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Large, rounded, hyperdense node without a fatty hilum
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Large, rounded, hyperdense node without a fatty hilum
allQuestions.explanation: Loss of the fatty hilum (no central lucency), rounding, and increased density suggest malignancy. A preserved fatty hilum with a bean shape is benign.

allQuestions.text: BI-RADS 5 is best described as:
allQuestions.explanation: BI-RADS 5 means >95% probability of malignancy and appropriate action is required. BI-RADS 4 is the 2–94% suspicious group, and BI-RADS 6 is already biopsy-proven.

allQuestions.text: What is the main value of obtaining both CC and MLO views in mammography?
options: Giving a three-dimensional localization of a lesion
originalOptions: Giving a three-dimensional localization of a lesion
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Giving a three-dimensional localization of a lesion
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Giving a three-dimensional localization of a lesion
allQuestions.explanation: The CC view shows whether a lesion is inner or outer, and the MLO view shows whether it is upper or lower. Together they localize it in three dimensions. Differentiating solid from cystic is the role of ultrasound.

allQuestions.text: Which chest radiograph projection makes the heart appear normal in size?

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is characteristic of post-primary (reactivation) tuberculosis?
options: Ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy as the sole finding
Large pleural effusion as the dominant feature
Uniform 1–3 mm nodules throughout both lungs

Large pleural effusion as the dominant feature
Uniform 1–3 mm nodules throughout both lungs
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Cavitation in the upper lobes
allQuestions.explanation: Post-primary TB favors the upper zones and is far more likely to cavitate than primary TB. Isolated hilar nodes and effusion are features of primary disease, and diffuse tiny uniform nodules are miliary TB.

allQuestions.explanation: The thin white visceral pleural line with an avascular lucent space beyond it is the key sign. Mediastinal shift occurs only in tension pneumothorax, and the mediastinum shifts away, not toward the affected side.

allQuestions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyctensionpneumothorax.png ]
allQuestions.explanation: Mobile chest x-ray shows a large right tension pneumothorax with a hyper-expanded hemithorax, splayed ribs, flattened diaphragm, and leftward mediastinal shift. Both lungs show consolidation, preventing further collapse of the right lung. This diagnosis is confirmed because a simple pneumothorax causes no mediastinal shift, while a pleural effusion would appear opaque rather than hyperlucent. Additionally, isolated lung collapse pulls the mediastinum toward the affected side instead of pushing it away, and a diaphragmatic hernia would typically display herniated abdominal contents rather than an empty air space.

allQuestions.text: Regarding pneumothorax, which of the following is TRUE?

Cavitary neoplasms are the usual cause of primary pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
Primary spontaneous pneumothorax typically occurs in short elderly women

allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
allQuestions.explanation: Air collects anteriorly and superiorly, so the tube is placed there. Laceration causes an ipsilateral pneumothorax, tension pushes the mediastinum away, and primary spontaneous pneumothorax affects tall young patients.

allQuestions.text: Regarding pneumothorax, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The chest tube should be inserted posterosuperiorly at the affected side

allQuestions.explanation: Tension pneumothorax gives a hyperlucent hemithorax with a collapsed lung. The mediastinum shifts away from it, and the tube is placed anterosuperiorly, not posteriorly or inferiorly.

allQuestions.text: Regarding normal appearances on chest imaging, which of the following is TRUE?

allQuestions.text: Which of the following statements about stage II sarcoidosis is WRONG?

Nodal enlargement with pleural effusion is the defining feature
Reticulonodular opacities may involve the upper zones

Nodal enlargement with pleural effusion is the defining feature

allQuestions.explanation: Stage II is defined by nodal enlargement plus parenchymal disease. Pleural effusion is not a staging criterion.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding cavitation in post-primary tuberculosis?

It develops mainly in the posterior segments of the upper lobes
The superior segment of the lower lobe can also be involved

allQuestions.text: Why does the heart appear magnified on an AP chest radiograph?
options: The scapulae overlie the cardiac shadow
The patient is usually rotated during the examination
The heart is farther from the detector
The beam traverses the patient from posterior to anterior
The lungs are hyperinflated on AP films
originalOptions: The scapulae overlie the cardiac shadow
The patient is usually rotated during the examination
The heart is farther from the detector
The beam traverses the patient from posterior to anterior
The lungs are hyperinflated on AP films
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The heart is farther from the detector
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The heart is farther from the detector
allQuestions.explanation: Magnification is geometric, because in the AP view the heart lies farther from the detector than in the PA view. Rotation and overlying scapulae are drawbacks of AP films but are not the cause of magnification, and a posterior-to-anterior beam describes the PA view.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following typically causes mediastinal shift AWAY from the affected side?
options: Complete obstruction of the main bronchus
originalOptions: Complete obstruction of the main bronchus
allQuestions.explanation: A large effusion exerts mass effect and pushes the mediastinum away from the affected side. Collapse (including complete main bronchus obstruction) pulls the mediastinum toward the affected side, consolidation preserves volume without shift, and a simple pneumothorax causes no shift unless it becomes tension.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic sign of pleural effusion on an erect frontal chest radiograph?
allQuestions.explanation: Fluid climbs the lateral chest wall, forming a concave-upward meniscus that slopes gently medially, together with blunting of the costophrenic angle. Air bronchogram indicates consolidation, signet ring indicates bronchiectasis, and cephalization and Kerley B lines are features of heart failure.

allQuestions.text: Regarding the thin white line seen on an erect chest radiograph in pneumothorax, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Lung markings extend peripheral to the line
The peripheral space is radiolucent compared with the adjacent lung
The line represents the parietal pleura
The mediastinum always shifts away from the affected side
The peripheral space appears denser than the adjacent lung
originalOptions: Lung markings extend peripheral to the line
The peripheral space is radiolucent compared with the adjacent lung
The line represents the parietal pleura
The mediastinum always shifts away from the affected side
The peripheral space appears denser than the adjacent lung
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) The peripheral space is radiolucent compared with the adjacent lung
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The peripheral space is radiolucent compared with the adjacent lung
allQuestions.explanation: The line is the visceral pleural edge, and the air-filled pleural space beyond it is lucent and avascular. Shift away from the pneumothorax occurs only in tension pneumothorax.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is TRUE regarding heart failure on chest radiography?
options: Pleural effusions are not a feature
Cephalization of the pulmonary vessels is seen
Kerley B lines are long lines at the lung apices
The cardiothoracic ratio is typically below 50%
originalOptions: Pleural effusions are not a feature
Cephalization of the pulmonary vessels is seen
Kerley B lines are long lines at the lung apices
The cardiothoracic ratio is typically below 50%
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) Cephalization of the pulmonary vessels is seen
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Cephalization of the pulmonary vessels is seen
allQuestions.explanation: Pulmonary venous congestion dilates the upper lobe veins (cephalization). Heart failure causes cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio >50%) and effusions, and Kerley B lines are 1–2 cm peripheral lines at the lung bases, not the apices.

allQuestions.text: A chest radiograph shows a thin visceral pleural line with absent lung markings peripheral to it and no mediastinal shift. What is the most likely diagnosis?
allQuestions.explanation: A visible visceral pleural edge with an avascular lucent space beyond it is diagnostic of pneumothorax, and the absence of mediastinal shift makes it non-tension. Tension pneumothorax shifts the mediastinum away, and effusion, collapse and consolidation all produce opacity.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding pleural effusion?
options: Blunting of the costophrenic angle is seen
A meniscus is seen on erect frontal films
A lateral decubitus view with the affected side down is the most sensitive projection
It appears lucent (radiolucent) on chest radiograph

allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) It appears lucent (radiolucent) on chest radiograph
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: It appears lucent (radiolucent) on chest radiograph
allQuestions.explanation: Fluid is soft-tissue density, so an effusion appears as an opacity (white). Pneumothorax is the pleural pathology that appears lucent.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is usually hyperdense on non-contrast CT?
allQuestions.explanation: Bone, acute blood, calcification, metal, and the lens are hyperdense on non-contrast CT. Fat, CSF, chronic blood, and air are hypodense.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is the most radiolucent on a plain radiograph?
allQuestions.explanation: Gas attenuates the X-ray beam least, so it appears black. Fat is dark grey, and bone is white.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding Wilms tumor?
options: It is the most common primary renal malignancy of childhood
It typically presents as a large solid intrarenal mass
It may extend into the renal vein and inferior vena cava
Calcification is seen in only a minority of cases

It typically presents as a large solid intrarenal mass
It may extend into the renal vein and inferior vena cava
Calcification is seen in only a minority of cases

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding Wilms tumor?

allQuestions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is hyperdense on CT scan?
allQuestions.explanation: Iodinated contrast is markedly hyperdense on CT. Fluid, fat, chronic blood, and air are iso- to hypodense.

allQuestions.text: Regarding MRI, which of the following is FALSE?

The quality of MRI images is lower in the chest region than in the brain region
allQuestions.explanation: MRI uses a strong magnet and radiofrequency waves, with no ionizing radiation. Radiographs and CT are the modalities that use it.

allQuestions.text: Reducing the kV from 90 to 70 in a radiograph, with image density maintained, will generally:
options: Decrease the contrast between air and soft tissue
originalOptions: Decrease the contrast between air and soft tissue
allQuestions.explanation: Lowering kV reduces beam penetration, so mAs must be increased to keep the same image density, and patient dose rises. Contrast between tissues improves rather than falls at lower kV.
allQuestions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

allQuestions.text: Regarding radiographs, which of the following is TRUE?

allQuestions.explanation: Metal is intense white on radiographs, denser than bone. Hydrogen content determines MRI signal, not radiographic density. A satisfactory NG tube follows the midline with its tip below the left hemidiaphragm. Radiography is cheap, and ovarian torsion is assessed first by ultrasound.

allQuestions.text: Regarding diagnostic radiology, which of the following is TRUE?

allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Ultrasound is relatively safer than CT scan
allQuestions.explanation: Ultrasound uses no ionizing radiation, while CT delivers a high dose. PACS is for archiving and communication of images, and iodinated contrast carries a risk of renal injury.

allQuestions.text: Regarding Hounsfield's scale, which one of the following is TRUE?

allQuestions.explanation: Splenic parenchyma is soft tissue density, roughly 50–65 HU. Gas is near -1000 HU, mesentery is fat (negative HU, -60 to -120), and compact bone approaches +1000 HU.

allQuestions.text: Regarding the ALARA principle, which of the following is FALSE?

allQuestions.text: Regarding MRI, which of the following is TRUE?

allQuestions.text: All of the following statements are FALSE EXCEPT:

allQuestions.explanation: Vasogenic edema surrounds tumors and abscesses (lymphoma, abscess, GBM) due to blood-brain barrier disruption; ischemic stroke instead produces cytotoxic edema from cellular swelling.

allQuestions.text: Which statement regarding cerebral venous sinus thrombosis is CORRECT?
options: The cavernous sinus is the most common site
Both cytotoxic and vasogenic edema can be seen
Sinus thrombosis does not cause hemorrhage
The vein of Labbé drains into the superior sagittal sinus
originalOptions: The cavernous sinus is the most common site
Both cytotoxic and vasogenic edema can be seen
Sinus thrombosis does not cause hemorrhage
The vein of Labbé drains into the superior sagittal sinus
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Both cytotoxic and vasogenic edema can be seen
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Both cytotoxic and vasogenic edema can be seen
allQuestions.explanation: Raised venous pressure first causes vasogenic edema, progressing to cytotoxic edema if venous infarction occurs. The superior sagittal sinus (not cavernous) is the most common site, hemorrhage is common, and the vein of Labbé drains into the transverse sinus.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following does NOT show restricted diffusion on MRI (DWI)?
allQuestions.explanation: Lymphoma, abscess, epidermoid cyst, and acute ischemia characteristically restrict diffusion; acute hemorrhage's DWI signal is variable and not a classic cause of true restricted diffusion.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is NOT a cause of restriction on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)?
allQuestions.explanation: Arachnoid cysts contain simple CSF-like fluid and do not restrict diffusion, unlike abscesses, acute ischemia, high-grade tumors, and post-ictal states.

allQuestions.text: A brain MRI lesion is isointense on T1 and hyperintense on T2. What stage of hemorrhage is most likely?
allQuestions.explanation: Intracellular oxyhemoglobin in the hyperacute stage is T1 isointense and T2 hyperintense; acute (deoxyhemoglobin) blood is instead T2 hypointense.

allQuestions.text: Which basal-ganglia blood-supply statement is INCORRECT?
options: The anterior limb of the internal capsule is supplied by the choroidal artery
The caudate is supplied by the medial lenticulostriate artery
The putamen and globus pallidus are supplied by the lateral lenticulostriate artery
The thalamus is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery

The putamen and globus pallidus are supplied by the lateral lenticulostriate artery

allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The anterior limb of the internal capsule is supplied by the choroidal artery
allQuestions.explanation: The anterior limb of the internal capsule is supplied by the medial lenticulostriate arteries and the recurrent artery of Heubner; the anterior choroidal artery instead supplies the posterior limb/retrolentiform region.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following statements regarding this lesion is TRUE? [img: Radiologynepiduralhematomatrue.png ]

allQuestions.text: Which is WRONG about this lesion? [img: Radiologynepiduralhematomawrong.png ]
options: The common cause of bleeding is the middle meningeal artery
Supratentorial location is more common than infratentorial
originalOptions: The common cause of bleeding is the middle meningeal artery
Supratentorial location is more common than infratentorial

MRI is the primary imaging modality for MS

MRI is the primary imaging modality for MS

allQuestions.text: Which of the following statements about multiple sclerosis (MS) is TRUE?
options: MS is limited to the peripheral nervous system

Lesions are mostly infratentorial in children

allQuestions.text: The cerebellum's blood supply mainly originates from which of the following?
allQuestions.explanation: The SCA and AICA (branches of the basilar artery) supply most of the cerebellum; only PICA arises from the distal vertebral artery.

allQuestions.text: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – select the correct statement.
options: Non-contrast MRI shows a hypointense filling defect
Non-contrast CT shows a hyperdense ("dense") sinus
Contrast-enhanced MRI shows the "empty delta" sign
Contrast-enhanced CT shows the "empty delta" sign
originalOptions: Non-contrast MRI shows a hypointense filling defect
Non-contrast CT shows a hyperdense ("dense") sinus

Contrast-enhanced CT shows the "empty delta" sign
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) Contrast-enhanced CT shows the "empty delta" sign
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Contrast-enhanced CT shows the "empty delta" sign
allQuestions.explanation: The empty delta sign is a triangular filling defect surrounded by enhancing dura, classically seen on contrast-enhanced CT venography; non-contrast CT instead shows a hyperdense (not empty) thrombosed sinus.

allQuestions.text: Homogeneous enhancement and hyperdensity on non-contrast CT is most typical of which lesion?
allQuestions.explanation: Primary CNS lymphoma is classically hyperdense on non-contrast CT (high cellularity) with homogeneous enhancement, unlike metastases or abscesses, which typically show ring enhancement with central necrosis.

allQuestions.text: Which MRI sequence is most sensitive for detecting blood breakdown products (hemosiderin/deoxyhemoglobin)?
allQuestions.explanation: Gradient echo/susceptibility-weighted sequences are exquisitely sensitive to blood products due to a blooming artifact, unlike T1, T2, or FLAIR.

allQuestions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynintraventricularhemorrhage.png ]
allQuestions.explanation: An acute intracerebral haemorrhage is centred in the basal ganglia of the right hemisphere with the extension of blood into both lateral ventricles (intraventricular haemorrhage), third & fourth ventricles as well as the foramina of Luschka and Magendie. There is no hydrocephalus at this stage.

allQuestions.text: Identify the neuroanatomical structures labeled 1, 2, and 4 on this axial brain CT, respectively. [img: Radiologynanatomy1brain.png ]

allQuestions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmcainfarct.png ]
allQuestions.explanation: DWI hyperintensity with ADC hypointensity (true restricted diffusion) confirms acute ischemic infarction, unlike chronic infarct (facilitated diffusion) or vasogenic edema (no restriction). Here, ADC (Apparent Diffusion Coefficient) map acts as a mirror image to confirm true tissue ischemia by turning dark.

allQuestions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynposteriorischemia.png ]
allQuestions.explanation: Hypodensity in the posterior/occipital vascular distribution reflects posterior circulation (PCA/vertebrobasilar) ischemia rather than an anterior circulation or hemorrhagic process.

allQuestions.text: Regarding posterior cranial fossa tumors in children, which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Ependymomas typically arise from the fourth ventricle
Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant posterior fossa tumor in children
The cystic component of a posterior fossa tumor is never enhanced
Pilocytic astrocytoma often has a cyst with an enhancing mural nodule
originalOptions: Ependymomas typically arise from the fourth ventricle
Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant posterior fossa tumor in children
The cystic component of a posterior fossa tumor is never enhanced
Pilocytic astrocytoma often has a cyst with an enhancing mural nodule
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The cystic component of a posterior fossa tumor is never enhanced
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The cystic component of a posterior fossa tumor is never enhanced
allQuestions.explanation: In pediatric posterior fossa tumors such as pilocytic astrocytoma, the cyst wall or an associated mural nodule commonly DOES enhance, making the "never enhanced" statement false.

allQuestions.text: Regarding posterior cranial fossa tumors in children, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Ependymomas typically show no cystic components
Cystic components in posterior fossa tumors usually enhance with contrast
Ependymomas are located outside the ventricular system
originalOptions: Ependymomas typically show no cystic components
Cystic components in posterior fossa tumors usually enhance with contrast
Ependymomas are located outside the ventricular system
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Ependymomas arise from the ventricles
allQuestions.explanation: Ependymomas classically arise from the ependymal lining of the ventricular system (most often the fourth ventricle), unlike the false statement that they are extraventricular.

allQuestions.text: A patient presents with seizures. Which of the following brain tumors is most commonly associated with seizures?
allQuestions.explanation: Oligodendrogliomas characteristically involve the cortex/subcortical white matter, making seizures a very common presenting symptom compared with the other listed tumors.

allQuestions.text: Which brain tumor is characteristically associated with a "butterfly" pattern on imaging?
allQuestions.explanation: GBM classically spreads across the corpus callosum, producing a bilateral, symmetric "butterfly glioma" appearance not typical of the other tumors.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is NOT a recognized cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH)?
allQuestions.explanation: Meningioma is not a recognized cause of SAH; trauma, ruptured aneurysm, and vasculitis are the classic causes.

allQuestions.text: Which of the statements about intracranial dural venous sinuses is FALSE?
options: Dural venous sinus thrombosis can involve cortical and deep cerebral veins
Contrast-enhanced axial MRI may show a filling defect in the affected sinus
The empty delta sign is seen on contrast-enhanced CT in venous sinus thrombosis
The empty delta sign appears on non-contrast CT scans
originalOptions: Dural venous sinus thrombosis can involve cortical and deep cerebral veins
Contrast-enhanced axial MRI may show a filling defect in the affected sinus
The empty delta sign is seen on contrast-enhanced CT in venous sinus thrombosis
The empty delta sign appears on non-contrast CT scans
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) The empty delta sign appears on non-contrast CT scans
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The empty delta sign appears on non-contrast CT scans
allQuestions.explanation: The empty delta sign requires contrast to visualize the enhancing dura around the non-enhancing clot; it is not seen on non-contrast CT, which instead shows a hyperdense sinus.

allQuestions.text: What is the most common site of hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage?
allQuestions.explanation: The putamen is the single most common site of hypertensive ICH, followed by thalamus, pons, and cerebellum.

allQuestions.text: All of the following can present in neurofibromatosis type 2, EXCEPT:
allQuestions.explanation: Multiple cutaneous/subcutaneous neurofibromas are a hallmark of NF1, not NF2; NF2 instead features bilateral vestibular schwannomas, meningiomas, and intramedullary ependymomas.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is a white matter structure?
allQuestions.explanation: The corona radiata is composed of white matter projection fibers; the others are all grey matter structures.

allQuestions.text: All of the following are true about schizencephaly, EXCEPT:
options: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
It can be unilateral or bilateral
Open-lip schizencephaly presents with more symptoms than closed-lip
There is pial communication in closed-lip schizencephaly
originalOptions: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
It can be unilateral or bilateral
Open-lip schizencephaly presents with more symptoms than closed-lip
There is pial communication in closed-lip schizencephaly
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
allQuestions.explanation: Schizencephaly clefts are actually lined by grey matter (heterotopic cortex), not white matter. Laterality, symptom severity, and the presence of pial-ependymal communication in both types are all accurate characteristics of the condition.
allQuestions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

allQuestions.text: All of the following are intramedullary lesions, EXCEPT:
allQuestions.explanation: Schwannoma is an intradural extramedullary tumor arising from a nerve root sheath, unlike astrocytoma, ependymoma, hemangioblastoma, and ganglioglioma, which are intramedullary.

allQuestions.text: All of the following appear hyperintense on T2 MRI, EXCEPT:
allQuestions.explanation: Air produces a signal void and appears hypointense on all MRI sequences, unlike fatty marrow, late subacute hematoma, choroid plexus papilloma, and GBM, which are typically T2 hyperintense.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is NOT found in hyperacute brain ischemia?
options: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
originalOptions: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
allQuestions.explanation: These are late/chronic infarct changes (>3 weeks); the hyperacute stage (0–6 hours) instead shows subtle grey-white loss, cortical hypodensity, gyral effacement, and loss of the insular ribbon sign.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the parietal bones with the occipital bone?
allQuestions.explanation: The lambdoid suture joins both parietal bones with the occipital bone posteriorly; coronal joins frontal to parietal, sagittal joins the two parietals, and metopic joins the two frontal bones.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the frontal and parietal bones?
allQuestions.explanation: The coronal suture joins the frontal and parietal bones, distinct from the squamosal suture which joins the temporal and parietal bones, the metopic suture which joins the two frontal bones, the sagittal suture which joins the two parietal bones, and the lambdoid suture which joins the occipital and parietal bones.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the two parietal bones?
allQuestions.explanation: The sagittal suture runs in the midline joining the two parietal bones to each other.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the two frontal bones?
allQuestions.explanation: The metopic suture is the embryological midline suture between the two frontal bones, which normally fuses in early childhood.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following radiologic features, if present, is supportive of the diagnosis of Sturge-Weber syndrome?
options: Restriction on DWI in both PCA territories
originalOptions: Restriction on DWI in both PCA territories
allQuestions.explanation: Sturge-Weber syndrome classically shows gyriform ("tram-track") cortical/subcortical calcification underlying the leptomeningeal angioma; the other features belong to different conditions (MS, tuberous sclerosis).
allQuestions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following statements about the Circle of Willis is FALSE?
options: The superior cerebellar artery (SCA) arises from the distal basilar artery
The Circle of Willis provides collateral circulation between anterior and posterior circulation
The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid artery to the posterior cerebral artery
The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
originalOptions: The superior cerebellar artery (SCA) arises from the distal basilar artery
The Circle of Willis provides collateral circulation between anterior and posterior circulation
The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid artery to the posterior cerebral artery
The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) arises from the distal vertebral artery
allQuestions.explanation: AICA is a branch of the proximal basilar artery; the distal vertebral artery instead gives rise to PICA. SCA does arise from the distal basilar artery, and the Circle of Willis does provide interhemispheric collateral flow.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is WRONG regarding cranial nerve involvement in multiple sclerosis?
options: The trigeminal nerve (CN5) can be affected
The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
The abducens nerve (CN6) can be affected
Optic nerve involvement (optic neuritis) is common
originalOptions: The trigeminal nerve (CN5) can be affected
The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
The abducens nerve (CN6) can be affected
Optic nerve involvement (optic neuritis) is common
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The oculomotor nerve is the most commonly affected cranial nerve
allQuestions.explanation: Optic neuritis (CN2) is the most common cranial nerve manifestation of MS, followed by CN5/6; oculomotor involvement is not the classic pattern.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following statements about MS lesion characteristics is TRUE?
options: Active plaques characteristically do not enhance with contrast
Diffuse cerebral atrophy is an early MS finding
T1-hypointense "black hole" lesions indicate a better prognosis
Enhancement never occurs in MS lesions
T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
originalOptions: Active plaques characteristically do not enhance with contrast
Diffuse cerebral atrophy is an early MS finding
T1-hypointense "black hole" lesions indicate a better prognosis
Enhancement never occurs in MS lesions
T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
allQuestions.correctAnswer: E) T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: T1-hypointense lesions ("black holes") correlate with axonal destruction and a worse prognosis
allQuestions.explanation: T1 hypointensity reflects irreversible axonal loss; active plaques classically DO enhance (reflecting blood-brain barrier breakdown), and diffuse atrophy is typically a late finding.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following statements about primary CNS lymphoma is FALSE?
options: It is typically hyperdense on non-contrast CT
It shows restricted diffusion on DWI
The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
It shows homogeneous enhancement in immunocompetent patients
originalOptions: It is typically hyperdense on non-contrast CT
It shows restricted diffusion on DWI
The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
It shows homogeneous enhancement in immunocompetent patients
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The ADC value is higher than normal brain parenchyma
allQuestions.explanation: Primary CNS lymphoma is highly cellular and restricts diffusion, so its ADC value is typically LOWER, not higher, than normal brain.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following anatomical relationships is CORRECT?
